appearance.assign.label: Appearance
appearance.assign.help: bodies?: [names]; faces?: [[x,y,z] on faces] (body?: which body, default the nearest); components?: [names or ids, or occurrence names]; appearance?: library name or stable starter.* ID (appearance.library) | color: "#rrggbb" or [r, g, b] (0–255), opacity? (0–1, default 1); name?: inert copied look label (requires color, mutually exclusive with appearance); pbr?: {metallic:0..1, roughness:0.045..1, dielectric_ior:1..3} (requires color/appearance and opacity 1); a starter ID or registered starter name resolves its recipe before color overrides; omitted pbr retains that response and pbr: null explicitly clears it. Unavailable glass recipes refuse through either selector. Other custom labels with an explicit color retain legacy scalar behavior. Neither appearance nor color (or color: null): clear, so the face follows its body, the body its component, the component its material
appearance.assign.description:
Give bodies, faces or components a look, or clear theirs: a library appearance or a starter
recipe by `appearance`, or a `color`. With neither (or `color: null`) the targets' own looks
are cleared, so a face follows its body, a body its component and a component its material.
One undo step; no dialogs.

fields.name: appearance
fields.description:
A library appearance's name or a starter recipe's name or stable `starter.*` id (see
`appearance.library`). With `color` too, that colour under this name. A recipe that
needs refraction (the glass ones) is refused.

fields.name: bodies
fields.description: Bodies, by name (a placed copy's name, `KB (K:2)`, means the body it shows).

fields.name: body
fields.description:
The body the `faces` points are on, for points that don't name one. Default: the
nearest body with a face there.

fields.name: color
fields.description:
The colour, `"#rrggbb"` or `[r, g, b]` (0–255); with `appearance`, it replaces the
recipe's colour. `null` (without `appearance`) clears the targets' looks.

fields.name: components
fields.description: Components, by name or id, or a placement's name (`K:2`).

fields.name: faces
fields.description: Faces, by a point on each, at most 10000.

fields.name: name
fields.description: A label for a copied look: needs `color`, not with `appearance`.

fields.name: opacity
fields.description:
0 (clear) to 1 (opaque). Default: 1, or the appearance's own. With `color` alone it
must be within 0–1; with `appearance` it is clamped there.

fields.name: pbr
fields.description:
The opaque PBR response (needs `color` or `appearance`, and opacity 1). Left out, a
recipe keeps its own; `null` clears it.

appearance.chain.label: Appearance Chain
appearance.chain.help: target: {body: name} | {body: name, face: zero-based model.faces index} | {component: name or id}; a placed copy's name (`KB (K:2)`, `K:2`) means the body or component it shows. Returns steps [{step: face|body|component|material, look: {name,color,opacity,pbr?} or null}] in precedence order and active (step or null). Component material is the common default look of its directly owned bodies, null if mixed/empty. Imported paint is a display fallback outside the four steps. Read-only; no dialogs

fields.description: target: {body: name} | {body: name, face: zero-based model.faces index} | {component: name or id}; a placed copy's name (`KB (K:2)`, `K:2`) means the body or component it shows. Returns steps [{step: face|body|component|material, look: {name,color,opacity,pbr?} or null}] in precedence order and active (step or null). Component material is the common default look of its directly owned bodies, null if mixed/empty. Imported paint is a display fallback outside the four steps. Read-only; no dialogs

appearance.copy.label: Copy Look
appearance.copy.help: target: appearance.chain target. Copies its resolved look to a transient session clipboard. No document change or dialogs.
appearance.copy.description:
`appearance.copy` takes one parameter, the `appearance.chain` target whose look goes into the
session's look clipboard. Unlike `appearance.pick_up`, which asks the UI to sample one, this call
has no form without a target.

fields.name: target
fields.description: A body, one of its faces, or a component: {body}, {body, face} or {component}.

appearance.favorite.label: Favorite Look
appearance.favorite.help: look: appearance.assign look; favorite: bool → validated look and preference request; UI library preference only, no document change or dialogs.

fields.description: look: appearance.assign look; favorite: bool → validated look and preference request; UI library preference only, no document change or dialogs.

appearance.library.label: Appearance Library
appearance.library.help: → 20 legacy scalar appearances, six opaque PBR finishes and 40 starter recipes with IDs, categories, provenance, requirements and availability; six starter glass recipes are unavailable

appearance.list.label: List Appearances
appearance.list.help: body?: name (or a placed copy's, `KB (K:2)`: the body it shows) → assigned appearances; with body, its resolved look and its faces' (face index, look)

fields.name: body
fields.description:
A body (or a placed copy's name, `KB (K:2)`, for the body it shows): the reply adds
`body`, its resolved look and its faces' looks.

appearance.paint.label: Paint Appearance
appearance.paint.help: appearance or color/name/opacity/pbr: appearance.assign look parameters; validates and returns look for ui.start paint. done?: true ends the UI tool. Programmatic calls never open UI.
appearance.paint.description:
`appearance.paint` takes a look exactly as `appearance.assign` does — the same five keys, read
by the same parser (`cmd::appearance_look`) — and `done: true` to end the UI's paint tool.

fields.name: appearance
fields.description:
A library appearance's name or a starter recipe's name or stable `starter.*` id (see
`appearance.library`). With `color` too, that colour under this name.

fields.name: color
fields.description:
The colour, `"#rrggbb"` or `[r, g, b]` (0–255); with `appearance`, it replaces the
recipe's colour.

fields.name: done
fields.description: `true` ends the UI's paint tool; no look is read.

fields.name: name
fields.description: A label for the look: needs `color`, not with `appearance`.

fields.name: opacity
fields.description: 0 (clear) to 1 (opaque). Default: 1, or the appearance's own.

fields.name: pbr
fields.description: The opaque PBR response (needs `color` or `appearance`, and opacity 1).

appearance.paste.label: Paste Look
appearance.paste.help: bodies/faces/components: appearance.assign targets. Applies the copied look atomically in one undo step; no dialogs.

fields.description: bodies/faces/components: appearance.assign targets. Applies the copied look atomically in one undo step; no dialogs.

appearance.pick_up.label: Pick Up Appearance
appearance.pick_up.help: target?: appearance.chain target; returns its resolved look, or requests the UI sampling tool when omitted. Programmatic calls never open UI.

fields.name: target
fields.description:
The body, face or component whose look to read. Left out, the reply asks the UI to
sample one.

appearance.replace.label: Replace Appearance
appearance.replace.help: from: library name | saved look {name,color,opacity,pbr?} (copy appearance.list in_design); to: library name | assignment look {appearance? | color, name?, opacity?, pbr?} (appearance.assign rules; no clear). Matches the full look including name and PBR. scope?: {bodies?: [names], components?: [names or ids]} (a placed copy's name means the body or component it shows), at most 10000 targets; body scope includes face overrides, component scope selects only the component override. Omitted scope means all overrides, including hidden/suppressed ones; physical defaults are unchanged. Duplicate targets count once. Returns count of rewritten overrides; zero adds no history. One undo step, atomic; no dialogs. Designs above 100000 overrides refuse

fields.description: from: library name | saved look {name,color,opacity,pbr?} (copy appearance.list in_design); to: library name | assignment look {appearance? | color, name?, opacity?, pbr?} (appearance.assign rules; no clear). Matches the full look including name and PBR. scope?: {bodies?: [names], components?: [names or ids]} (a placed copy's name means the body or component it shows), at most 10000 targets; body scope includes face overrides, component scope selects only the component override. Omitted scope means all overrides, including hidden/suppressed ones; physical defaults are unchanged. Duplicate targets count once. Returns count of rewritten overrides; zero adds no history. One undo step, atomic; no dialogs. Designs above 100000 overrides refuse

assembly.bom.label: Bill of Materials
assembly.bom.help: component?: id or name (default the design); levels?: flat (default: every part at any depth, counted through its subassemblies) | top (the component's direct children, subassemblies as one row each); group_by?: ["part_number"] (default; components without a part number get a row per definition) | ["definition"]; group_children?: true (a component with a part number is one row, the parts placed inside it listed under it as children: [{item, part_number, description, revision, each, count, definition}], not as rows of their own); path?: write a .csv or .json file (children as items 1.1, 1.2…); format?: csv|json (default from the path). Each component's bom_type counts: phantom has no row (what it holds counts here), reference counts nowhere, purchased and inseparable are one row (in flat, an inseparable one's purchased parts are listed too, under it with group_children and a part number) → rows: [{item, part_number, description, revision, bom_type, count, definition, components, properties, children?}] sorted by part number, total_occurrences (children included)
assembly.bom.description:
The bill of materials below a component: its parts, counted through subassemblies, by part
number. Each component's bom type counts: a phantom has no row (what it holds counts where it
is placed), a reference counts nowhere, and a purchased or inseparable component is one row.

fields.name: component
fields.description: The component, by id or name (default: the design).

fields.name: format
fields.description: With `path`: `csv` or `json`, in any case (default: from the path's extension).

fields.name: group_children
fields.description:
A component with a part number is one row, the parts placed inside it listed under it as
`children` rather than as rows of their own (default false).

fields.name: levels
fields.description:
`flat` (the default): every part at any depth, counted through its subassemblies; `top`:
the component's direct children, subassemblies as one row each.

fields.name: path
fields.description:
Also write the bill of materials to this `.csv` or `.json` file (children as items 1.1,
1.2…).

assembly.bom.reason: not in the live demo: it needs Mechvane's own handling on the server (install Mechvane to use it)

assembly.constraint.create.label: Constrain
assembly.constraint.create.help: type: mate|flush|distance|concentric|insert|parallel|perpendicular|angle|tangent|point_on_axis; a, b: references, as joint.create's origins (a face or a datum plane for a plane, a circle or an axis for an axis, a point; b moves); offset?: the gap (mm or an expression; needed for distance); angle?: deg or an expression (needed for angle); flip?: turn b over; name? (default: the rule and a number, Mate1); quiet?. Kept as a joint of the kind the rule needs (mate and flush planar, distance planar or point on plane, concentric cylindrical, insert revolute, tangent line on plane, point on axis point on line), made where the parts are, so b moves no further than the rule needs → joint, name, dof, conflicts, fixed as joint.create
assembly.constraint.create.description:
Constrain two parts by a geometric rule between a reference on each: the rule is kept as a
joint of the kind it needs (a mate is planar), made where the parts are, so b moves no further
than the rule needs and keeps every motion it leaves free. Several constraints between one pair
add up. One undo step.

fields.name: a
fields.description: A joint origin: the name of a joint origin made with joint.origin, or an object that says where it is, in world coordinates. Give one of face, circle, edge, point, plane or axis (a point [x, y, z]; for face and circle also a face's name; a plane or axis by name or definition object), or a frame {origin, z, x?}.

fields.name: angle
fields.description: A number (degrees for an angle, mm for a distance; below 1e9 in size), or an expression (text) over the design's parameters, such as "width / 2" or "30 deg".

fields.name: b
fields.description: A joint origin: the name of a joint origin made with joint.origin, or an object that says where it is, in world coordinates. Give one of face, circle, edge, point, plane or axis (a point [x, y, z]; for face and circle also a face's name; a plane or axis by name or definition object), or a frame {origin, z, x?}.

fields.name: flip
fields.description:
Turn b over: its reference along a's instead of the way the rule puts it. Default: a mate
is against, a flush along, the others as the parts face now.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The constraint's name. Default: the rule and the first free number (Mate1).

fields.name: offset
fields.description: A number (degrees for an angle, mm for a distance; below 1e9 in size), or an expression (text) over the design's parameters, such as "width / 2" or "30 deg".

fields.name: quiet
fields.description: Leave out `dof` and `fixed` in the reply. Default: false.

fields.name: type
fields.description: The rule: mate (two planes against each other), flush (two planes facing the same way), distance (a plane or a point `offset` from a plane), concentric (two round faces on one axis), insert (two round edges at one centre: only a turn is left), parallel, perpendicular, angle (two planes or axes), tangent (a cylinder resting on a plane) or point_on_axis. Case, spaces, `_` and `-` are ignored; coincident and axis are also taken.

assembly.constraint.create.reason: its two references are taken with the workspace's own picker (component, face), not as raw references

assembly.constraint.edit.label: Edit Constraint
assembly.constraint.edit.help: constraint: id|name (a joint made with assembly.constraint.create); type?: a rule as assembly.constraint.create takes it (the references it has must fit it; the gap carries over); offset?: the gap (mm or an expression); angle?: an angle rule's angle; flip?: true turns b over (from the new rule's way after a type change, else from how it faces now); name?; suppressed?; quiet?. Changed as joint.edit changes a joint: its values start again where its parts are → conflicts, errors, dof, fixed as joint.edit
assembly.constraint.edit.description:
Change a constraint (a joint made with `assembly.constraint.create`) in place: its rule, gap,
angle, facing, name or suppression. A new rule must fit the references the constraint has; the gap
carries over. The change goes through joint.edit: the values start again where the parts are.

fields.name: angle
fields.description: An angle rule's angle: an angle, or an expression. Needed to change to angle.

fields.name: constraint
fields.description: A feature's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: flip
fields.description: True turns b over: from the new rule's way after a type change, else from how it faces now.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The constraint's new name.

fields.name: offset
fields.description: The gap: a length, or an expression the constraint follows. Default: the gap it has.

fields.name: quiet
fields.description: Leave out the degrees of freedom and the fixed occurrences in the reply.

fields.name: suppressed
fields.description: Suppress the constraint (true) or bring it back (false).

fields.name: type
fields.description: The new rule, as assembly.constraint.create takes it. Default: the rule it has.

assembly.constraint.edit.reason: not in the live demo: it needs Mechvane's own handling on the server (install Mechvane to use it)

assembly.mass_properties.label: Mass Properties
assembly.mass_properties.help: no parameters → occurrences: [{occurrence (0: the design's own bodies), name, component, path, group, fixed, frame {origin, x, y, z}, bodies: [{name, material, density_g_cm3, closed, volume_mm3, mass_kg}], open_bodies_skipped, mass}], groups: [{group, occurrences, fixed, frame_occurrence, frame, mass}] (occurrences an unsuppressed rigid joint ties together, and a nested occurrence no joint places with its parent; fixed: holds the design or a grounded occurrence), warnings. mass: {mass_kg, center_of_mass_mm (world), center_of_mass_local_mm, inertia_world_kg_mm2, inertia_local_kg_mm2 (about the centre of mass, in world and frame axes)} or null when massless. Read-only; pending moves count; each body at its material's density (the default material's when none is assigned)
assembly.mass_properties.description:
Mass, centre of mass and inertia tensor of every occurrence of the design and of every rigid
group (occurrences joined by rigid joints, which move as one body), from each body's material
density. Read-only.

body.print_face.label: Print Face
body.print_face.help: body: its name; point?: [x, y, z] on a flat face of it, in mm (omit to clear) → {body, face?}: marks the face a slicer export (file.send_to_slicer, file.save_mesh with slicer, file.open_in_easyprint), or an STL or 3MF export with lay_on_print_faces (file.export, file.export_stl, file.export_3mf, file.save_mesh), lays the body on: turned so the face points down at Z = 0, the centre of mass over the origin. One per body, replacing the last; flat faces of solid bodies only. A print face that is gone or no longer flat is reported in the export's warnings, and the body exported as it lies
body.print_face.description:
Mark the flat face of a body at a point as the body's print face, or clear it. A slicer
export (`file.send_to_slicer`, `file.save_mesh` with `slicer`, `file.open_in_easyprint`), and an
STL or 3MF export with `lay_on_print_faces` (`file.export`, `file.export_stl`, `file.export_3mf`,
`file.save_mesh`), lays the body on its print face: turned so the face points down and lies at
Z = 0, the centre of mass over the origin. A body has one print face at most; marking another
replaces it.

fields.name: body
fields.description: The body, by name. Solid bodies only: a mesh body can't have a print face yet.

fields.name: point
fields.description: A point on the flat face to mark, in mm. Default: none, which clears the body's print face.

body.rename.label: Rename Body
body.rename.help: body: its name, or bodies: several body names (each in turn gets the first of name, name (2), name (3)… that no other body has), name: the new name (features that use the bodies follow)
body.rename.description:
Rename a body, or several bodies with one name (numbered after the first); the features that
use them follow. A placed copy's name means the body it shows. One undo step.

fields.name: bodies
fields.description: Body names, as `body` takes one. The first body gets `name`, the next ones `name (2)`, `name (3)` and so on; a numbered name another body already has is skipped.

fields.name: body
fields.description: A body's name. A placed copy's name (`KB (K:2)`) means the body it shows.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Text of 1 to 128 bytes once surrounding spaces are cut.

body.repair.label: Repair Part
body.repair.help: body: its name (a part the modelling kernel refuses, or an open part that should be a solid); gap?: expr (default 0.2 mm, at most 1 mm: free edges that pair up within it are sewn, each sewn edge carrying its own gap as its tolerance); patch_holes?: bool (default false: loops of free edges left are patched, in the plane of the faces around them where those are that plane, else tangent to them, and sewn in; otherwise the reply offers the patches); name? → the feature, and repair: what changed face by face (rebuilt and refused faces, sewn gaps, holes with their surface.patch), faces and largest edge tolerance before and after, closed, modelling, volume. Refused with why when nothing applies
body.repair.description:
Repair a part the modelling kernel refuses, or an open part that should be a solid: faces
SMLib refuses on their own are rebuilt on their own surfaces (geometry unchanged), free edges
that pair up within `gap` are sewn (each sewn edge carries its own gap as its tolerance; the
body's and the other edges' stay), and with `patch_holes` the loops of free edges left (missing
faces) are patched and sewn in. One undoable feature; refused, with why, when nothing applies.

fields.name: body
fields.description: The part (body name).

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: gap
fields.description:
The widest gap between two free edges that is sewn, more than 0 and at most 1 mm.
Default: 0.2 mm.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

fields.name: patch_holes
fields.description:
Patch each loop of free edges no pair explains (a missing face) and sew the patch in: the
plane of the faces around it where they are all that plane, else a patch tangent to them
(G1). Default: false (the reply offers the patches).

browser.collapse_all.label: Collapse All
browser.collapse_all.help: path?: [occurrence ids] (that placement's branch); component?: id; omit both for the whole tree: every placement, folder and group at every level. The row it starts from (the design row for the whole tree) stays open, so its first level remains visible. Display only; not an undo step → open, open_by_default, closed_by_default
browser.collapse_all.description:
Open every row of the Browser below a row (`browser.expand_all`) or close them, the row
itself staying open (`browser.collapse_all`). Display only: not saved with the design and not
an undo step. Give `path` or `component`, not both; neither takes the whole tree.

fields.name: component
fields.description: A component's id; 0 is the design.

fields.name: path
fields.description: A placement, by the occurrence ids from the design down.

browser.collapse_all.reason: acts only on SolidCraft's hidden model browser

browser.expand_all.label: Expand All
browser.expand_all.help: path?: [occurrence ids] (that placement and its descendants); component?: id (that component's own folders); omit both for the whole tree, including folders that start closed (Origin, Named Views, Features). Display only: open/closed rows are not saved in the design and are not an undo step → open, open_by_default, closed_by_default
browser.expand_all.description:
Open every row of the Browser below a row (`browser.expand_all`) or close them, the row
itself staying open (`browser.collapse_all`). Display only: not saved with the design and not
an undo step. Give `path` or `component`, not both; neither takes the whole tree.

fields.name: component
fields.description: A component's id; 0 is the design.

fields.name: path
fields.description: A placement, by the occurrence ids from the design down.

browser.expand_all.reason: acts only on SolidCraft's hidden model browser

browser.group.label: New Group
browser.group.help: folder?: bodies|sketches|construction; component?: id (default 0); parent?: group id (the new group nests in it, taking its component and folder; at most 8 levels); name?; items?: [keys] (they leave other groups)
browser.group.description: Make a group in a Browser folder, of the items given or empty. One undo step.

fields.name: component
fields.description: The component whose folder it is. Default: 0, the design.

fields.name: folder
fields.description: A browser folder: bodies, sketches or construction.

fields.name: items
fields.description: Item keys (strings).

fields.name: name
fields.description: The group's name, at most 128 bytes. Default: "Group" and the next number in the folder.

fields.name: parent
fields.description:
The group the new one nests in, which gives it its component and folder (at most 8
levels).

browser.move.label: Move Browser Items
browser.move.help: folder, component?, items: [keys (strings) and group ids (numbers)]; group?: id (into it; omit for the folder's top level); before?: key or group id (position in it; default the end). A group cannot go into itself or past 8 levels
browser.move.description:
Move items and groups in a Browser folder: into a group or to the folder's top level, before
an item or group or at the end. A group can't go into itself or past 8 levels. One undo step.

fields.name: before
fields.description: Put them before this item key or group id, in the list they go into. Default: the end.

fields.name: component
fields.description: The component whose folder it is. Default: 0, the design.

fields.name: folder
fields.description: A browser folder: bodies, sketches or construction.

fields.name: group
fields.description: The group to move them into. Default: the folder's top level.

fields.name: items
fields.description: Item keys (strings) and group ids (numbers); a number is always a group.

browser.order.label: Order Browser Items
browser.order.help: folder: bodies|sketches|construction|components, component?, order: [keys (strings) and top-level group ids (numbers)] (display order; for `components`, the ids of the components placed in it)
browser.order.description:
Set the display order of a Browser folder. An item that sits in a group belongs to the
group's list only. One undo step.

fields.name: component
fields.description: The component whose folder it is. Default: 0, the design.

fields.name: folder
fields.description: A browser folder: bodies, sketches, construction or components.

fields.name: order
fields.description: Item keys (strings) and top-level group ids (numbers); a number is always a group.

browser.rename_group.label: Rename Group
browser.rename_group.description: Rename a Browser group. One undo step.

fields.name: group
fields.description: A browser group's id (see `browser.group`).

fields.name: name
fields.description: Text of 1 to 128 bytes once surrounding spaces are cut.

browser.reparent.label: Move to Component
browser.reparent.help: Moves placements, features and bodies into a component. occurrences?: [ids or paths], features?: [ids or names], bodies?: [names], component?: where they go (default: the active one), component_path?: its placement → component, occurrences, features, bodies (what moved). One undo step, all or nothing: placements move first (taking what they hold), then features (taking the bodies they made), then the bodies still elsewhere (a body transfer, which leaves its features behind)
browser.reparent.description:
Move placements, timeline features and bodies into a component in one undo step, all or
nothing. Placements move first and take what they hold, then features, which take the bodies
they made, then the bodies still elsewhere (a body transfer, which leaves its features
behind). Anything already in the component is left alone.

fields.name: bodies
fields.description: The bodies to move, by name.

fields.name: component
fields.description: The component they go to, by id or name. Default: the active component.

fields.name: component_path
fields.description: The placement of that component to place them by, as occurrence ids from the top.

fields.name: features
fields.description: The features to move, by id or name.

fields.name: occurrences
fields.description: The placements to move.

browser.ungroup.label: Ungroup
browser.ungroup.help: group: id (its items and child groups go up to the group that holds it, or the folder)
browser.ungroup.description:
Remove a group: its items and child groups go up to the group that holds it, or the folder,
in the place the group had. One undo step.

fields.name: group
fields.description: A browser group's id (see `browser.group`).

browser.visibility.label: Show/Hide
browser.visibility.help: visible: bool; items?: [sketch id or name | body name | construction name | joint name | O|X|Y|Z|XY|XZ|YZ]; or joints?: [joint id or name] (their glyphs; they still constrain and move parts); or features?: [feature id or name] (the bodies they made; path?: [occurrence ids] for only that placement's); or folder?: bodies|sketches|construction|origin|joints|all (all of it; showing also shows its browser folders and groups, and `all` takes in the occurrence hides too); or tree_folders?: [browser folder or group key: c0/bodies, o:4/sketches, o:4/origin, c0/g7, c0/joints, c0/canvases, c0/point_clouds] (the folder or group itself: its items keep their own state; component origin items use o:4/origin/XY etc. in items); or paths?: [[occurrence ids]] (exact placements and descendants), isolate?: bool (with paths or items of bodies, and visible:true: everything else is hidden, other placements as placements). Saved with the design and undone like any other change (the camera is not)
browser.visibility.description:
Show or hide what is in the Browser: name one kind of target (`items`, `joints`, `features`,
`folder`, `tree_folders` or `paths`). Saved with the design and undone like any other
change; the camera is not. With `isolate`, everything else is hidden.

fields.name: features
fields.description: Feature ids or names.

fields.name: folder
fields.description:
All of a kind: bodies, sketches, construction, origin, joints or all. Showing also shows
the browser folders and groups that hold it, and `all` takes in the occurrence hides.

fields.name: isolate
fields.description:
With `paths`, or `items` of bodies, and `visible: true`: show only those and hide
everything else, other placements as placements. Default: false.

fields.name: items
fields.description: Sketches (id or name), bodies, construction items, joints or origin items (O, X, Y, Z, XY, XZ, YZ), by name.

fields.name: joints
fields.description: Joint ids (numbers) or names.

fields.name: path
fields.description:
With `features`: only the bodies of this placement, which must be one of the features'
component.

fields.name: paths
fields.description: Placements, each by the occurrence ids from the design down; each with its descendants.

fields.name: tree_folders
fields.description: Browser folder or group keys: `c0` (the design) or `o:` and the placement's occurrence ids joined by `/`, then `/bodies`, `/sketches`, `/construction`, `/joints`, `/canvases`, `/point_clouds` or `/g` and a group id.

fields.name: visible
fields.description: true to show, false to hide.

canvas.calibrate.label: Calibrate Canvas
canvas.calibrate.help: canvas: id or name; a, b: two points on the canvas plane [x,y]; distance: their true distance (mm): scales the image about a
canvas.calibrate.description:
Scale a canvas so that two points on it are a known distance apart: the image is scaled about
the first point. One undo step.

fields.name: a
fields.description: A sketch point in mm: [x, y] or {"x", "y"}.

fields.name: b
fields.description: A sketch point in mm: [x, y] or {"x", "y"}.

fields.name: canvas
fields.description: A canvas's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: distance
fields.description: A distance in mm: above 0 (more than 0.000000001) and below 1 000 000 000.

canvas.decal.label: Decal
canvas.decal.help: path | data; face: [x,y,z] on a planar face (the image is centred there), or the picked face as sketch.create's plane takes it ({face, body, index, path?}); width?: mm; angle?: deg; opacity?: (default 1)
canvas.decal.description:
Put an image on a planar face of the model, like a sticker, kept in the design. Give the image
as `path` or as base64 `data`; only PNG and JPEG are taken, up to 16 MiB. The image goes into
the active component. One undo step.

fields.name: angle
fields.description: Its rotation on the plane, in degrees (a number of 1e9 or more is ignored). Default: 0.

fields.name: at
fields.description:
A point [x, y, z] in mm, projected onto the plane, for the centre when `center` is not
given. Default: the picked point.

fields.name: center
fields.description:
Where the image's centre is, on the face's plane, in mm. Default: `at`, or the picked
point.

fields.name: data
fields.description: The image itself, a PNG or JPEG, as base64. Wins over `path`.

fields.name: face
fields.description: A point [x, y, z] in mm on a planar face, or a picked face {"face": [x, y, z], "body"?, "index"?, "path"?, "fixed"?}: "body" (the picked body's world name) and "index" (the face's index in it) pick the face exactly and go together; "path" is the occurrence path of the body's placement (at most 64 nonzero ids); "fixed": true keeps the plane where the face is now.

fields.name: flip
fields.description: Mirror it left to right. Default: false.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Its name. Default: "Decal" and the first number no canvas's name has.

fields.name: offset
fields.description: Move the face's plane this far along its normal (mm or a length expression).

fields.name: opacity
fields.description: Its opacity, 0 (clear) to 1 (opaque); a value outside is clamped (a number of 1e9 or more is ignored, as if left out). Default: 1.

fields.name: path
fields.description:
A PNG or JPEG file to read (not blank, under 4096 characters). Used when `data` is not
given.

fields.name: width
fields.description:
The image's width on the plane, in mm (above 0, below 1e7); its height follows the
image. Default: 100.

canvas.decal.reason: not in the live demo: it needs Mechvane's own handling on the server (install Mechvane to use it)

canvas.delete.label: Delete Canvas
canvas.delete.description: Remove a canvas or decal from the design. One undo step.

fields.name: canvas
fields.description: A canvas's id (a number) or its name.

canvas.edit.label: Edit Canvas
canvas.edit.help: canvas: id or name; center?, width?, angle?: deg, opacity?, flip?, visible?, name?, locked? (a locked canvas refuses center, width, angle, flip, Calibrate and Delete)
canvas.edit.description:
Change a canvas or decal: its place, size, angle, opacity, mirroring, visibility or name. Keys
left out stay as they are. One undo step.

fields.name: angle
fields.description: Its new rotation on the plane, in degrees (a number of 1e9 or more is ignored).

fields.name: canvas
fields.description: A canvas's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: center
fields.description: The image's new centre on its plane, in mm.

fields.name: flip
fields.description: Mirror it left to right, or not.

fields.name: locked
fields.description:
Lock it or unlock it. A locked canvas refuses a new centre, width, angle or flip, Calibrate
and Delete until it is unlocked; its opacity, visibility and name can still change.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Its new name; blank text keeps the name.

fields.name: opacity
fields.description: Its new opacity, 0 (clear) to 1 (opaque); a value outside is clamped (a number of 1e9 or more is ignored, as if left out).

fields.name: visible
fields.description: Show it or hide it.

fields.name: width
fields.description: Its new width, in mm (above 0, below 1e7); its height follows the image.

canvas.insert.label: Canvas
canvas.insert.help: path | data (base64 PNG or JPEG); plane?: XY|XZ|YZ|{face: [x,y,z]}|… (default XY); center?: [x,y] on the plane, or at?: [x,y,z]; width?: mm (default 100); angle?: deg; opacity?: 0…1 (default 0.5); flip?; name?
canvas.insert.description:
Place an image on a plane as a reference to trace, kept in the design. Give the image as
`path` or as base64 `data`; only PNG and JPEG are taken, up to 16 MiB. The image goes into the
active component. One undo step.

fields.name: angle
fields.description: Its rotation on the plane, in degrees (a number of 1e9 or more is ignored). Default: 0.

fields.name: at
fields.description:
A point [x, y, z] in mm, projected onto the plane, for the centre when `center` is not
given. Default: the picked point when `plane` is a picked face, else the plane's origin.

fields.name: center
fields.description:
Where the image's centre is, on the plane, in mm. Default: `at`; else the picked point when
`plane` is a picked face; else the plane's origin.

fields.name: data
fields.description: The image itself, a PNG or JPEG, as base64. Wins over `path`.

fields.name: flip
fields.description: Mirror it left to right. Default: false.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Its name. Default: "Canvas" and the first number no canvas's name has.

fields.name: offset
fields.description: Move the plane this far along its normal (mm or a length expression).

fields.name: opacity
fields.description: Its opacity, 0 (clear) to 1 (opaque); a value outside is clamped (a number of 1e9 or more is ignored, as if left out). Default: 0.5.

fields.name: path
fields.description:
A PNG or JPEG file to read (not blank, under 4096 characters). Used when `data` is not
given.

fields.name: plane
fields.description: A plane: XY, XZ or YZ (or Top, Front or Right; any case), a construction plane's name or feature id, a picked planar face {"face": [x, y, z], "body"?, "index"?, "path"?, "fixed"?}, or an explicit plane {"origin"?, "x_dir", "y_dir"}: two directions [x, y, z] that aren't parallel and an origin in mm, numbers only (default: the origin).

fields.name: width
fields.description:
The image's width on the plane, in mm (above 0, below 1e7); its height follows the
image. Default: 100.

canvas.insert.reason: not in the live demo: it needs Mechvane's own handling on the server (install Mechvane to use it)

canvas.straighten.label: Straighten Canvas
canvas.straighten.help: canvas: id or name; a, b: two points on the canvas plane [x,y] along a line of the image; angle?: deg, the direction that line should have (0 horizontal, the default; 90 vertical): turns the image about a, the shorter way
canvas.straighten.description:
Turn a canvas so that a line drawn on its image, from `a` to `b`, gets the direction `angle`:
0 makes it horizontal, 90 vertical. The image turns about `a`, the shorter way (a line has no
arrow, so the turn is at most 90 degrees either way and the image stays the right way up). Its
size does not change. One undo step.

fields.name: a
fields.description: A sketch point in mm: [x, y] or {"x", "y"}.

fields.name: angle
fields.description:
The direction the line should have on the plane, in degrees from the plane's x axis,
counter-clockwise: 0 horizontal, 90 vertical. Default: 0.

fields.name: b
fields.description: A sketch point in mm: [x, y] or {"x", "y"}.

fields.name: canvas
fields.description: A canvas's id (a number) or its name.

canvas.to_sketch.label: Canvas to Sketch
canvas.to_sketch.help: canvas?: id or name (default: the last canvas); name?: the new sketch's name. Traces the canvas image (dark drawing on a light background, or the reverse) into a new sketch on the canvas plane, lying exactly on the image: lines, splines and holes
canvas.to_sketch.description:
Trace a canvas or decal image into a new sketch lying exactly on its plane: the drawing is
told from the background, its outlines become lines and cubic splines, and its holes stay
holes. The picture is read at up to 512 pixels on a side, at most 40 megapixels.

fields.name: canvas
fields.description: The canvas, by id or name. Default: the last canvas in the design.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The new sketch's name. Default: `<the canvas's name> sketch`.

component.activate.label: Activate Component
component.activate.help: component: id or name (0 or "root" for the design); occurrence?, path?: exact placement used to author shared geometry
component.activate.description:
Make a component the active one: new sketches and features go into it, authored in its
frame. With `occurrence` (and `path`), the placement that shared geometry is authored
through. A change of what is active, not an undo step.

fields.name: component
fields.description: A component's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: occurrence
fields.description: An occurrence's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: path
fields.description: An exact placement path: 1 to 64 occurrence ids from the root down.

component.break_link.label: Break Link
component.break_link.help: component: id or name of a linked component — keeps its bodies as they are and forgets the design file
component.break_link.description: Forget a component's link to its design file and keep its bodies as they are. One undo step.

fields.name: component
fields.description: A component's id (a number) or its name.

component.capture_position.label: Capture Position
component.capture_position.help: keeps pending occurrence moves and saves every moving joint's values → captured, joints
component.capture_position.description:
Make every pending occurrence move the occurrence's placement, and save every moving joint's
current values for Revert Position. The exploded view is shown, never captured: it stays
shown, and the design keeps its placements.

component.copies.label: Find Identical Copies
component.copies.help: component: id or name of a linked component → copies: [{component, name}], the components not linked whose own history builds the same bodies
component.copies.description:
Find the components, not linked, whose own history builds the same bodies as a linked
component. The design is not changed.

fields.name: component
fields.description: A component's id (a number) or its name.

component.copy_bodies.label: Paste Bodies
component.copy_bodies.help: bodies: [names, as the Browser shows them: a body seen in another placement of its component (`Cube (B:2)`) is copied from there]; component?: where the copies go (default: the active one); component_path?: its placement to place them by (default: its only one, else the active one; a component placed more than once gets them in every instance). Each copy stays where its body is in the world; the copies' names come back as `bodies`

fields.description: bodies: [names, as the Browser shows them: a body seen in another placement of its component (`Cube (B:2)`) is copied from there]; component?: where the copies go (default: the active one); component_path?: its placement to place them by (default: its only one, else the active one; a component placed more than once gets them in every instance). Each copy stays where its body is in the world; the copies' names come back as `bodies`

component.create.label: New Component
component.create.help: name?, parent?: component id or name (default: the active one); parent_path?: exact parent placement; activate?: bool (default true); grounded?: bool (default: true for the design's first part, false otherwise)
component.create.description:
Make a new component, in the active component unless `parent` says another, and make it the
active one unless `activate` is false. The design's first part is grounded; the others are
not. Bodies are not moved here (`component.move_bodies`, `component.from_bodies`).

fields.name: activate
fields.description: Make it the active component. Default: `true`.

fields.name: grounded
fields.description: Ground its placement. Default: `true` for the design's first part, `false` otherwise.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The new component's name. Default: a name made from the design's naming.

fields.name: parent
fields.description: A component's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: parent_path
fields.description: An exact placement path: up to 63 occurrence ids from the root down; empty for the design itself.

component.cycle_color.label: Cycle Component Color
component.cycle_color.help: component: id or name; saves the next identification colour and turns Component Colors on; shared by every instance, separate from appearances
component.cycle_color.description:
Give a component the next colour of the Component Colors palette (`component.cycle_color`). The
colour is shared by every instance of the component and is separate from its appearances.

fields.name: component
fields.description: A component's id (a number) or its name.

component.delete.label: Delete Component
component.delete.help: component: deletes it, its subcomponents, occurrences and features
component.delete.description:
Delete a component with its subcomponents, placements and features. Refused for the design
itself, and for a tree that supplies a body transfer recorded outside it.

fields.name: component
fields.description: A component's id (a number) or its name.

component.delete.reason: removes a part from the assembly: Mechvane's joints and bolted connections must follow

component.edit_in_place.label: Edit in Place
component.edit_in_place.help: component: id or name of a linked component; path?: its placement (occurrence ids, default its first) → in the app window: open the design it links in a tab of its own with the assembly drawn around it (component.finish_edit goes back); fails when it is not linked, the assembly has no file yet, something is open or running in it, or the file is missing, on a network location not allowed yet or open in another SolidCraft; asked during the agent's turn it opens once the turn ends (queued: true); elsewhere it only checks
component.edit_in_place.description:
Edit a linked component's design in place. In the app window: open the design it links in a
tab of its own, with the rest of the assembly drawn faded around it as the placement `path`
puts it; `component.finish_edit` goes back. It fails when the component is not linked, the
assembly has no file yet, something is open or running in it, or the linked file is missing,
on a network location not allowed yet or open in another SolidCraft. Asked while the
assembly's agent is in its turn, the part opens once the turn ends (`queued`). Outside the
window it only checks the component and the placement.

fields.name: component
fields.description: A feature's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: path
fields.description:
The placement to edit it at, as occurrence ids from the top of the assembly down
(`component.list`). Default: the component's first placement.

component.extract.label: Extract to File
component.extract.help: component: id or name of a component that is not linked; path: the .sc design to write → its history, subcomponents and their joints move to that design, and the component becomes linked to it (as component.insert_design makes it); returns path, file, feature, bodies, notices (what stays behind), warnings and copies (components that build the same bodies: see component.replace_with_link)
component.extract.description:
Move a component's history, subcomponents and their joints into a design file of its own and
link the component to that file, as `component.insert_design` would have made it. The
component must not be linked already. Anything that crosses the component's boundary is
refused. One undo step.

fields.name: component
fields.description: A component's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: path
fields.description: The design file to write, a `.sc`.

component.extract.reason: reads or writes a file outside the design: needs a file picker

component.finish_edit.label: Finish Edit
component.finish_edit.help: no parameters → in the app window: go back from the linked design edited in place to its assembly, which reads it again; fails while the design has unsaved changes (run file.save first) or something is open in it; asked during the agent's turn it finishes once the turn ends (queued: true); elsewhere nothing changes
component.finish_edit.description:
Finish editing a linked component's design in place. In the app window: go back to the
assembly around it, which reads the link again, and close the part's tab when the edit opened
it. It fails while the part has unsaved changes (save it first) or something is open in it;
asked while the part's agent is in its turn, it finishes once the turn ends (`queued`). Outside the window
nothing is edited in place, so nothing changes.

component.from_bodies.label: Create Components from Bodies
component.from_bodies.help: bodies: [names] → one new component per body, named after it
component.from_bodies.description:
Make one new component per body, in the active component and named after the body, and move
each body into its component, keeping it where it is in the world. All or nothing, one undo
step; refused while the timeline is rolled back.

fields.name: bodies
fields.description: 1 to 1000 different body names.

component.hide_history.label: Hide Component History
component.hide_history.help: component: id or name; keeps the component's features in the design but leaves them out of the History bar (#10393)
component.hide_history.description:
Keep a component's features in the design but out of the History bar (`component.hide_history`),
or put them back (`component.show_history`). A component inside one that is hidden is left out of
the bar too; the design itself never is, and its features always show.

fields.name: component
fields.description: A component's id (a number) or its name.

component.insert_design.label: Insert Design
component.insert_design.help: path: a .sc design → a new component linked to it, holding its solid bodies as placed in that design and a copy of its design properties; configuration?: a row name or id (null or omitted: the saved source state); name? (default: the design's name); parent?: component id or name (default: the active one); translate?: [x,y,z] in mm from the destination parent's origin (default [0,0,0], also with reuse); reuse?: bool (default false): insert a free occurrence, reusing an existing link to the same file and configuration when available
component.insert_design.description:
Insert a design file as a new component linked to it: its solid bodies as placed in that
design, and a copy of its design properties. The link remembers the file, so
`component.update_links` can read it again. One undo step. With `reuse`, a design already
linked gets another placement instead of another link.

fields.name: configuration
fields.description:
Source configuration row, by name or stable id. Omitted or null follows the source's
saved state. The link stores the resolved id, so renaming the row keeps the selection.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The component's name. Default: the design's name.

fields.name: parent
fields.description: A component's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: path
fields.description: The design (`.sc`) to link, by file path.

fields.name: reuse
fields.description:
Reuse an existing link to the same file and configuration when there is one, placing
another occurrence of it. Default: false.

fields.name: translate
fields.description: Where to place it, in mm from the parent's origin. Default: [0, 0, 0], also with `reuse`.

component.insert_design.reason: reads or writes a file outside the design: needs a file picker

component.links.label: List Links
component.links.help: → linked components: component, name, path, configuration (selected row id, omitted when following the saved source state), file (resolved), found (null when the file is on a network location not allowed, or names a device: it is not looked for), changed (whether the file is no longer what this design last read: Update Links reads it again; null when not found or the link is older than this record), then host (the network location); state (missing, unreadable, not_allowed: a network location not allowed or outside the folders this agent may use) and reason when the file can't be reached

component.list.label: List Components
component.list.help: compact?: bool (counts of bodies, features, sketches and construction planes instead of their names; occurrences leave out identity transforms; children as occurrence ids); bodies?: bool (with compact: body names, not their count)
component.list.description:
List the components as a tree: each with its bodies, features, sketches, construction planes,
placements and children, the active component and the pending moves. The design is not
changed.

fields.name: bodies
fields.description:
With `compact`: body names, not their count. Read only with `compact: true`. Default:
`false`.

fields.name: compact
fields.description:
Counts of bodies, features, sketches and construction planes instead of their names;
placements leave out identity transforms; children as occurrence ids. Default: `false`.

component.metadata.label: Part Properties
component.metadata.help: component: id or name (0 or "root": the design's own properties) → component, name, part_number, description, revision, bom_type (components only), metadata (as saved, other tools' keys too), properties: {name: text}
component.metadata.description:
Read the part properties of a component, or of the design itself (`0` or `root`): part
number, description, revision, bill of materials type, the `metadata` object as saved and the
free properties.

fields.name: component
fields.description: The component, by id or name (0 or "root": the design itself).

component.metadata.set.label: Change Part Properties
component.metadata.set.help: component: id or name (not the root: use document.metadata.set); part_number?, description?, revision?: text (empty or null removes); bom_type?: normal|phantom|reference|purchased|inseparable (empty or null: normal); values?: {key: value} (SolidCraft's keys, as document.metadata's properties lists them, bom_type, or a reverse-DNS key holding an object); properties?: {name: text, …} (free properties; empty or null removes). All or nothing, one undo step → component, metadata, properties, changed: [keys]
component.metadata.set.description:
Change a component's part properties in one undo step (all or nothing): `part_number`,
`description`, `revision` and `bom_type`, `values` for several keys at once (also another
tool's reverse-DNS keys), and `properties` for free properties. Not the design's own
(`document.metadata.set`). Give at least one of them. A change that sets what is already
there makes no undo step.

fields.name: bom_type
fields.description:
How the component counts in the bill of materials: `normal`, `phantom`, `reference`,
`purchased` or `inseparable`. Empty text or null: `normal`.

fields.name: component
fields.description: The component, by id or name (0 or "root": the design itself).

fields.name: description
fields.description: The description: text of at most 4096 bytes. Empty text or null removes it.

fields.name: part_number
fields.description: The part number: text of at most 4096 bytes. Empty text or null removes it.

fields.name: properties
fields.description: Free properties, {name: text, …}, at most 256 names (a name is 1 to 128 bytes of text without control characters; a number or boolean is kept as its text). Empty text or null removes a property.

fields.name: revision
fields.description: The revision: text of at most 4096 bytes. Empty text or null removes it.

fields.name: values
fields.description: Several properties at once, {key: value, …}, at most 256 keys: SolidCraft's keys (the ones `document.metadata`'s `properties` lists) and `bom_type`, which take text, or a reverse-DNS key such as `com.example.tool`, which takes an object. Each key reads its value as the parameter of the same name does (`part_number`, `bom_type`, …): for a text key, empty text or null removes it; for `bom_type` it means `normal`.

component.move_bodies.label: Move Bodies to Component
component.move_bodies.help: bodies: [names], component; component_path?: its placement to place them by (default: its only one, else the active one; a component placed more than once gets them in every instance); from_path?: the placement of their component they move from (default: its only one, else its first, where its bodies have their own names)
component.move_bodies.description:
Move bodies into another component, keeping them where they are in the world. All or
nothing, one undo step; refused while the timeline is rolled back.

fields.name: bodies
fields.description: 1 to 1000 different body names.

fields.name: component
fields.description: A component's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: component_path
fields.description: An exact placement path: up to 64 occurrence ids from the root down; empty for the design itself.

fields.name: from_path
fields.description: An exact placement path: up to 64 occurrence ids from the root down; empty for the design itself.

component.move_features.label: Move Features to Component
component.move_features.help: features: [ids or names] (sketches too); component?: where they go (default: the active one) → moved, component, bodies. Ids, names and timeline order stay; the geometry stays where it is in the world; the bodies the features made move with them. Refused while the timeline is rolled back, for a component placed more than once, and for a move that would break a feature (nothing changes)
component.move_features.description:
Move timeline features (sketches too) into a component. Their ids, names and timeline order
stay, the geometry stays where it is in the world, and the bodies they made move with them.
Nothing changes when the move would break a feature, while the timeline is rolled back, or
for a component placed more than once.

fields.name: component
fields.description: The component they go to, by id or name. Default: the active component.

fields.name: features
fields.description: The features to move, by id or name.

component.move_sketches.label: Move Sketches to Component
component.move_sketches.help: sketches: [ids or names] (a number is an id; a string is an exact name, then an id), component; the sketches keep their own coordinates (component.move_features keeps them where they are in the world), except that a sketch on an exactly attached face stays where it is on the face
component.move_sketches.description:
Move sketches into another component. They keep their own coordinates (`component.move_features`
keeps them where they are in the world), except that a sketch on an exactly attached face
stays where it is on the face.

fields.name: component
fields.description: A component's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: sketches
fields.description: The sketches: one name, or a list of 1 to 10000 names and ids. A number is an id; a string is an exact name, then an id.

component.move_sketches.to_parts.label: Move Sketches to Their Parts
component.move_sketches.to_parts.help: sketches?: [ids or names] (default: every sketch in the design) → moved, stayed, sketches [{sketch, name, component, part}], kept [{sketch, name, code, reason}]. Each sketch whose plane is an exactly attached face of a part's body goes to that part, as component.move_sketches moves it, and stays where it is on the face; the others (on an origin, construction or fixed plane, on a body of the design itself, or already in their part) stay where they are. One undo step
component.move_sketches.to_parts.description:
Move sketches to the part whose face they are drawn on (`component.move_sketches.to_parts`),
in one undo step. A sketch whose plane is an exactly attached face of a part's body goes to
that part, staying where it is on the face; the others stay where they are.

fields.name: sketches
fields.description: The sketches to look at, by id or name. Default: every sketch in the design.

component.paste_from_design.label: Paste from Another Design
component.paste_from_design.help: component?: where it goes (default: the active one); component_path?: its placement (default: the active one, else its only one). Pastes what was copied in another design, at the same world coordinates: its bodies as imported bodies (no history) in one Import feature, or its components as independent copies with their history, appearances, joints and motion (as `component.paste_new`); the user parameters they use come along, renamed `w_2` when taken. A component that uses what isn't in it (another body, sketch or parameter) is refused, saying what. Returns `bodies` and `feature`, or the pasted components' `paths`

fields.description: component?: where it goes (default: the active one); component_path?: its placement (default: the active one, else its only one). Pastes what was copied in another design, at the same world coordinates: its bodies as imported bodies (no history) in one Import feature, or its components as independent copies with their history, appearances, joints and motion (as `component.paste_new`); the user parameters they use come along, renamed `w_2` when taken. A component that uses what isn't in it (another body, sketch or parameter) is refused, saying what. Returns `bodies` and `feature`, or the pasted components' `paths`

component.paste_new.label: Paste New
component.paste_new.help: component: independently copy its nested definition graph and history, materials and styles; occurrence?, path?: selected source placement; parent?: component the copy goes in (default: the source placement's; not the component or one inside it); in_place?, parent_path?: as occurrence.copy; translate?: [x,y,z]. Reassigned external bodies become base geometry; retained external links and omitted boundary joints are reported
component.paste_new.description:
Paste New: an independent copy of a component, with its nested components, features, bodies,
materials, styles, joints and motion, placed at the source placement's transform (pending
moves included) moved by `translate`. Unlike `occurrence.copy`, the copy shares nothing with
the original. A body reassigned from outside becomes base geometry; links kept to outside
things and joints omitted at the boundary are listed in `notices`.

fields.name: component
fields.description: A component's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: in_place
fields.description:
`false`: the copy has the source transform within its parent. `true`: it sits where the
source placement is in the world, and `translate` is along the world axes. Default:
`false`.

fields.name: occurrence
fields.description: An occurrence's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: parent
fields.description: A component's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: parent_path
fields.description: An exact placement path: up to 64 occurrence ids from the root down; empty for the design itself.

fields.name: path
fields.description: An exact placement path: 1 to 64 occurrence ids from the root down.

fields.name: translate
fields.description: A point in mm: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}.

component.properties.label: Component Physical Properties
component.properties.help: component?: id or name (default active); descendants?: bool (default true); about?: [x, y, z] (mm). Measures the first placement, or all placements for root, including pending moves; material-aware mass and center of mass in world coordinates; volume, density, mass, center of mass and inertia_g_mm2 (the inertia tensor about the body's center of mass, world axes, from its tessellation) only for closed, consistently oriented bodies; total.open_bodies_skipped counts open bodies excluded from volume/mass totals; total.first_moment_g_mm (mass × center of mass), inertia_g_mm2 about the total center of mass, principal_moments_g_mm2 (smallest first) and principal_axes (unit, right-handed); with about, total.inertia_about {point, inertia_g_mm2}
component.properties.description:
Measure a component where its first placement puts it (every placement for the design):
material-aware mass and centre of mass in world coordinates, volume, density, and inertia
for closed, consistently oriented bodies, with totals and principal moments. Pending moves
are included. The design is not changed.

fields.name: about
fields.description: A point in mm, also given the total inertia about it (`total.inertia_about`).

fields.name: component
fields.description: A component's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: descendants
fields.description: Include the components and placements inside it. Default: `true`.

component.relink.label: Relink Source
component.relink.help: component: id or name of a linked component; path: a saved design (.sc or .json); configuration?: row name or id, null to follow the saved source state (omitted: keep the selection for the same file, otherwise follow the new file) — replaces the source and linked bodies for all its occurrences, preserving identities and placements; occurrence?: one of its placements — when it has others, only that placement comes to show the design, as a placement of the component already linked to it or of a new one under the same parent, keeping its position and joints (component is then the one it shows, previous_component the one it showed); returns path, previous_path, warnings, joint_errors and joint_conflicts
component.relink.description:
Replace the source of a linked component with another saved design, for all its occurrences,
keeping their identities and placements, or with `occurrence` for that one only. The design is
read and checked before anything changes; one undo step.

fields.name: component
fields.description: A component's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: configuration
fields.description:
Source configuration row, by name or stable id. Omitted preserves the selection for
the same source file; a different file follows its saved state. Null clears the selection.

fields.name: occurrence
fields.description:
One of its placements, by id. When the component has other placements, only this one
comes to show the design, as a placement of the component already linked to it or of a
new one under the same parent, keeping its position, grounding and joints.

fields.name: path
fields.description: The saved design to link instead, `.sc` or `.json`.

component.relink.reason: reads or writes a file outside the design: needs a file picker

component.rename.label: Rename Component
component.rename.description: Rename a component, or the design itself (id 0). Placements still named after it follow.

fields.name: component
fields.description: A component's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Text with something in it; once surrounding blanks are cut, at most 128 bytes.

component.replace_with_link.label: Replace with Link
component.replace_with_link.help: component or components: [ids or names] of components that are not linked; with: a linked component, or path: a .sc design (its link here, else a new linked component) → each component's history goes and its placements become placements of the linked component; refused when its bodies are not the same as the link's; returns component, name, replaced and warnings
component.replace_with_link.description:
Make components that are not linked, and build the same bodies as a linked component, more
placements of it: each one's history goes and its placements become placements of the linked
component. One is refused when its bodies are not the same as the link's. One undo step.

fields.name: component
fields.description: A component's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: components
fields.description: Components, each by id or name; only the first 1000 are used.

fields.name: path
fields.description:
Without `with`: a design file (`.sc`). The component linked to it here, or else a new
linked component.

fields.name: with
fields.description: A component's id (a number) or its name.

component.replace_with_link.reason: reads or writes a file outside the design: needs a file picker

component.revert_position.label: Revert Position
component.revert_position.help: occurrences?: [ids] (default all); drops selected pending occurrence moves; with no occurrences the joints also go back to the values Capture Position saved (clamped to limits) → reverted, joints
component.revert_position.description:
Drop pending occurrence moves, putting the occurrences back where they were captured. Without
`occurrences`, the joints also go back to the values Capture Position saved, clamped to their
limits. One undo step, not a history step.

fields.name: occurrences
fields.description: 1 to 10000 occurrence ids.

component.show_history.label: Show Component History
component.show_history.help: component: id or name; puts a component's features back in the History bar after Hide Component History (#10393)
component.show_history.description:
Keep a component's features in the design but out of the History bar (`component.hide_history`),
or put them back (`component.show_history`). A component inside one that is hidden is left out of
the bar too; the design itself never is, and its features always show.

fields.name: component
fields.description: A component's id (a number) or its name.

component.unlock.label: Unlock Contents
component.unlock.help: component: removes the rigid joints that hold its contents together (an imported assembly's rigid group), so its parts move and take joints one by one → joints (the ids removed)
component.unlock.description:
Remove the rigid joints that hold a component's contents together (an imported assembly's
rigid group), so its parts move and take joints one by one. Refused for the design and when
nothing holds the contents together.

fields.name: component
fields.description: A component's id (a number) or its name.

component.update_links.label: Update Links
component.update_links.help: component?: id or name (default: every linked component); components?: a list of ids or names, which goes on past a design it cannot read (that one keeps its bodies, is named in failed and gets a warning) — reads the linked designs again and replaces their bodies where they changed, as one undo step; → updated, unchanged, failed ([{component, name, error}]), warnings (also joints whose faces are gone or that no longer solve)
component.update_links.description:
Read the linked designs again and replace the bodies of the components whose file changed,
as one undo step. Without `component` or `components`, every linked component is read. A
component that is not linked is refused.

fields.name: component
fields.description: A component's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: components
fields.description: Components, each by id or name.

component.update_links.reason: not in the live demo: it needs Mechvane's own handling on the server (install Mechvane to use it)

config.activate.label: Activate Configuration
config.activate.help: row: a row's name, or its id from config.table — sets its parameter values and suppressions
config.activate.description:
Switch to a configuration row: its parameter values, suppressions, materials and appearances
are set, and its rules run. Refused, with nothing changed, when a feature that builds now
would fail in it.

fields.name: row
fields.description: A configuration row: its name, or its id as `config.table` lists it.

config.column.label: Configuration Column
config.column.help: param? | feature? | material? | appearance? (target name); delete?: bool
config.column.description:
Add a column to the configuration table, or delete one: give exactly one of `param`,
`feature`, `material`, `appearance`, `component_appearance` and `face_appearance`. An added
column is filled in every row with the design's current value; the rows are checked against
the table's rules afterwards. One undo step.

fields.name: appearance
fields.description: A body, by name: its look in each row.

fields.name: component_appearance
fields.description: A component's name or id, or an occurrence's name (its component).

fields.name: delete
fields.description: Delete the column instead of adding it. Default: false.

fields.name: face_appearance
fields.description: A face, whose look each row sets; to delete its column (with `delete`), the column's key as `config.table` lists it.

fields.name: feature
fields.description: A feature, by name: whether each row suppresses it.

fields.name: material
fields.description: A body, by name: its material in each row.

fields.name: param
fields.description: A parameter, by name: its value in each row.

config.configure.label: Configure
config.configure.help: params?: [parameter names]; features?: [feature names]; materials?: [body names]; appearances?: [body names] (columns to add; with no rows yet, a "Default" row takes the current values)
config.configure.description:
Add columns to the configuration table: parameters, feature suppressions, and bodies' and
components' materials and looks, each filled in every row with the design's current value. A
column the table has is left as it is. With no rows yet, a "Default" row takes the current
values and becomes the active row. One undo step.

fields.name: appearances
fields.description: Bodies whose look to configure, by name.

fields.name: component_appearances
fields.description:
Components whose look to configure: each a component's name or id, or an occurrence's name
(its component). At most 500.

fields.name: face_appearances
fields.description:
Faces whose look to configure, each picked as `face_appearance` is for `config.column`
(not by a column key). At most 500.

fields.name: features
fields.description: Features whose suppression to configure, by name.

fields.name: materials
fields.description: Bodies whose material to configure, by name.

fields.name: params
fields.description: Parameters to configure, by name, as `parameters.list` gives them.

config.preview.label: Preview Configuration
config.preview.help: row: a row's name, or its id from config.table — validates a rebuild without changing the design or history
config.preview.description:
Switch to a configuration row: its parameter values, suppressions, materials and appearances
are set, and its rules run. Refused, with nothing changed, when a feature that builds now
would fail in it.

fields.name: row
fields.description: A configuration row: its name, or its id as `config.table` lists it.

config.row.label: Configuration Row
config.row.help: name (a row's name, or its id from config.table); from? (row to copy, by name or id; default current values); values?: {column key: expression, suppression, material name, appearance name or Look object}; rename?; delete?: bool
config.row.description:
Add a row to the configuration table, change one, rename it or delete it. A new row starts
from `from`'s cells, or the design's current values; `values` then sets cells. Rows are checked
against the table's rules, and a parameter value against the parameters it drives, before
anything changes. The design keeps its active row's values until a row is activated. One undo
step.

fields.name: delete
fields.description:
Delete the row instead; `from`, `values` and `rename` are then not used. The last row can't
be deleted while the table has rules. Default: false.

fields.name: from
fields.description:
A row to copy the cells of, by name or id. Default: the row's own cells, or the design's
current values for a new row.

fields.name: name
fields.description:
The row, by name (1 to 128 bytes once spaces at either end are dropped) or by id. A name the
table doesn't have adds a row (at most 2000); an id must be one of its rows.

fields.name: rename
fields.description:
A new name for the row, which must exist: 1 to 128 bytes once spaces at either end are
dropped, not another row's.

fields.name: values
fields.description: Cells to set, by column key as `config.table` lists it (`param:W`, `suppress:Block`, `material:Body1`…), or by a parameter's or a suppressed feature's name. A cell is an expression for a parameter, true or false (suppressed) for a feature, a material's name for a material column, and a look's name or a look object for a look column; at most 4096 bytes. Each key must be a column the table has.

config.rule.label: Configuration Rule
config.rule.help: rule?: {id,name,enabled,condition,effect}; rules?: [rule…] (added or replaced together, then the rows checked once); id? + delete?; id? + index? (ordered move)
config.rule.description:
Add, replace, delete or move the configuration table's rules, which drive parameters and
suppressions from conditions, in the order they run. Give `rule`, `rules`, or `id` with
`delete` or `index`. Every row is then checked against the rules; if one fails, nothing
changes. One undo step.

fields.name: delete
fields.description: With `id`: delete the rule. Default: false (move it to `index`).

fields.name: id
fields.description: Without `rule` or `rules`: the rule to delete or move, by id.

fields.name: index
fields.description:
With `id` and without `delete`: where to move the rule, from 0 (it runs first); less than
the number of rules.

fields.name: rule
fields.description: A rule to add, or to replace the rule with its id.

fields.name: rules
fields.description:
Without `rule`: rules to add or replace together, the rows then checked once with all of
them in place (rules that only hold together can be added). At most 2048.

config.rules.label: Configuration Rules
config.rules.help: ordered typed rules, rows and active state
config.rules.description:
The configuration table: its columns, rows and rules, the active row, and whether the design
still matches it. Read-only.

config.table.label: Display Configuration Table
config.table.help: → columns (param:<name> or suppress:<feature>), rows (each with its fixed id), the active row's name and whether the design still matches it
config.table.description:
The configuration table: its columns, rows and rules, the active row, and whether the design
still matches it. Read-only.

Only when the SOLIDCRAFT_CRASH_TEST environment variable is set

diagnostics.profile.help: enabled?: bool (start or stop recording); reset?: bool (forget what was recorded); top?: rows (default 20, 0: all); trace?: path (write the recorded spans as a Chrome trace-event file, for chrome://tracing or Perfetto). Returns what was recorded before enabled and reset apply: {compiled, enabled, wall_ms, spans, dropped, by_category: [{category, self_ms, share}], rows: [{category, name, count, total_ms, self_ms, max_ms}], rows_total, trace?}, the rows the most self time first. Categories: solidcore (the kernel's calls), kernel, feature (one per feature computed, by its type), doc, command, import (STEP/IGES stages), io. Self time is a span's time less the spans inside it; total counts its outermost run only. Recording also starts with SOLIDCRAFT_PROFILE=1, the CLI's --profile and the app's preference; off, it costs nothing measurable. Read-only
