diagnostics.report_issue.label: Report an Issue
diagnostics.report_issue.help: title: string; description?: string; type?: bug | feature | question; app?: slug (default solidcraft); system?, repro?, log?, screenshot?: bool (default true); design?, crash?: bool (default false). Files a problem report on tickets.solidcraft.io for the person: the app gathers what the report dialog would, sends it as a draft and opens it in their browser to review and file. Ask the person first. design and crash are never sent on an agent's word: asking for them shows the report dialog for the person to tick them. Returns {report, status, message?, url?, ticket?, dropped?}; follow it with diagnostics.report_issue_status. Needs the SolidCraft app (not headless)
diagnostics.report_issue.description:
File a problem report on tickets.solidcraft.io for the person using SolidCraft, as the report
dialog would: the app gathers system info, the failed operation, the log and a screenshot,
sends them as a draft and opens it in the person's browser to review and file. Ask the person
first. Their design and crash dumps are never sent on an agent's word: asking for them shows
the report dialog for the person to tick them.

fields.name: app
fields.description: The app the ticket is for, by slug. Default: solidcraft.

fields.name: crash
fields.description: Ask to attach the latest crash report. Default: false. Only the person can agree to it.

fields.description: What happened and what was expected (Markdown).

fields.name: design
fields.description:
Ask to attach the design file. Default: false. Only the person can agree to it, in the
report dialog.

fields.name: log
fields.description: Attach the last lines of the log. Default: true.

fields.name: repro
fields.description: Attach the failed operation's details (the command, its parameters and error). Default: true.

fields.name: screenshot
fields.description: Attach a screenshot of the window. Default: true.

fields.name: system
fields.description: Attach system info (version, commit, OS, GPU). Default: true.

fields.name: title
fields.description: A short title for the problem.

fields.name: type
fields.description: bug (default), feature or question.

diagnostics.report_issue.reason: crash reports, issue reports to SolidCraft's servers, kernel switches

doc.open.label: Open
doc.open.help: path: .sc design (or a .solidcraft design from an earlier release), .dxf/.svg drawing (opens as a new, unsaved design with an XY sketch, using sketch.insert_dxf/sketch.insert_svg units and defaults), or a .step/.stp/.igs/.fcstd/.3dm/.3mf/.stl/.obj/.glb/.gltf/.kicad_pro/.kicad_pcb file (STEP, IGES, FreeCAD, Rhino, 3MF, STL, OBJ, glTF or KiCad PCB; opens as a new design holding the file as a component named after it, as file.insert_step and file.insert_mesh make), or a .ply/.xyz/.pts point cloud (opens as a new design holding it, as pointcloud.insert makes; its `units` and `max_points` as there); up?: z|y for a STEP, IGES, FreeCAD, Rhino or glTF file (see file.insert_step and file.insert_mesh); names?: auto|solid|product|instance for a STEP, IGES, FreeCAD or Rhino file (see file.insert_step); units?: for an STL or OBJ file (see file.insert_mesh); origin?: bool for a mesh file (see file.insert_mesh); folder?: bool for a STEP, IGES, FreeCAD or Rhino file (see file.insert_step); reuse_import?: bool (STEP/IGES: reuse an unchanged import from the local saved-model cache, default true; false recomputes without reading or writing the cache; → import_reused: bool, content_sha256: exact source digest); history?: features|solids for a FreeCAD file (see file.insert_step); for a KiCad PCB: thickness?: board thickness in mm (default from the board); components?: bool (default true); copper?: "overlay" (default: flat copper just above the board), "none" (leave the traces out) or "mesh" (modelled with thickness; true also means mesh; pads are included whenever copper is enabled); silkscreen?: bool (default true: the silk shapes and text); color?: "#rrggbb" or [r, g, b] (board substrate colour); representation?: mesh|brep (the board itself; default brep: a solid whose faces can be picked); read_only?: bool (a design: saving to its own file is refused, file.save_as keeps the changes elsewhere); verify?: bool (default false: a design's signature is checked and reported, `signature`) → open_elsewhere: {host, user, app, opened} when another SolidCraft has the design open (its lock file is fresh); newer_file: {format, reads_up_to, unknown_changes, not_understood, notice} and warnings when a newer SolidCraft saved it: it opens all the same, and what this version can't read is named there and kept by saving
doc.open.description:
Open a file as the design: a SolidCraft design (`.sc`, or a `.solidcraft` design from an
earlier release), a `.dxf` or `.svg` drawing (a new, unsaved design with an XY sketch, with
the units and defaults of `sketch.insert_dxf` and `sketch.insert_svg`), a STEP, IGES,
FreeCAD, Rhino, 3MF, STL, OBJ or glTF file (a new design holding the file as a component
named after it, as `file.insert_step` and `file.insert_mesh` make), or a `.ply`, `.xyz` or
`.pts` point cloud (a new design holding it, as `pointcloud.insert` makes). The open design
is replaced.

fields.name: folder
fields.description:
For a STEP, IGES, FreeCAD or Rhino file (ignored for other files): true puts an import that
brings more than one item into the history (its Import feature and the rigid joints holding
its parts) into a new history folder named `Group #N`. Default: false.

fields.name: history
fields.description:
For a FreeCAD file only (ignored for other files): its sketches and features rebuilt as
SolidCraft features, or only its solids as one Import feature. Default: features.

fields.name: max_points
fields.description:
For a point cloud file only (ignored for other files): the most points kept. Default:
5000000.

fields.name: names
fields.description:
For a STEP, IGES, FreeCAD or Rhino file only (refused for any other): what the bodies are
named after. Default: auto.

fields.name: origin
fields.description:
For a 3MF, STL, OBJ or glTF file only (refused for any other): true moves the mesh so its
box is centred on X and Y with its base on Z = 0. Default: false.

fields.name: path
fields.description: A file path: text with a character that is not white space, under 4096 bytes long (the schema's maxLength counts characters).

fields.name: read_only
fields.description:
For a design: saving to its own file is refused (`file.save_as` keeps the changes
elsewhere). Default: false.

fields.name: reuse_import
fields.description:
For a STEP or IGES file: false recomputes the import without reading or writing the local
saved-model cache. Default: true.

fields.name: units
fields.description:
For a point cloud, STL, OBJ or PLY file: the unit its coordinates are in, scaled to
millimetres as it is read (refused for a 3MF or glTF file, which states its own; ignored
for other files). Default: mm.

fields.name: up
fields.description:
For a STEP, IGES, FreeCAD, Rhino or glTF file only (refused for any other): which way is up
in the file. Default: z for STEP, IGES, FreeCAD and Rhino, y for glTF.

fields.name: verify

design opens without spending the time a full verification takes.

document.inspect.help: measure?: bool (include body measurements); sketch_counts?: bool (each sketch also gives its plane and its number of points and constraints); timeline?: true (default) | "summary" (each feature as id, name, type, with error, warning, suppressed and rolled_back only when set) | false (left out); bodies?: true (default) | "names" (only the body names, nothing measured) | false (left out)
document.inspect.description:
Read the design: its name, units, properties, parameters, timeline, bodies and sketches, the
selection and the undo and redo depth. Read-only.

fields.description:

names, nothing measured; false leaves `bodies` out.

timing; `"summary"` each as its id, name and type, with `error`, `warning`, `suppressed`

`timeline` out.

file.save.label: Save
file.save.help: path? (default: current file; a name that opens as another kind of file, such as .step, .stl or .dxf, is refused: file.export writes those); format?: container|json (default: json for .json, otherwise container); compression?: fast|compact (default: fast); cache?: bool (the evaluated model, so the design opens without rebuilding; default: true); preview?: bool (saved display meshes, default: false); overwrite?: bool (replace the design's file even though another program or computer changed it since it was opened or saved; without it that save is refused); sign?: bool (the app's own Save only: sign the save with GnuPG, appending a provenance record; container only; a script or agent is refused); signing_key?: fingerprint or user id (default: GnuPG's default signing key) → signature: {method, fingerprint, user_id?} when signed
file.save.description:
Write the design to a file and make that file the design's own: the next `file.save` writes
it again. With no `path`, the design's current file is written; a design that has none yet
needs a `path`. A name that opens as another kind of file (`.step`, `.stl`, `.dxf` and the
like) is refused: `file.export` writes those. Not an undo step.

fields.name: cache
fields.description:
Keep the evaluated model in the file, so the design opens without rebuilding. Default:
true. Plain json has no room for it.

fields.name: compression
fields.description: fast or compact. Default: fast. The handler refuses any other word.

fields.name: format
fields.description:
container (`.sc`) or json. Default: json for a path ending in `.json`, otherwise
container. The handler refuses any other word.

fields.name: overwrite
fields.description:
Replace the design's file even though another program or computer changed it since it was
opened or saved; without it that save is refused. Only matters when the path is the
design's own file. Default: false.

fields.name: path
fields.description:
The design file to write. Default: the design's current file. A blank value counts as
left out.

fields.name: preview
fields.description: Keep the display meshes in the file. Default: false.

fields.name: sign
fields.description:
Sign the saved design with GnuPG, appending one record to its provenance. Default: false.
Accepted only from the app's own Save (the user chose the key); a script or agent is
refused.

fields.name: signing_key
fields.description:
The GnuPG key to sign with: a fingerprint or user id. Default, or a blank value: GnuPG's
default signing key.

file.save.reason: reads or writes a path, sends to a slicer or uploads: needs a file picker

file.save_as.label: Save As
file.save_as.help: path (a design file name, .sc as a rule; one that opens as another kind of file, such as .step, .stl or .dxf, is refused: file.export writes those); format?: container|json (default: json for .json, otherwise container); compression?: fast|compact (default: fast); cache?: bool (the evaluated model, so the design opens without rebuilding; default: true); preview?: bool (saved display meshes, default: false); overwrite?: bool (as file.save, when `path` is the design's own file); sign?: bool and signing_key? (as file.save, and likewise only from the app's own Save)
file.save_as.description:
Write the design to a new file (a design file name, `.sc` as a rule) and make that file the
design's own. A name that opens as another kind of file (`.step`, `.stl`, `.dxf` and the like)
is refused: `file.export` writes those. A design with no name of its own, or one borrowed from
the file it was saved as before, takes the new file's name. Not an undo step.

fields.name: cache
fields.description:
Keep the evaluated model in the file, so the design opens without rebuilding. Default:
true. Plain json has no room for it.

fields.name: compression
fields.description: fast or compact. Default: fast. The handler refuses any other word.

fields.name: format
fields.description:
container (`.sc`) or json. Default: json for a path ending in `.json`, otherwise
container. The handler refuses any other word.

fields.name: overwrite
fields.description:
As for `file.save`, when `path` is the design's own file: replace it even though another
program or computer changed it. Default: false.

fields.name: path
fields.description: The design file to write: text, not blank, under 4096 bytes.

fields.name: preview
fields.description: Keep the display meshes in the file. Default: false.

fields.name: sign
fields.description:
Sign the saved design with GnuPG, appending one record to its provenance. Default: false.
Accepted only from the app's own Save (the user chose the key); a script or agent is
refused.

fields.name: signing_key
fields.description:
The GnuPG key to sign with: a fingerprint or user id. Default, or a blank value: GnuPG's
default signing key.

file.save_as.reason: reads or writes a path, sends to a slicer or uploads: needs a file picker

file.save_mesh.label: Save As Mesh
file.save_mesh.help: path; format?: stl|3mf|3mf-tagged (default from the extension, else stl; 3mf-tagged: docs/formats/3mf-face-tags.md); bodies?: [names] (default: all); ascii?: bool (STL); slicer?: id or name from file.slicers, the program path it lists, or a program the user added under Custom… (send the saved file there, through the same steps as file.send_to_slicer: a slicer that has to be started first is waited for; may be deprecated later in favour of file.send_to_slicer or a Send to App workflow, kept for scripts); single_instance?: bool (default true; see file.send_to_slicer); quality?: standard|fine|finest (STL, OBJ and 3MF: how closely the mesh follows curved faces, a chord tolerance of 2e-4, 5e-5 or 1e-5 of each body's size; default standard); objects?: body|component (3MF only: one object per body, the default, or one object for each placed component with two or more bodies, with those bodies as its parts, so a slicer loads them as one object with parts); lay_on_print_faces?: bool (default false: each body with a print face (body.print_face) is saved laid on it; a file sent to `slicer` is laid on them whatever this says)
file.save_mesh.description: Save bodies as a mesh file: binary or ASCII STL, 3MF, or 3MF with a face tag on each triangle. The format is `format`, else the extension of `path`, else STL. With `slicer`, the saved file is then sent to that program. Nothing is added to undo.

fields.name: ascii
fields.description:
STL only (read only when `format` is `stl`): true writes ASCII STL instead of binary.
Default: false.

fields.name: bodies
fields.description: The bodies to save, by name. Default: every body.

fields.name: format
fields.description:
The file format, in any case: `stl`, `3mf`, or `3mf-tagged` (3MF with a face tag on each
triangle, docs/formats/3mf-face-tags.md). Default: from the extension of `path` (`.3mf`
gives 3mf), else stl.

fields.name: lay_on_print_faces
fields.description:
True saves each body with a print face (`body.print_face`) laid on it, as a slicer export
lays it: turned so the face points down at Z = 0, its centre of mass over the origin. Each
body is laid on its own, so several land on the origin together; a part of a 3MF object
(`objects: component`) stays as it lies. A file sent to `slicer` is laid on them whatever
this says. Default: false.

fields.name: objects
fields.description:
3MF only: `body` is one object per body; `component` is one object for each placed
component with two or more bodies, with those bodies as its parts, so a slicer loads them as
one object with parts (other bodies stay objects of their own). `component` is refused for
other formats. Default: body.

fields.name: path
fields.description: The file to write: not blank, fewer than 4096 UTF-8 bytes.

fields.name: quality
fields.description:
How closely the mesh follows curved faces (STL, OBJ and 3MF), in any case: `standard`, `fine`
or `finest`, a chord tolerance of 2e-4, 5e-5 or 1e-5 of each body's size. Default: standard.

fields.name: single_instance
fields.description:
Read only when `slicer` is given: true opens the file in the window the slicer already has
open, for slicers that load files that way (see `file.send_to_slicer`). Default: true.

fields.name: slicer
fields.description:
A slicer to send the saved file to, after it is written where `path` says, through the
same steps as `file.send_to_slicer`: an id or a name from `file.slicers`, the program path
it lists, or a program the user added under Custom…. A slicer that has to be started first
is waited for. Kept for scripts; may be deprecated later in favour of `file.send_to_slicer`
or a Send to App workflow. Default: none.

file.save_mesh.reason: not in the live demo: it needs Mechvane's own handling on the server (install Mechvane to use it)

file.send_to_slicer.label: Send to Slicer
file.send_to_slicer.help: slicer: id or name from file.slicers, or a program the user added under Custom…; bodies?: [names] (default: the selected bodies); wait?: block|return|no (default block: a slicer that drops a file at a cold start is started alone and the call waits up to 10 s for it to be ready, then sends; return: start it and answer {starting}; no: send now); single_instance?: bool (default true: PrusaSlicer, SuperSlicer and Cura load the file in the window that is open); format?: 3mf|stl|3mf-tagged (default 3mf, in millimetres; STL if that can't be written) → saves the bodies in this user's slicer folder and opens the file in the slicer. The file name stays the same for the same design and bodies, so sending again replaces it (use the slicer's Reload from disk)

fields.description: slicer: id or name from file.slicers, or a program the user added under Custom…; bodies?: [names] (default: the selected bodies); wait?: block|return|no (default block: a slicer that drops a file at a cold start is started alone and the call waits up to 10 s for it to be ready, then sends; return: start it and answer {starting}; no: send now); single_instance?: bool (default true: PrusaSlicer, SuperSlicer and Cura load the file in the window that is open); format?: 3mf|stl|3mf-tagged (default 3mf, in millimetres; STL if that can't be written) → saves the bodies in this user's slicer folder and opens the file in the slicer. The file name stays the same for the same design and bodies, so sending again replaces it (use the slicer's Reload from disk)

file.send_to_slicer.reason: reads or writes a path, sends to a slicer or uploads: needs a file picker

file.slicers.label: Installed Slicers
file.slicers.help: → the slicers found on this machine: [{id, name, program, icon?}]; pass an id, a name or the program path as file.send_to_slicer's or file.save_mesh's `slicer`
file.slicers.reason: reads or writes a path, sends to a slicer or uploads: needs a file picker

file.verify.label: Verify Signature
file.verify.help: path? (default: the design's current file) → {path, status, reason?, truncated, records: [{method, key_id, user_id?, author?, created?, format, covered}]}: status is unsigned, valid, not_covered (signed earlier, saved since without a key), invalid or unsupported

fields.name: path
fields.description: The design file to verify. Default: the design's current file.

file.verify.reason: reads or writes a path, sends to a slicer or uploads: needs a file picker

frame.end_cap.label: End Cap
frame.end_cap.help: faces: [{face:[x,y,z],body,index,path?}] planar end faces of frame members, picked in world mm (1–256); thickness: length in design units or a parameter expression; offset?: inset of the plate from the outside of the profile, a length; ratio?: the inset as a share of the thickness (give offset or ratio, not both; neither: the plate is flush with the outside of the profile); chamfer?: corner chamfer length along each edge from the corner (default 0; a rounded corner needs at least its rounding); direction?: outward|inward (default outward: past the end; inward: the member is cut back by the thickness and the cap takes its place). One separate body per face, named `<member> End Cap`; the plate is the profile's outer outline on a closed section (tube, pipe, bar), its outside on an open one (angle, channel, beam, slotted extrusion): the edges on the rectangle round the profile with their rounds and chamfers, inward stretches closed along the rectangle. Common name/body_names fields supported.
frame.end_cap.description:
The keys `features::add_feature` reads for every feature command, whatever else it takes:
the feature's name, the new bodies' names and the bodies taking part. A feature command's
parameters include it with

```ignore
#[serde(flatten, deserialize_with = "feature_common")]
pub common: FeatureCommon,
```

Two keys `add_feature` also reads aren't here. `targets` it reads only for primitives; the
other commands that read it are the ones that combine bodies. `operation` it reads for every
feature (a cut where the active component has no bodies takes part in all of them), but only
the commands that combine bodies take one; those declare it with their own type
([`OperationParam`] or [`ExtrudeOperation`]), and for the rest it is a caller's mistake.

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: chamfer
fields.description: The corner chamfer, along each edge from the corner (default 0: sharp corners).

fields.name: faces
fields.description: The open end faces to close, each a planar end of a frame member.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: offset
fields.description: The inset from the profile's outer edge as a length (give this or `ratio`).

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

fields.name: ratio
fields.description:
The inset as a share of the thickness (give this or `offset`; neither: flush with the
outside of the profile).

fields.name: thickness
fields.description: A length: a number in the design's length unit, or an expression such as "w / 2" or "30 mm".

frame.member.label: Frame Member
frame.member.help: sketch: the frame sketch (id or name; 2D or 3D); lines?: [curve ids] (one member each; default: every straight line drawn in the sketch: not construction, not projected or otherwise linked, not of no length); profile: {kind: bar|round_bar|rect_tube|round_tube|angle|channel|i_beam, …its dimensions: each a number in the design's units or a length expression over its parameters ("tube_wall", "2 in"); a channel's flange_slope is an angle (a number of degrees)} (frame.profile.list gives each kind's dimensions and an example; dimensions left out take defaults from the profile's size) | {size: a standard steel size by name, such as "RSC 203x89", "PFC 200x90x30", "RSA 50x50x5", "SHS 100x100x5", "RHS 200x100x6.3" or "CHS 42.4x3.2" (frame.profile.list lists them), alone: it brings its dimensions} | profile_sketch: a sketch whose profile is the section, in its own x and y around its origin, with profiles?: picks as solid.extrude takes them (default: its material, nested loops alternating, so two circles make a tube); anchor?: origin|center|centroid|top_left|top|top_right|left|right|bottom_left|bottom|bottom_right (the profile point that sits on each line, default origin); locate?: [x,y] (the profile point that sits on each line, in mm from the profile's own origin: a bar's or an angle's bottom-left corner, a channel's web back at mid-height, the centre of other profiles; takes precedence over `anchor` and keeps the member attached at that point when the profile size changes); angle?: angle expr (the profile turned about the line; default 0: its y as near world up as the line allows, a vertical member's x along world X); mirror?: bool (the profile mirrored across its y axis); name?; body_name? (what the members are named after, then numbered: `Rail`, `Rail (2)`…; default the size's name, `RSC 203x89`, the profile's description, `Rect Tube 40x40x3`, or the profile sketch's name); names?: {line id: name} (names to keep, as Edit Feature keeps them). One body per line, from its start to its end; each member keeps its name when other lines are added or deleted. Returns the feature and the bodies it made
frame.member.description:
Lay structural members along the lines of a frame sketch: one body per line, from its start
to its end, its cross-section square to the line. The section is a built-in `profile` or the
profiles of a `profile_sketch`, one of them. Each member keeps its name when other lines are
added or deleted. Returns the feature and the bodies it made.

fields.name: anchor
fields.description: The profile point that sits on each line. Default: origin.

fields.name: angle
fields.description:
How far the profile turns about the line, a number of degrees or an expression. Default:
0, which puts its y as near world up as the line allows (a vertical member's x along
world X).

fields.name: body_name
fields.description:
What the members are named after, then numbered: `Rail`, `Rail (2)`… Default: the
standard size's name (`RSC 203x89`), the profile's description (`Rect Tube 40x40x3`), or
the profile sketch's name.

fields.name: exact_regions
fields.description:
With `profile_sketch`: each index or point pick in `profiles` is exactly the region it
names, where it would otherwise take the whole drawn profile a face's projected outline
cuts into regions. Default: false. Not used with `profile`.

fields.name: lines
fields.description:
The lines to lay members along, by curve id, one member each. Default: every straight
line drawn in the sketch that isn't construction, projected or otherwise linked, or of no
length.

fields.name: locate
fields.description:
The profile point that sits on each line, [x, y] in mm from the profile's own origin (a
bar's or an angle's bottom-left corner, a channel's web back at mid-height, the centre of
other profiles). Takes precedence over `anchor`; the member stays attached at that point
when the profile's size changes.

fields.name: mirror
fields.description: The profile mirrored across its y axis, before it turns. Default: false.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: names
fields.description:
Names to keep, by line id, as Edit Feature keeps them. A line not listed gets a name from
`body_name`.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, which every feature records; each an existing body or `*`. Members
are new bodies, whatever this lists.

fields.name: profile
fields.description: A built-in profile: {"kind": bar | round_bar | rect_tube | round_tube | angle | channel | i_beam, …its dimensions}. Each dimension is a number in the design's units or a length expression over its parameters ("tube_wall", "2 in"); a channel's `flange_slope` is an angle, a number of degrees or an angle expression. `frame.profile.list` gives each kind's dimensions and an example. A dimension that is left out and isn't required takes a default worked out from the profile's size. Or a standard steel size by name, {"size": "RSC 203x89"}, alone: it brings its own dimensions (`frame.profile.list` lists the sizes).

fields.name: profile_sketch
fields.description: A sketch's feature id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: profiles
fields.description: Which sketch profiles to use: "all" (the default, any case), an index, or a list of indices, of {"point": [x, y]} inside a profile, or of curve selections (a list of curve ids, {"curves": [ids]} or {"loops": [...]}). Picks by index or point are stored by the curves around the profile.

fields.name: sketch
fields.description: A sketch's feature id (a number) or its name.

frame.profile.insert.label: Insert Profile
frame.profile.insert.help: profile: {kind: bar|round_bar|rect_tube|round_tube|angle|channel|i_beam, …its dimensions: each a number in the design's units or a length expression over its parameters ("tube_wall", "2 in"); a channel's flange_slope is an angle (a number of degrees)} (frame.profile.list gives each kind's dimensions and an example; dimensions left out take defaults from the profile's size) | {size: a standard steel size by name, such as "RSC 203x89", "PFC 200x90x30", "RSA 50x50x5", "SHS 100x100x5", "RHS 200x100x6.3" or "CHS 42.4x3.2" (frame.profile.list lists them), alone: it brings its dimensions}; at?: [x,y] (sketch mm, default the origin); anchor?: origin|center|centroid|top_left|top|top_right|left|right|bottom_left|bottom|bottom_right (the profile point placed on `at`: its origin, the default and a built-in profile's centre, its bounding box's centre, its centroid, or a corner or edge middle of its bounding box); angle?: radians, counter-clockwise; fixed?: bool (default true: the curves are locked, so solving the sketch keeps the shape); sketch?: id|name (default: the sketch being edited). Returns the section as frame.profile.properties does. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)
frame.profile.insert.description:
Draw a built-in profile into a sketch as lines and arcs, placed by its anchor and turned about
it. A tube's inside is drawn too, so the wall is one profile. One undo step.

fields.name: anchor
fields.description: The profile point that is placed on `at`. Default: origin.

fields.name: angle
fields.description:
How far the profile turns about the anchor, in radians counter-clockwise (not degrees).
Default: 0.

fields.name: at
fields.description: Where the anchor goes, in sketch mm. Default: the origin.

fields.name: fixed
fields.description: Lock the curves, so that solving the sketch keeps the shape. Default: true.

fields.name: profile
fields.description: A built-in profile: {"kind": bar | round_bar | rect_tube | round_tube | angle | channel | i_beam, …its dimensions}. Each dimension is a number in the design's units or a length expression over its parameters ("tube_wall", "2 in"); a channel's `flange_slope` is an angle, a number of degrees or an angle expression. `frame.profile.list` gives each kind's dimensions and an example. A dimension that is left out and isn't required takes a default worked out from the profile's size. Or a standard steel size by name, {"size": "RSC 203x89"}, alone: it brings its own dimensions (`frame.profile.list` lists the sizes).

fields.name: sketch
fields.description: The sketch to draw in, by id or name. Default: the sketch being edited.

frame.profile.list.label: Profile Library
frame.profile.list.help: family?: RSC|PFC|RSA|SHS|RHS|CHS (list only that family's sizes). Returns kinds: [{kind, label, required, optional, example}]: the built-in profiles, each SolidCraft's own parametric definition; and sizes: [{family, kind, standard, source, names, additional?}]: the standard steel sizes by name, each family with the published table its dimensions come from (frame.profile.properties with {profile: {size}} gives a size's dimensions and section)
frame.profile.list.description: List the built-in profiles and the standard steel sizes.

fields.name: family
fields.description: List only this family's sizes. Default: every family.

frame.profile.properties.label: Profile Properties
frame.profile.properties.help: profile: {kind: bar|round_bar|rect_tube|round_tube|angle|channel|i_beam, …its dimensions: each a number in the design's units or a length expression over its parameters ("tube_wall", "2 in"); a channel's flange_slope is an angle (a number of degrees)} (frame.profile.list gives each kind's dimensions and an example; dimensions left out take defaults from the profile's size) | {size: a standard steel size by name, such as "RSC 203x89", "PFC 200x90x30", "RSA 50x50x5", "SHS 100x100x5", "RHS 200x100x6.3" or "CHS 42.4x3.2" (frame.profile.list lists them), alone: it brings its dimensions}; density?: kg/m³ (adds mass_per_m, kg/m). Returns profile (every default filled in), area (mm²), centroid [x,y] (mm, from the bounding box centre), ixx, iyy, ixy (mm⁴ about the centroid), width, height
frame.profile.properties.description:
Work out a built-in profile's section: its area, centroid and second moments, about axes
through the centroid, parallel to the profile's x and y.

fields.name: density
fields.description: The material's density, which adds `mass_per_m`. Default: none, and no `mass_per_m`.

fields.name: profile
fields.description: A built-in profile: {"kind": bar | round_bar | rect_tube | round_tube | angle | channel | i_beam, …its dimensions}. Each dimension is a number in the design's units or a length expression over its parameters ("tube_wall", "2 in"); a channel's `flange_slope` is an angle, a number of degrees or an angle expression. `frame.profile.list` gives each kind's dimensions and an example. A dimension that is left out and isn't required takes a default worked out from the profile's size. Or a standard steel size by name, {"size": "RSC 203x89"}, alone: it brings its own dimensions (`frame.profile.list` lists the sizes).

inspect.accessibility.label: Accessibility Analysis
inspect.accessibility.help: direction?: [x,y,z] the tool comes from (default Z, from above); clear?: true turns the analysis off

fields.name: direction
fields.description: An axis: X, Y or Z (any case), or a direction [x, y, z] that isn't zero.

inspect.analysis.label: View Analysis
inspect.analysis.help: off?: true turns the view analysis on now off. → active: the command id of the view analysis on (inspect.zebra, inspect.draft, inspect.curvature_map, inspect.environment_map, inspect.accessibility, inspect.continuity, inspect.isocurve or inspect.curvature_comb), or null. One is on at a time: turning one on turns the one on before off. Read-only without `off`
inspect.analysis.description:
Say which view analysis is on (zebra, draft, curvature map, environment map, accessibility,
continuity, isocurves or curvature combs: one at a time), or turn it off.

fields.name: off
fields.description: Turn the view analysis on now off.

inspect.center_of_mass.label: Center of Mass
inspect.center_of_mass.help: bodies?: [names] (default all): the centre of mass (uniform density) of each and of all together, from the exact mass properties `inspect.measure` takes → center, volume, bodies: [{body, center, volume}], skipped: [{body, reason}] (bodies that enclose no volume or could not be measured)
inspect.center_of_mass.description:
The centre of mass of bodies, at uniform density, each and all together, where the bodies
are placed in the assembly.

fields.name: bodies
fields.description: The bodies, by name (default: all). A body whose volume can't be measured is left out.

inspect.clearance.label: Clearance
inspect.clearance.help: bodies?: [names] (default: every solid body, in world placement, but those in `against`; mesh bodies are not measured); against?: [names] (only pairs with one body in `bodies` and the other here); min_volume?: mm³ (default 0.01: smaller overlaps count as contact); clearance?: mm (default 0: report pairs closer than this); nearest?: n (each body of `bodies` gets its n nearest others); skip_within?: "occurrence" (pairs of bodies of one occurrence) | "component" (pairs of bodies inside one placed component, its subcomponents included) | null; tolerance?: mm (default 1e-6: a gap below it is contact, 0) → overlaps: [{a, b, volume_mm3, area_mm2, bbox, center}]; near: [{a, b, distance_mm, from, to, overlap_mm3?: a contact's shared volume below min_volume, exact?: false when measured on the meshes}], nearest by body (the same for pairs that overlap: 0); nearest: {body: [{body, distance_mm}]}; unchecked: [{a, b, reason}] (pairs whose overlap could not be worked out; each mesh body, STL/3MF/OBJ import, is not measured and is listed as {a: name, b: null, reason: "mesh body: not checked"}, also when named in `bodies` or `against`; the result's `bodies` counts the solid bodies only); pairs_checked; pairs_reused (of those, measured by an earlier call: neither body changed or moved since); pairs_pruned (ruled out by their boxes); ms. Distances are measured on the exact faces and edges, the meshes only rule pairs out
inspect.clearance.description:
Find the solid bodies that overlap, and those closer than `clearance`, in world placement.
Distances are measured on the exact faces and edges; the meshes only rule pairs out. Mesh
bodies aren't measured: each is listed in `unchecked`.

fields.name: against
fields.description: Only pairs with one body in `bodies` and the other here.

fields.name: bodies
fields.description: The bodies to check (default: every solid body but those in `against`).

fields.name: clearance
fields.description: Report pairs closer than this, in mm: 0 to 1 000 000 (default 0).

fields.name: min_volume
fields.description: Smaller overlaps count as contact, in mm³ (default 0.01).

fields.name: nearest
fields.description:
Each body of `bodies` gets its this many nearest others, 0 to 1000 (default 0); a
fraction is rounded down.

fields.name: skip_within
fields.description: Pairs not to check: of bodies of one occurrence (`occurrence`), or inside one placed component, its subcomponents included (`component`). null checks every pair.

fields.name: tolerance
fields.description: A gap below this is contact, 0, in mm: 0 to 1 (default 1e-6).

inspect.colored_components.label: Component Colors
inspect.colored_components.help: enabled?: bool (omitted: toggle); temporary component colours, without changing appearances
inspect.colored_components.description:
Show or hide the temporary component colours (`inspect.colored_components`): the one flag
the command reads, as its handler reads it (`cmd/inspect.rs`'s `colored_components`).

fields.name: enabled
fields.description: True shows the colours, false hides them; left out, the command toggles them.

inspect.compare.label: Compare Bodies
inspect.compare.help: a, b: body names (default: the two selected bodies, or the design's only two), in world placement; tolerance?: mm (0.001 to 10, default 0.01): surfaces closer than this agree; spacing?: mm (default 0.5): the largest piece of a face sampled as one point, coarser for a body that would need more than max_points? (default 8 million, up to 50 million) samples; max_regions? (default 50); color?: true | {only_in_a?, only_in_b?: "#rrggbb"} (colours the faces that hold a region, red where only a has material and green where only b has: the faces mostly beyond the tolerance, else the one with the largest share; an undo step) → a, b: volume_mm3, area_mm2, center_of_mass, bbox; difference: b − a; deviation: a_to_b, b_to_a (max_mm, mean_mm, at, area_beyond_mm2); regions, largest first: side (only_in_a | only_in_b), volume_mm3, center and bbox (measured_by: "boolean": exact, the pieces of a − b or b − a there, measured as inspect.measure does; "not measured": the cut could not be made, so volume_mm3 and center are null and not_measured says why, never an estimate), area_mm2, max_deviation_mm, at, faces_a, faces_b (face indices, as model.faces lists them); identical; verdict; warnings (a body whose surface does not enclose what it measures, lines left out, a cut that could not be made). The regions are found from the two surfaces, so near-identical bodies compare too
inspect.compare.description:
Compare two bodies laid over each other, in world placement: measure both, sample each
surface's distance to the other, and find, measure and (with `color`) colour the places where
only one of them has material. It works from the two surfaces, without a boolean of the
bodies, so near-identical bodies compare too.

fields.name: a
fields.description:
The first body, by name. Give both `a` and `b`, or neither: then the two selected bodies,
or the design's only two.

fields.name: b
fields.description: The second body, by name.

fields.name: max_points
fields.description: The most samples per body: 10 000 to 50 million (default 8 million).

fields.name: max_regions
fields.description: The most regions measured: 1 to 1000 (default 50); more are counted in `unlisted_regions`.

fields.name: spacing
fields.description:
The largest piece of a face sampled as one point, in mm: 0.01 to 1000 (default 0.5),
coarser for a body that would need more than `max_points` samples.

fields.name: tolerance
fields.description: Surfaces closer than this agree, in mm: 0.001 to 10 (default 0.01).

inspect.compare_picture.label: Compare Picture
inspect.compare_picture.help: reference: path to a PNG or JPEG the model should match; view?/camera?/bodies?/rows? as inspect.silhouette; crop_px?: [x, y, w, h] in pixels, or crop_fraction?: [x, y, w, h] as fractions 0..1 of the picture (to take one view off a board); part_fills_crop?: false — with true the crop box is the part itself and no background search runs, for a crop that tightly frames the part; fit?: "width" | "height" | "both" (default "width"): one uniform scale, taken from the named dimension ("both" claims both and scales by width, reporting aspect_mismatch when the shapes differ); overlay?: false leaves the overlay PNG out → overlap (0..1), edges: top|bottom|left|right in mm at nine stations (positive where the model reaches past the picture, null where a station misses one of the two), the grid and its mm_per_px, and overlay_png (red model, blue picture) as base64 PNG. The compare is outline only: holes are not compared — both the picture's and the model's holes are filled

fields.description: reference: path to a PNG or JPEG the model should match; view?/camera?/bodies?/rows? as inspect.silhouette; crop_px?: [x, y, w, h] in pixels, or crop_fraction?: [x, y, w, h] as fractions 0..1 of the picture (to take one view off a board); part_fills_crop?: false — with true the crop box is the part itself and no background search runs, for a crop that tightly frames the part; fit?: "width" | "height" | "both" (default "width"): one uniform scale, taken from the named dimension ("both" claims both and scales by width, reporting aspect_mismatch when the shapes differ); overlay?: false leaves the overlay PNG out → overlap (0..1), edges: top|bottom|left|right in mm at nine stations (positive where the model reaches past the picture, null where a station misses one of the two), the grid and its mm_per_px, and overlay_png (red model, blue picture) as base64 PNG. The compare is outline only: holes are not compared — both the picture's and the model's holes are filled

inspect.compare_picture.reason: not in the live demo: it needs Mechvane's own handling on the server (install Mechvane to use it)

inspect.continuity.label: Continuity Analysis
inspect.continuity.help: body?: name (default: the visible bodies); edges?: [x,y,z] points or {"index": i} (default: every edge of the body; a pick must match one body); samples?: 3…257 stations along each edge, ends included (default 33); gap_tolerance_mm? (default 0.001), angle_tolerance_deg? (default 1), curvature_tolerance_per_mm? (default 0.01), curvature_change_tolerance_per_mm2? (default 0.001), curvature_change_rate_tolerance_per_mm3? (default 0.0001); add?: true keeps the seams already shaded and adds these (measuring an edge again replaces it); clear?: true turns the analysis off. → each edge's worst gap (G0), normal angle (G1), curvature jump (G2), jump of the curvature's change across the seam dκ/ds (G3) and of that change's rate d²κ/ds² (G4), from the faces' exact derivatives, as {value, at: [x,y,z], edge_fraction}; its order (g0…g4: the highest every station meets within the tolerances, null where the faces do not meet), its verdict (smooth: g2 or better, curvature_jump, sharp or gap) and a summary; the seams are shaded in the viewport

fields.name: add
fields.description: Preserve other measured seams, replacing only matching body/edge records.

fields.name: angle_tolerance_deg
fields.description: Normal angle tolerance in degrees. Default 1.

fields.name: body
fields.description: Body name; otherwise visible bodies. At most 64 bodies in one call.

fields.name: curvature_change_rate_tolerance_per_mm3
fields.description: Tolerance on the jump of that change's rate (G4) in inverse mm³.

fields.name: curvature_change_tolerance_per_mm2
fields.description: Tolerance on the jump of the curvature's change across the seam (G3) in inverse mm².

fields.name: curvature_tolerance_per_mm
fields.description: Curvature tolerance in inverse mm. Default .01.

fields.name: edges
fields.description: At most 512 edge indices or points. Empty/absent measures all seams.

fields.name: gap_tolerance_mm
fields.description: Positional tolerance in mm, 0…1e9 exclusive. Default .001.

fields.name: samples
fields.description: Integer stations per edge, 3…257. Default 33.

inspect.curvature_comb.label: Curvature Comb Analysis
inspect.curvature_comb.help: curves?: [sketch curve ids] (sketch?: id|name, default active) | edges?: [[x,y,z] points on body edges: the edge whose exact curve passes nearest] | faces?: [[x,y,z] points on faces] with count?: isoparametric curves each way (default 4; combs along the face's iso grid); density?: teeth per curve, 2…2000 (default 40; on an edge or an iso curve exactly that many, evenly spaced along its parameter); scale?: comb length per unit curvature (default auto: the longest tooth a fifth of the combs' size); length?: a multiplier on the automatic scale, 0.01…100 (default 1; ignored with `scale`); add?: true keeps the combs shown and adds these, every comb again at one scale (with nothing picked it draws those shown again with this call's options, or turns the analysis on with none); clear?: true turns the analysis off. Every comb of a call shares one scale, so tooth lengths compare across curves; the viewport draws them. The curvature is exact: from each sketch curve, edge curve (line, circle, ellipse, B-spline, NURBS, intersection curve) or face surface's own derivatives, never from the display mesh; a face's teeth are the surface's normal curvature along each iso curve, along the surface normal. → combs: [{curve, teeth: [[foot, tip]], envelope: [tip], max_curvature, min_radius}] (those shown, with `add`), scale
inspect.curvature_comb.description:
Curvature combs: teeth along each curve, edge or face isocurve, each as long as the curvature
there times `scale`, standing out on the convex side. Give `curves`, `edges` or `faces`, or
more than one.

fields.name: add
fields.description:
Keep the combs shown and add these, every comb again at one scale. With nothing picked it
draws those shown again with this call's options.

fields.name: clear
fields.description: Turn the analysis off.

fields.name: count
fields.description: With `faces`: how many isoparametric curves each way (default 4; 1 to 50).

fields.name: curves
fields.description: Sketch curve ids (the first 1000 are used).

fields.name: density
fields.description: Teeth per curve (default 40; 2 to 2000).

fields.name: length
fields.description: A multiplier on the automatic scale (default 1; 0.01 to 100). Ignored with `scale`.

fields.name: scale
fields.description:
Tooth length per unit of curvature (mm²). Default, or when not above 0: the longest tooth
is a fifth of the size of everything combed.

fields.name: sketch
fields.description: The sketch the curves are in (default: the one being edited). Read only with `curves`.

inspect.curvature_map.label: Curvature Map Analysis
inspect.curvature_map.help: radius?: mm shown red (default: a tenth of the model's size); clear?: true turns the analysis off

fields.name: radius
fields.description:
Radius in mm shown red, greater than 1e-6 and less than 1e9.
Default a tenth of the largest model diagonal, or 10 mm for an empty model.

inspect.draft.label: Draft Analysis
inspect.draft.help: pull?: [x,y,z] direction (default Z); angle?: degrees (default 1); clear?: true turns the analysis off

fields.name: angle
fields.description: Threshold in degrees, 0 inclusive to 90 exclusive. Default 1.

fields.name: pull
fields.description: An axis: X, Y or Z (any case), or a direction [x, y, z] that isn't zero.

inspect.environment_map.label: Environment Map Analysis
inspect.environment_map.help: clear?: true turns the analysis off

inspect.interference.label: Interference
inspect.interference.help: bodies?: [names] (default: all, in world placement; a name that is no body is refused); budget_s?: seconds (default 240, at most 86400: pairs not finished by then are listed in unchecked as "not checked: the time budget … ran out" and the call returns); exclude_pairs?: [[a, b]] (pairs left out, such as a pin in its hole: each side a body's world name or an occurrence id|name, matching every body under it; pairs_excluded counts them) → interferences: pairs that overlap with the overlap volume, area, bounding box and centre, and a_part, b_part: {component, path: [occurrence names], path_ids} where each body sits (also on unchecked pairs); unchecked: [{a, b, reason}], the pairs that could not be checked, with the reason, and each mesh body (STL, 3MF or OBJ import: not intersected) as {a: name, b: null, reason: "mesh body: not checked"}, so count: 0 is not read as no overlap (checked counts the solid bodies). Bodies are pruned by bounding box first, then by their display meshes (pairs whose meshes stay apart by more than their chord tolerances, neither inside the other, are clear without a boolean), so any number of bodies is fine; the pairs left are intersected exactly, in parallel on desktop, the slowest first; at most 20000 pairs whose boxes overlap are intersected per call (truncated: true and skipped_pairs: n say when more were left out). Also: pairs_candidate (boxes overlap), pairs_cleared (by the meshes), pairs_intersected, pairs_not_checked, pairs_excluded, budget_exceeded, threads (worker threads; 0: on the calling thread), boolean_ms and tessellate_ms (kernel time summed over the pairs), slowest: [{a, b, ms, boolean_ms, tessellate_ms}] and ms
inspect.interference.description:
Find the pairs of solid bodies that share volume, in world placement, and how much. Pairs are
ruled out by their boxes, then by their meshes; the pairs left are intersected exactly,
slowest first, within `budget_s`. Mesh bodies aren't intersected: each is listed in
`unchecked`.

fields.name: bodies
fields.description:
The bodies to check, by name. Default (or `null`): every body. A name that is no body is
refused.

fields.name: budget_s
fields.description:
The seconds the exact checks may take, above 0, at most 86400 (a day). Pairs not finished
by then are listed in `unchecked`, and the call returns. Default (or `null`): 240.

fields.name: exclude_pairs
fields.description:
Pairs left out, such as a pin in its hole: `[a, b]`, each side a body's world name or an
occurrence's id or name, matching every body under it. Default: none.

inspect.isocurve.label: Isocurve Analysis
inspect.isocurve.help: faces: [[x,y,z]…] points on faces (1…100); count?: whole number of curves each way, 1…100 (default 8); add?: true keeps the faces already shown; clear?: true turns the analysis off. → each face's isoparametric curves, u = const and v = const of its surface, evenly spaced across it and cut to its trims, as points (`curves`) and per face (`faces`); the viewport draws them
inspect.isocurve.description:
The isoparametric curves of faces, u = const and v = const of each face's surface, cut to its
trims; `faces` unless `clear`.

fields.name: add
fields.description: Keep the faces already shown.

fields.name: clear
fields.description: Turn the analysis off.

fields.name: count
fields.description: How many curves each way (default 8; 1 to 100).

inspect.measure.label: Measure
inspect.measure.help: bodies?: [names] (default all); names_only?: bool (each world body's name and its definition's, nothing measured) → closed per body; volume_mm3, center_of_mass, density_g_cm3 and mass_g only for closed, consistently oriented bodies; area, bbox and counts for all; total.open_bodies_skipped counts bodies excluded from volume/mass totals; or items: [1-2 selections] (face/edge: type, body, and point on it or index from model.faces/model.edges, or both) → length/area/volume; a face's perimeter_mm, with outer_perimeter_mm and inner_perimeter_mm on a flat face with holes; diameter, radius, circumference or arc_length/angle_deg of circles, arcs and cylinders; slot sizes; min (distance_mm, from, to), max, center_distance (centre to centre, or from an axis) and angle
inspect.measure.description:
How `inspect.measure` selects: bodies, or one or two picked items. With `items`, `bodies` and
`names_only` are not read, so the check leaves them alone.

fields.name: bodies
fields.description: The bodies to measure, by name. Default: all. Not read with `items`.

fields.name: items
fields.description:
One or two selections to measure, instead of bodies: a face or edge `{type, body, point}`,
`{type, body, index}` (as `model.faces` and `model.edges` list it) or both, or a body,
vertex, sketch curve or profile as `Sel` has it.

fields.name: names_only
fields.description:
Give each body's name and its definition's and measure nothing. Default: false. Not read
with `items`.

inspect.minimum_radius.label: Minimum Radius Analysis
inspect.minimum_radius.help: curves?: [sketch curve ids] (sketch?) | edges?: [[x,y,z]…] | faces?: [[x,y,z]…] (default: every face of every body); the smallest radius of curvature of each and where it is
inspect.minimum_radius.description:
The smallest radius of curvature of each sketch curve, edge or face, and where it is. With
none of `curves`, `edges` and `faces`: every face of every body.

fields.name: curves
fields.description: Sketch curve ids (the first 1000 are used).

fields.name: sketch
fields.description: The sketch the curves are in (default: the one being edited). Read only with `curves`.

inspect.parameter_sweep.label: Parameter Sweep
inspect.parameter_sweep.help: parameter: name; values: [number | expression] (at most 200) | from, to: numbers, steps? (default 10, at most 199: steps + 1 values) → for each value, in a copy of the design (the design itself is not changed): {value, ms (the rebuild), ok, failed: [{feature, name, error}], warned: [{feature, name, warning}] (features that build at the current value and fail or warn at this one), joints_lost: [{joint, name, origin?: a|b, why}], joints_flipped: [{joint, name, origin: a|b, degrees}] (an origin's z turned more than 90° on its own part from where it is now), sketches_flipped: [{sketch, name, degrees}] (the sketch plane's normal turned more than 90°), sketches_failed: [{sketch, name, failing, folded}] (a solve that fails, or keeps a triangle's turn or an offset's side only by flipping it)} (or {value, ms, ok: false, error} where the parameter takes no such value); summary: {values, ok, slowest_ms, failed, joints_lost, joints_flipped, sketches_flipped, sketches_failed} (how many values show each)
inspect.parameter_sweep.description:
Rebuild the design in a copy at each value of a parameter and report what fails, turns over
or loses its reference there, against the design as it is. The design itself isn't changed.
Give `values`, or `from` and `to`.

fields.name: from
fields.description: The first value of an even sweep (used only with `to`).

fields.name: parameter
fields.description: The parameter, by name, as `parameters.list` lists it.

fields.name: steps
fields.description: With `from` and `to`: how many steps between them (default 10), so `steps + 1` values.

fields.name: to
fields.description: The last value of an even sweep (used only with `from`).

fields.name: values
fields.description: The values to sweep, each a number or an expression (at most 1000 bytes, not blank), set as the parameter's expression in turn.

inspect.parameter_variants.label: Compare Parameter Variants
inspect.parameter_variants.help: variants: [{name, set: {parameter: number | expression}}] (1 to 12; up to 16 existing parameters each). Rebuild each set together in a separate copy of the open design. Returns baseline and ordered results with volume, mass, body counts and rebuild regressions. No edits are kept.
inspect.parameter_variants.description: Compare independent sets of parameter values without editing the design.

fields.name: variants
fields.description: Candidates to evaluate, in order, each starting from the open design.

inspect.section.label: Section Analysis
inspect.section.help: plane: XY|XZ|YZ | construction plane name or id | {origin, normal}; offset?: expr along the plane's normal (XY: +Z, XZ: +Y, YZ: +X); at?: expr, the cut's world coordinate on the named plane's axis (XY: Z, XZ: Y, YZ: X), instead of offset; flip?: bool; hatch?: bool (hatch the cut faces, in each body's colour; default true); or clear: true. Returns the cut's origin and normal, and for a named plane its axis and at

fields.name: at
fields.description: World coordinate on a named plane's normal axis; mutually exclusive with offset.

fields.name: offset
fields.description: Signed distance along the original plane normal, in design units or an expression.

fields.name: plane
fields.description: Required unless clearing. XY/XZ/YZ, construction name/id, or {origin?,normal}.

inspect.silhouette.label: Silhouette
inspect.silhouette.help: view?: front|back|left|right|top|bottom|iso (default front); or camera?: {target: [x,y,z], yaw, pitch, distance, fov?} (mm, radians; fov 0 means parallel); bodies?: [world body names] (default visible bodies, named hidden bodies included); rows?: mask height in pixels (default 240, clamped to 16..1024) → tightly framed run-length mask, box_mm, mm_per_px, right/up, projection, body and triangle counts
inspect.silhouette.description: A tightly framed, view-aligned union of the projected body meshes, as a run-length mask. Changes nothing in the design.

fields.name: bodies
fields.description: One body name, or a list of up to 10000.

fields.name: camera
fields.description: An orbit camera, in mm and radians. Other keys are ignored.

fields.name: rows
fields.description: The mask's height in pixels, clamped to 16..1024. Default: 240.

fields.name: view
fields.description: A standard view to look from. Not with `camera`. Default: front.

inspect.zebra.label: Zebra Analysis
inspect.zebra.help: stripes?: number across the view (default 12); clear?: true turns the analysis off

fields.name: stripes
fields.description: Stripe frequency across the view, including fractional values. Default 12; 1…200.

joint.as_built.label: As-Built Joint
joint.as_built.help: type, a: occurrence, b: occurrence (stay where they are); at?: joint origin (default: b's origin) — the joint's frame; one on a or b is kept on its face or hole there, so the joint follows it as the design changes; name?; limits?: [[min, max] | null…]; quiet?: bool
joint.as_built.description:
Add a joint between two occurrences that stay where they are: its frame is a joint origin
(`at`, default b's origin), and the joint starts with the origins coinciding as they are. An
origin on a or b is kept on its face or hole there, so the joint follows it as the design
changes. One undo step.

fields.name: a
fields.description: An occurrence by id or name (0 or `root`: the root), or the name of a component: its first occurrence.

fields.name: at
fields.description: A joint origin: the name of a joint origin made with joint.origin, or an object that says where it is, in world coordinates. Give one of face, circle, edge, point, plane or axis (a point [x, y, z]; for face and circle also a face's name; a plane or axis by name or definition object), or a frame {origin, z, x?}.

fields.name: b
fields.description: An occurrence by id or name (0 or `root`: the root), or the name of a component: its first occurrence.

fields.name: limits
fields.description:
The limits of each value: [min, max] pairs, with null for a value without limits. Default:
none.

fields.name: name
fields.description:
The joint's name. Default: its type, `Joint` and the first number no joint's name has.
Blank text gives the default.

fields.name: quiet
fields.description: Leave out `dof` and `fixed` in the reply. Default: false.

fields.name: type
fields.description: A joint's type: rigid, revolute (turns), slider (slides), cylindrical (both), pin_slot, planar or ball; or a relation that ties only some directions or points, made where the parts are: parallel, perpendicular, angle, point_on_plane, point_on_line or line_on_plane. Case, spaces, `_` and `-` are ignored, and rotate, slide, square, point_on_face, point_on_axis and line_on_face are also taken.

fields.name: value
fields.description: Like `values`: only whether it is given matters.

fields.name: values
fields.description:
Not a value of this joint, which starts at zero: only whether `values` is given matters.
Given, a relation type is not started from where its parts are.

joint.as_built.reason: Mechvane's adopt_joint keeps the joint checkable

joint.cam.label: Cam
joint.cam.help: a: the cam's joint (revolute); b: the follower's joint, a slider (a translating follower) or a revolute (an oscillating one),          b driven by a; profile: {sketch: id|name, index?: the profile (default: the largest)} | {edges: [[x,y,z]…] (points on edges of          the cam's bodies forming one closed loop, world), occurrence?}: the cam's outline, in a plane square to its axis, read again          whenever the design changes; follower?: knife|roller|flat (default knife; flat: a face square to a slider's line); radius?: the          roller's radius (mm, an expression or {circle: [x,y,z], occurrence?}: the roller's round face, which is its tip too); tip?: a          joint origin where the follower touches: its knife's point or its roller's centre, such as {circle: [x,y,z]} on the roller          (needed for an oscillating follower; a translating one's line runs through it, by default along its slider's axis); flip?: bool (ride the cam from the other side          than the one the follower is on now); link?: index (replace that motion link; profile, follower, radius and tip left out then keep that cam's definition, picked profile and round face included, and flip left out keeps the side it rides from now) → link, lift: {min, max, rise, unit} (b's travel          over a turn of the cam), reverse (the side it rides from), follower_offset (mm: how far a translating follower's line passes          from the cam's axis); b keeps where it is, also when the link replaces another (at the current pose)
joint.cam.description:
Drive a follower from a cam: the cam's turn sets the follower's travel (a slider, a translating
follower) or turn (a revolute, an oscillating one) from the cam's outline, and the follower
keeps where it is. The link is read again whenever the design changes.

fields.name: a
fields.description: A joint's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: b
fields.description: A joint's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: flip
fields.description: Ride the cam from the other side than the one the follower is on now. Default: false.

fields.name: follower
fields.description:
The follower's kind: knife, roller or flat (a face square to a slider's line). Default:
knife.

fields.name: link
fields.description: Replace that motion link (its index in `joint.list`'s `links`) instead of adding one.

fields.name: profile
fields.description: The cam's outline, in a plane square to its axis, read again whenever the design changes: {sketch, index?}, a closed profile of a sketch; or {edges, occurrence?}, points on edges of the cam's bodies that form one closed loop. A call with `sketch` is the first form, whatever else it has.

fields.name: quiet
fields.description: Leave out `dof` and `fixed` in the reply. Default: false.

fields.name: radius
fields.description: A length: a number (mm), an expression (text of at most 1000 bytes, kept as typed so it follows the design's parameters), or {circle: [x, y, z], occurrence?}, the round face there, by its radius, read again whenever the design changes. The circle is a point on the round face (not its centre), or the face's name as model.faces lists it.

fields.name: tip
fields.description: A joint origin: the name of a joint origin made with joint.origin, or an object that says where it is, in world coordinates. Give one of face, circle, edge, point, plane or axis (a point [x, y, z]; for face and circle also a face's name; a plane or axis by name or definition object), or a frame {origin, z, x?}.

joint.create.label: Joint
joint.create.help: type: rigid|revolute|slider|cylindrical|pin_slot|planar|ball, or a relation: parallel|perpendicular|angle|point_on_plane|point_on_line|line_on_plane (ties only some directions or points, made where the parts are; several between two parts add up); a, b: joint origins ({occurrence, face|circle|edge|point: [x,y,z] in world, or face|circle: "<face name>", plane: "XY"|"o:<ids>/origin/<item>"|"<name>", axis: "Z"|"o:<ids>/origin/<item>"|"<name>"; z? for a point, end?, x? as joint.origin} | origin name); values?: [angles in deg or expressions, distances]; limits?: [[min, max] | null…]; flip?: bool (default false: the origins are mated, b's z against a's as two faces meet - two plane or axis datums mate aligned, each part keeping its side of the datum, and flip mates them; true: b's z along a's, so two origins given at one point with the same z and x stay as they are; a point origin without x takes its x from z, so give x on both, or use joint.as_built, to keep a turned part where it is); offset?: mm or an expression; angle?: deg or an expression (an angle relation's tilt from mated; for other joints the default is none, or a half turn where that turns b less, so faces that already meet stay as they are); name?; quiet?: bool (leave out dof and fixed). An expression (text) is kept with the joint and worked out again whenever the design changes, so the joint follows the parameters it names; a joint whose expression no longer works out (a parameter deleted) is left out of the solve with the reason in its errors
joint.create.description:
Add a joint between two occurrences, mated at two joint origins, and re-solve. A relation type
(parallel, perpendicular, angle, point_on_plane, point_on_line, line_on_plane) ties only some
directions or points and is made where the parts are. An expression given for `offset`,
`angle` or a value is kept with the joint and worked out again whenever the design changes. The
joint starts at its values inside its limits, and a part moved to a limit is said so in
`warnings`. One undo step.

fields.name: a
fields.description: A joint origin: the name of a joint origin made with joint.origin, or an object that says where it is, in world coordinates. Give one of face, circle, edge, point, plane or axis (a point [x, y, z]; for face and circle also a face's name; a plane or axis by name or definition object), or a frame {origin, z, x?}.

fields.name: angle
fields.description: A number (degrees for an angle, mm for a distance; below 1e9 in size), or an expression (text) over the design's parameters, such as "width / 2" or "30 deg".

fields.name: b
fields.description: A joint origin: the name of a joint origin made with joint.origin, or an object that says where it is, in world coordinates. Give one of face, circle, edge, point, plane or axis (a point [x, y, z]; for face and circle also a face's name; a plane or axis by name or definition object), or a frame {origin, z, x?}.

fields.name: flip
fields.description:
Whether b's z lies along a's instead of against it. Default: false (the origins are mated,
b's z against a's as two faces meet); true keeps two origins given at one point with the
same z and x as they are. A point origin without x takes its x from z, so give x on both,
or use joint.as_built, to keep a turned part where it is.

fields.name: limits
fields.description:
The limits of each value: [min, max] pairs, with null for a value without limits. Default:
none.

fields.name: name
fields.description:
The joint's name. Default: its type, `Joint` and the first number no joint's name has.
Blank text gives the default.

fields.name: offset
fields.description: A number (degrees for an angle, mm for a distance; below 1e9 in size), or an expression (text) over the design's parameters, such as "width / 2" or "30 deg".

fields.name: quiet
fields.description: Leave out `dof` and `fixed` in the reply. Default: false.

fields.name: type
fields.description: A joint's type: rigid, revolute (turns), slider (slides), cylindrical (both), pin_slot, planar or ball; or a relation that ties only some directions or points, made where the parts are: parallel, perpendicular, angle, point_on_plane, point_on_line or line_on_plane. Case, spaces, `_` and `-` are ignored, and rotate, slide, square, point_on_face, point_on_axis and line_on_face are also taken.

fields.name: value
fields.description: A number (degrees for an angle, mm for a distance; below 1e9 in size), or an expression (text) over the design's parameters, such as "width / 2" or "30 deg".

fields.name: values
fields.description:
The joint's values to start at: one per coordinate (angles in degrees, distances in mm, or
expressions the joint then follows). Default: 0 for each, or for a relation or a joint that
closes a loop, where the parts are. Wins over `value`.

joint.create.reason: made with Mechvane's add_joint so the joint can be checked later

joint.delete.label: Delete Joint
joint.delete.help: joint: id|name (or origin: name, link: index)
joint.delete.description:
Delete a joint (and the motion links it is in), a joint origin or a motion link. Give
`origin` to delete a joint origin, or else `link` to delete a motion link, or else `joint`.
With `origin` or `link` the other keys are not read. One undo step.

fields.name: joint
fields.description: A joint's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: link
fields.description:
The motion link to delete, by its index in `joint.list`'s `links` (a negative number is
0). Wins over `joint`; not read when `origin` is given.

fields.name: origin
fields.description: The joint origin to delete, by name. Wins over `link` and `joint`.

fields.name: quiet
fields.description:
Leave out `dof` and `fixed` in the reply. Read only when a joint is deleted. Default:
false.

joint.delete.reason: not in the live demo: it needs Mechvane's own handling on the server (install Mechvane to use it)

joint.drive.label: Drive Joints
joint.drive.help: joint: id|name; value | values: [angles in deg or expressions, distances] (values not given keep theirs; a value driven drops the expression joint.create gave it; clamped to the limits; the other joints of a closed loop follow, and the motion stops where the loop can no longer close → stopped_by_loop); quiet?: bool (leave out dof and fixed) → values: [{name, value, unit: deg|mm, limits}] as joint.list gives them; requested: the values asked for, in the same form; held: [{name, requested, value, unit, why}] for each driven value that ended up elsewhere (a motion link sets it, as a screw's travel follows its turn; a limit; contact; a closed loop); moved: whether any occurrence moved; reason: why the joint can move nothing (suppressed: nothing is stored; its origins lost; its chain joined to nothing grounded → unconnected: the occurrence named; or, when nothing moved, the first held value's why); index?: zero-based coordinate to drive with value (the other coordinates follow); continuous?: bool (drag frame, suppress UI echo); stop_at_budget?: bool (default false: a contact check past its sample or work budget fails the drive; true: the drive stops at the last placement checked clear → stopped_by_budget {budget: samples|work|intersections, fraction})
joint.drive.description:
Set a joint's values by hand, as far as its limits, contact sets and closed loops allow; the
other joints of a closed loop follow, and the motion stops where the loop can no longer close.
A value driven drops the expression joint.create gave it. Give `value` or `values`, or `index`
with `value` to drive one coordinate while the others follow.

fields.name: continuous
fields.description:
A frame of a drag: the reply says `continuous`, and the app's command line doesn't echo it.
Default: false.

fields.name: index
fields.description:
Drive only this coordinate, counted from zero (0 for a revolute joint's angle); the others
follow. Goes with `value`, not `values`.

fields.name: joint
fields.description: A joint's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: quiet
fields.description: Leave out `dof` and `fixed` in the reply. Default: false.

fields.name: stop_at_budget
fields.description:
Where a contact check runs past its sample or work budget: false fails the drive; true
stops it at the last placement checked clear (`stopped_by_budget`). Default: false.

fields.name: value
fields.description: A number (degrees for an angle, mm for a distance; below 1e9 in size), or an expression (text) over the design's parameters, such as "width / 2" or "30 deg".

fields.name: values
fields.description:
The values to drive to: one per coordinate (angles in degrees, distances in mm, or
expressions worked out once). A value not given keeps its own. Not with `index`.

joint.edit.label: Edit Joint
joint.edit.help: joint; a?, b?: joint origins as joint.create takes them (a side left out keeps its place; the two must stay on different occurrences); type?, flip?, offset?, angle? (a number, or an expression the joint then follows), suppressed?, name?; the joint re-solves, keeping its limits and expressions (a relation's values start again where its parts are); an edit that places it again (not a rename alone) meets a loop it closes as joint.create does, turning an angle a half turn where only that meets it
joint.edit.description:
Edit a joint in place. The sides `a` and `b` take a joint origin as joint.create does; a side
left out keeps its place, and the two must stay on different occurrences. The joint re-solves
and keeps its limits, its drive and the expressions it follows; a relation's values start
again where its parts are when its sides, type, offset, angle or flip change.

fields.name: a
fields.description: Side a: a joint origin, as joint.create takes it. Default: a keeps its place.

fields.name: angle
fields.description: The turn about that distance: an angle, or an expression the joint follows.

fields.name: b
fields.description: Side b: a joint origin, as joint.create takes it. Default: b keeps its place.

fields.name: flip
fields.description: Whether b's z lies along a's instead of against it, as joint.create's `flip`.

fields.name: joint
fields.description: A feature's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The joint's new name.

fields.name: offset
fields.description: The distance from a's frame to b's along z: a length, or an expression the joint follows.

fields.name: quiet
fields.description: Leave out the degrees of freedom and the fixed occurrences in the reply.

fields.name: suppressed
fields.description: Suppress the joint (true) or bring it back (false).

fields.name: type
fields.description: The joint's type, as joint.create takes it (rigid, revolute, slider, ...).

joint.edit.reason: changed with Mechvane's edit_joint so the joint can be checked later

joint.find_limits.label: Find Joint Limits
joint.find_limits.help: joint: id|name; index? (one value; default every value); refine?, step?, occurrences?, against?, contact_sets?, exclude_pairs? (as joint.sweep) → values: [{index, dof, unit, value (now), min, max, min_by, max_by, range}], each value swept both ways from where it is, its own limits ignored, closed loops following; each side stops at the first contact (bisected to `refine`), where a loop cannot close, or at another limit (another value's, or another joint's through a motion link): min_by/max_by {a, b, at} | "loop" | "limit" | "budget" (its work ran out: the last value checked clear) | "turn" (an angle with no contact within a turn: a turn from the other side, or ±180° from now when nothing is met at all) | "range" (a distance with no contact within the parts' reach: min/max null); touching_at_start, overlapping_at_start: [{a, b, depth_mm}] (already passing into each other: they stop it only going deeper), refine_mm, gap_method, gap_tolerance_mm, pairs (0: no two parts to check, so nothing is swept). The design is not changed
joint.find_limits.description:
Find where each value of a joint can go before the parts it moves touch another body. The
design is not changed.

fields.name: against
fields.description: The parts that stay: each of `occurrences` is checked only against these.

fields.name: contact_sets
fields.description: Check the pairs of the design's contact sets instead (not with `occurrences`).

fields.name: exclude_pairs
fields.description:
Pairs left out: `[a, b]`, each an occurrence's id or name; a pair of bodies is left out
when one is under `a` and the other under `b`. Default: none.

fields.name: index
fields.description: Which value (0 for a revolute's angle). Default: every value of the joint.

fields.name: joint
fields.description: A joint's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: occurrences
fields.description: The parts checked against each other. Default: every occurrence.

fields.name: refine
fields.description:
mm: each stop is bisected until no part moves more than this between the last clear value
and the touching one (above 0, at most 1000). Default: 0.01.

fields.name: step
fields.description:
Between samples, in the value's unit (degrees for angles, mm for distances; above 0).
Default: fine enough that no part passes through another between two.

joint.gear.label: Gear
joint.gear.help: a, b: joints that turn (revolute), b driven by a; ra, rb: the gears' pitch radii (or tooth counts): mm, an expression, or {circle: [x,y,z], occurrence?}: the round face there, its radius (read again whenever the design changes, so the ratio follows edits); internal?: bool (one is a ring gear: both turn the same way; by default b turns the other way); reverse?: bool; link?: index (replace that motion link; a radius left out then keeps the old gear's, picked round face included) → link, ratio (b's degrees per a's); b keeps where it is, also when the link replaces another (at the current pose)
joint.gear.description:
Gear one turning joint to another: b turns the other way from a by the ratio of the pitch
radii (the same way for an internal gear), and keeps where it is, so the teeth mesh at the pose
they are in. The ratio follows the radii (an expression or a round face) as the design changes.

fields.name: a
fields.description: A joint's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: b
fields.description: A joint's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: internal
fields.description: One is a ring gear: both turn the same way. Default: false (b turns the other way).

fields.name: link
fields.description: Replace that motion link (its index in `joint.list`'s `links`) instead of adding one.

fields.name: quiet
fields.description: Leave out `dof` and `fixed` in the reply. Default: false.

fields.name: ra
fields.description: A length: a number (mm), an expression (text of at most 1000 bytes, kept as typed so it follows the design's parameters), or {circle: [x, y, z], occurrence?}, the round face there, by its radius, read again whenever the design changes. The circle is a point on the round face (not its centre), or the face's name as model.faces lists it.

fields.name: rb
fields.description: A length: a number (mm), an expression (text of at most 1000 bytes, kept as typed so it follows the design's parameters), or {circle: [x, y, z], occurrence?}, the round face there, by its radius, read again whenever the design changes. The circle is a point on the round face (not its centre), or the face's name as model.faces lists it.

fields.name: reverse
