fields.description: Turn b the other way round. Default: false.

joint.inspect.label: Inspect Joint
joint.inspect.help: joint?: id|name (default: every joint) → joints: [{id, name, type, suppressed, visible, flip, offset (mm), angle (deg), values: as joint.list gives them, dofs, expressions?: {offset?, angle?, values?}, a, b: {occurrence, occurrence_name, component, component_name, path (occurrence names from the top, `/` between), snap (as saved: type, pick, face, end, edge, corner, x, point, z, in the component's coordinates), references: [{role: face|end|x|edge|corner, name, role_in_feature?: (top, side:c1…), feature?: {id, name, type} (the feature that made the face; error when it is gone), sketch?: {id, name, curve, curve_type} (a face swept from a sketch curve), faces?: [an edge's two faces], unverified?: a name saved before exact names}], resolves, frame?: {origin, z, x} in the world, error?: why the origin is lost}, links: [{index, role: driver|driven, …as joint.list}], errors, conflicts}] (reads only: nothing changes)
joint.inspect.description:
Say what a joint is defined by and attached to: its two origins (the snap as saved, and the
feature, face, edge or sketch curve each name refers to), whether each is found today and why
not, its type, offset, angle, flip, values, expressions and motion links. Reads only: nothing
changes.

fields.name: joint
fields.description: The joint, by id or name. Default: every joint.

joint.limits.label: Joint Limits
joint.limits.help: joint; index?: value index (default 0); min?, max? (omit both to clear)
joint.limits.description:
Set one of a joint's value limits, or clear it. A value already past the new limit moves to
it. Give `min` and `max` together, or neither to clear.

fields.name: index
fields.description:
Which value, counted from zero (0 for a revolute joint's angle); a negative number is 0.
Default: 0.

fields.name: joint
fields.description: A joint's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: max
fields.description: A number (degrees for an angle, mm for a distance; below 1e9 in size), or an expression (text) over the design's parameters, such as "width / 2" or "30 deg".

fields.name: min
fields.description: A number (degrees for an angle, mm for a distance; below 1e9 in size), or an expression (text) over the design's parameters, such as "width / 2" or "30 deg".

fields.name: quiet
fields.description: Leave out `dof` and `fixed` in the reply. Default: false.

joint.list.label: List Joints
joint.list.help: → joints (type, occurrences, values, limits; expressions: {offset?, angle?, values?} when they were typed as expressions), origins, links, degrees of freedom, conflicts, floating: [{occurrences, joints}] (joint chains joined to nothing grounded: the solver places none of them, so driving them moves nothing)
joint.list.description: List the joints, motion links and joint origins, with the solve.

fields.name: quiet
fields.description: Leave out `dof` and `fixed` in the reply. Default: false.

joint.motion_link.label: Motion Link
joint.motion_link.help: a, b: joints; ratio (b = ratio · a + offset): b's units per a's (mm per deg for an angle driving a distance); offset?: in b's units (deg for an angle, mm for a distance, or an expression); ia?, ib?: value indices (default 0); link?: index (put this link in place of that motion link, as the gear and cam commands do) → link: the link's index, as joint.list numbers them
joint.motion_link.description:
Tie one joint's value to another's: b = ratio · a + offset, in b's units, so that when a is
driven b follows. The link starts at b's value now (the offset is `offset`, or 0). A joint
follows one link at most, and two joints may not drive each other.

fields.name: a
fields.description: A joint's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: b
fields.description: A joint's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: ia
fields.description: Which of a's values drives, counted from zero (a negative number is 0). Default: 0.

fields.name: ib
fields.description: Which of b's values follows, counted from zero (a negative number is 0). Default: 0.

fields.name: link
fields.description: Replace that motion link (its index in `joint.list`'s `links`) instead of adding one.

fields.name: offset
fields.description: A number (degrees for an angle, mm for a distance; below 1e9 in size), or an expression (text) over the design's parameters, such as "width / 2" or "30 deg".

fields.name: quiet
fields.description: Leave out `dof` and `fixed` in the reply. Default: false.

fields.name: ratio
fields.description: A number below 1e9 in size.

joint.origin.label: Joint Origin
joint.origin.help: name?, occurrence?: id|name (default: from the pick, or the named face's component), path?: [occurrence ids from the root] (the placement picked on, ending at the occurrence: a part in a sub-assembly placed more than once is then on that copy; default: the occurrence's first placement, or with no occurrence the placement nearest the pick), face: [x,y,z] | "<name>" (centre of a planar face) | circle: [x,y,z] | "<name>" (centre of a round end: a point on its wall or rim, the end's centre, or the round face's name as model.faces lists it) | edge: [x,y,z] (a point on an edge of a planar face: the edge's middle, z out of the face, y into it; on?: [x,y,z] a point on the face (default: the larger planar face beside the edge); corner?: [x,y,z] near one end: the corner there, x and y along its two edges into the face; found again by name, so it follows the face as it changes size; z?: [x,y,z] the frame's z instead of the face's normal, along the edge when it runs that way, x chosen from z: an edge or corner picked as it is, kept as a point where it can't be found by name) | point: [x,y,z], z?: [x,y,z] | plane: "XY"|"XZ"|"YZ"|"o:<ids>/origin/<item>"|"<name>" | axis: "X"|"Y"|"Z"|"o:<ids>/origin/<item>"|"<name>"; a circle's z?: [x,y,z] (a round edge's centre with the way out of it: its end by name when that is the frame it shows, else a point there); body?: the named face's body; end?: "<name>" (a circle's end: the face across its rim there; default the end nearer the pick); x?: [x,y,z] (a direction, world) | "<face name>" | {face: [x,y,z]} (the frame's x: a direction, a plane's normal, or the way to another hole's axis; keeps a round origin's turn; a point's x is a direction, laid square to its z, default: chosen from z alone). Faces are kept by name: the origin follows its face, and a circle its end, when the design changes
joint.origin.description:
Make a named joint origin: a frame on a face, a round edge, an edge, a point, or given
outright, that joints can then take for a side by its name. Give one of `face`, `circle`,
`edge`, `point` or `frame`; a face or circle given by its name is found again by name, so the
origin follows its face as the design changes. Keys that apply only to some of these (`on` and
`corner` to an edge; `end` to a circle; `body` to a name) are read only then.

fields.name: axis
fields.description: An axis to sit on: "X", "Y" or "Z", "o:<ids>/origin/<item>" (a placement's origin axis), a construction axis's name, or an axis definition object.

fields.name: body
fields.description: With a face or circle given by its name: the body the face is on.

fields.name: circle
fields.description: A point in world coordinates, or a face's name as model.faces lists it (1 to 16384 characters).

fields.name: corner
fields.description:
With `edge`: a point near one end of the edge, for the corner there (x and y along its two
edges into the face), found again by name.

fields.name: edge
fields.description: A point [x, y, z] in mm, or {x, y, z}, each number below 1e9 in size.

fields.name: end
fields.description:
With `circle`: the end, by the name of the face across its rim there. Default: the end
nearer the pick. Refused for any other origin; for a circle given as a point with `z` it
is not checked.

fields.name: face
fields.description: A point in world coordinates, or a face's name as model.faces lists it (1 to 16384 characters).

fields.name: frame
fields.description: An explicit frame in world coordinates.

fields.name: name
fields.description:
The origin's name. Default: `Joint Origin` and the first number no origin's name has.
Blank text gives the default. A name already taken is refused.

fields.name: occurrence
fields.description: An occurrence by id or name (0 or `root`: the root), or the name of a component: its first occurrence.

fields.name: on
fields.description: With `edge`: a point on the face to use. Default: the larger planar face beside the edge.

fields.name: path
fields.description:
The placement picked on: occurrence ids from the top of the assembly down, ending at
`occurrence`, so a part in a sub-assembly placed more than once is on that copy. Default:
the occurrence's first placement, or with no occurrence the placement nearest the pick.

fields.name: plane
fields.description: A plane to sit on: "XY", "XZ" or "YZ" (the design's own), "o:<ids>/origin/<item>" (a placement's origin plane), a construction plane's name, or a plane definition object.

fields.name: point
fields.description: A point [x, y, z] in mm, or {x, y, z}, each number below 1e9 in size.

fields.name: x
fields.description:
The frame's x, its turn about z: a direction, a face's name or {face}. Read for a `face`,
a `circle` and a `point` (a direction there). Default: chosen from z alone, or the x the
face's frame has now.

fields.name: z
fields.description:
The frame's z, a direction in world coordinates, instead of the face's normal. Read for an
`edge` (then along the edge when it runs that way), a `circle` given as a point (the way
out of its end) and a `point`.

joint.rack_pinion.label: Rack and Pinion
joint.rack_pinion.help: a, b: a joint that turns (revolute: the pinion) and one that slides (slider: the rack), in either order, b driven by a; radius: the pinion's pitch radius (mm, an expression, or {circle: [x,y,z], occurrence?}): the rack travels radius × the turn in radians; reverse?: bool; link?: index (replace that motion link; the radius left out then keeps the old pinion's, picked round face included) → link, ratio (mm per degree, or degrees per mm); b keeps where it is, also when the link replaces another (at the current pose)
joint.rack_pinion.description:
Couple a turning joint to a sliding one as a rack and pinion: the rack travels the pinion's
radius times the turn in radians. b is driven by a, in either order of turning and sliding, and
keeps where it is, so the teeth mesh at the pose they are in.

fields.name: a
fields.description: A joint's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: b
fields.description: A joint's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: link
fields.description: Replace that motion link (its index in `joint.list`'s `links`) instead of adding one.

fields.name: quiet
fields.description: Leave out `dof` and `fixed` in the reply. Default: false.

fields.name: radius
fields.description: A length: a number (mm), an expression (text of at most 1000 bytes, kept as typed so it follows the design's parameters), or {circle: [x, y, z], occurrence?}, the round face there, by its radius, read again whenever the design changes. The circle is a point on the round face (not its centre), or the face's name as model.faces lists it.

fields.name: reverse
fields.description: Move the rack the other way round. Default: false.

joint.reach.label: Reach Point
joint.reach.help: occurrence: id|name; point: [x,y,z] (where its point goes, world); at?: [x,y,z] (its point, in the world where it is now; default: the centre of          its bodies' box); z?: [x,y,z] (the way its axis then points); axis?: [x,y,z] (that axis, in the world now; default: its own z); joints?: [ids          or names] (only these move toward the point; the other joints of a closed loop they are in follow); quiet?: bool; continuous?: bool (a frame          of a drag: the answer says continuous, and the app's command line doesn't echo it). Moves the values of the joints          on its chain from where they are to the nearest pose, within their limits, through motion links, keeping closed loops closed as joint.drive does          (contact sets are not checked) → reached; error_mm (and error_deg with z): how close it got; point: where its point is; values: [{joint, name,          values}] of the joints that moved, as joint.list gives them; moved; stopped_by_limit: [{joint, value, limit: min|max}]: the limits it rests on          short of the point; stopped_by_loop: {joint}: the closed loop that stopped it (its chain alone gets closer); reason: why nothing can move
joint.reach.description:
Move an occurrence's point to a place in the world by changing the values of the joints on its
chain, from where they are to the nearest pose within their limits, through motion links and
keeping closed loops closed as joint.drive does (contact sets are not checked). With `z` the
occurrence's axis is turned to point that way too. Reaches as far as it can: the reply says how
close it got and what stopped it.

fields.name: at
fields.description: A point [x, y, z] in mm, or {x, y, z}, each number below 1e9 in size.

fields.name: axis
fields.description: A direction [x, y, z] or {x, y, z} of numbers below 1e9 in size, not the zero vector.

fields.name: continuous
fields.description:
A frame of a drag: the reply says `continuous`, and the app's command line doesn't echo it.
Default: false.

fields.name: joints
fields.description: A list of joints, each by id or name.

fields.name: occurrence
fields.description: An occurrence by id or name (0 or `root`: the root), or the name of a component: its first occurrence.

fields.name: point
fields.description: A point [x, y, z] in mm, or {x, y, z}, each number below 1e9 in size.

fields.name: quiet
fields.description: Leave out `dof` and `fixed` in the reply. Default: false.

fields.name: z
fields.description: A direction [x, y, z] or {x, y, z} of numbers below 1e9 in size, not the zero vector.

joint.rigid_group.label: Rigid Group
joint.rigid_group.help: occurrences: [ids or names] (move together, as they are)
joint.rigid_group.description:
Join occurrences so that they move together, as they are: a rigid joint, made as built, from
the first occurrence to each of the others. One undo step for each joint.

fields.name: occurrences
fields.description: 2 to 1000 occurrences, each by id or name.

joint.screw.label: Screw
joint.screw.help: joint: a cylindrical joint (its turn drives its travel) | a, b: a joint that turns and one that slides, b driven by a; pitch: travel per turn (mm or an expression); reverse?: bool (a left-hand thread); link?: index (replace that motion link; the pitch left out then keeps the old screw's) → link, ratio (mm per degree, or degrees per mm); b keeps where it is, also when the link replaces another (at the current pose)
joint.screw.description:
Couple a turn to a travel as a screw: one cylindrical joint whose turn drives its travel, or a
joint that turns and one that slides, b driven by a. The travel is the pitch for each turn, and
b keeps where it is.

fields.name: a
fields.description: A joint's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: b
fields.description: A joint's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: joint
fields.description: A joint's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: link
fields.description: Replace that motion link (its index in `joint.list`'s `links`) instead of adding one.

fields.name: pitch
fields.description: A length: a number (mm), an expression (text of at most 1000 bytes, kept as typed so it follows the design's parameters), or {circle: [x, y, z], occurrence?}, the round face there, by its radius, read again whenever the design changes. The circle is a point on the round face (not its centre), or the face's name as model.faces lists it.

fields.name: quiet
fields.description: Leave out `dof` and `fixed` in the reply. Default: false.

fields.name: reverse
fields.description: A left-hand thread. Default: false.

joint.solve.label: Solve Joints
joint.solve.help: re-place the occurrences from the joints → conflicts, errors, dof
joint.solve.description: Re-place the occurrences from the joints, and report conflicts, errors and degrees of freedom.

fields.name: quiet
fields.description: Leave out `dof` and `fixed` in the reply. Default: false.

joint.sweep.label: Sweep Joint
joint.sweep.help: joint: id|name; from, to: its value the sweep runs between (degrees for angles, mm for distances, or expressions); index? (which value, default 0); step? (between samples, in the joint's unit; default: fine enough that no part passes through another between two); refine?: mm (the first contact is bisected until no part moves more than this between the last clear value and the touching one; default 0.01); occurrences?: [ids or names] (checked against each other; default every occurrence), with against?: [ids or names] (the parts that stay: each of `occurrences` only against these), or contact_sets?: true (the pairs of the design's contact sets); exclude_pairs?: [[a, b]] (occurrences by id or name: pairs of bodies under a and b are not checked, such as a pin in its hole); budget_s?: seconds (at most 86400; past them the sweep stops with what it found; its work is then not capped. Without it the work caps, 4096 samples, 64 bisection steps and 500 million triangle tests, stop it the same way); report_gaps?: bool (the nearest gap at every sample, default false); apply?: bool (leave the design where the sweep stopped; default false: the design is not changed) → stopped_at (the last value clear of contact, or where a loop or limit stopped it; null: it reached `to`), stopped_by: {a, b, at: [x,y,z] (where they touch, world), a_part, b_part: {component, path: [occurrence names], path_ids} (where each touching body sits)} | "loop" | "limit" | "budget" (stopped_at: the last value checked clear) | null, samples: [{value, min_gap_mm?, pair?, parts?}], min_gap? (report_gaps: {part: {mm, at_value, to}}, the nearest each part came to another), unit, gap_method ("mesh": distances between the tessellations), gap_tolerance_mm (how far those can be off: 0 when every face is flat), pairs (checked), touching_at_start: [[a, b]] (pairs already touching at `from`, such as parts joined face to face or a door on its frame: these stop it only once they pass into each other deeper than they start), touching_parts (where their bodies sit), budget_s, budget_exceeded, budget_ran_out: "time" | "samples" | "bisections" (a contact reported less refined than `refine`) | "intersections" | "work" | null, applied. The parts are tested at the samples and through the bisection; the motion is on a copy (closed loops follow, contact sets do not stop it)
joint.sweep.description:
Drive one value of a joint from `from` toward `to` on a copy of the design, and stop at the
first contact between the parts checked (bisected to `refine`), where a closed loop can't
close, or at a limit. Closed loops follow; contact sets don't stop it. The design is not
changed unless `apply` is true.

fields.name: against
fields.description: The parts that stay: each of `occurrences` is checked only against these.

fields.name: apply
fields.description:
Leave the design where the sweep stopped, in one undo step. Default: false: the design
is not changed.

fields.name: budget_s
fields.description:
Seconds the sweep may take (above 0, at most 86400): past them it stops and returns what
it found, `stopped_by` `budget`, and its work is then not capped. Default: no time budget;
the work caps (4096 samples, 64 bisection steps, 500 million triangle tests) stop it the
same way.

fields.name: contact_sets
fields.description: Check the pairs of the design's contact sets instead (not with `occurrences`).

fields.name: exclude_pairs
fields.description:
Pairs left out, such as a pin in its hole: `[a, b]`, each an occurrence's id or name; a
pair of bodies is left out when one is under `a` and the other under `b`. Default: none.

fields.name: from
fields.description: A joint value: a number, in degrees for an angle and in mm for a distance, smaller than 1e9 in size, or an expression (`"90 deg"`, `"Opening"`).

fields.name: index
fields.description: Which value (0 for a revolute's angle). Default: 0.

fields.name: joint
fields.description: A joint's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: occurrences
fields.description: The parts checked against each other. Default: every occurrence.

fields.name: refine
fields.description:
mm: the first contact is bisected until no part moves more than this between the last
clear value and the touching one (above 0, at most 1000). Default: 0.01.

fields.name: report_gaps
fields.description:
Report the nearest gap at every sample, and the nearest each part came to another
(`min_gap`). Default: false.

fields.name: step
fields.description:
Between samples, in the value's unit (degrees for angles, mm for distances; above 0, at
most 1e9). Default: fine enough that no part passes through another between two.

fields.name: to
fields.description: A joint value: a number, in degrees for an angle and in mm for a distance, smaller than 1e9 in size, or an expression (`"90 deg"`, `"Opening"`).
