library.apply.label: Apply Local Library Entry
library.apply.help: path, entry: qualified ID, revision: exact content SHA-256; targets?: {bodies?, faces?: [{body,point}], components?}; name?: physical material name on import. Copies values in one undo step; material conflicts are explicit
library.apply.description:
Copy one library entry, at an exact revision, into this design in one undo step: an
appearance onto bodies, faces or components, or a physical material (assigned to bodies).

fields.name: entry
fields.description: The entry's qualified id, as `library.inspect` lists it (at most 129 bytes).

fields.name: name
fields.description:
For a physical material: the name to give it in this design (1 to 128 bytes). Default:
the entry's name. A material of that name already in the design is reused if it is the
same, and refused if it differs. An appearance entry refuses it.

fields.name: path
fields.description: The library file.

fields.name: revision
fields.description:
The entry's revision, as `library.inspect` lists it: the SHA-256 of its content, 64 hex
digits. An entry whose content has changed since is refused.

fields.name: targets
fields.description: What a library entry is copied onto: at most 1024 targets in all.

library.apply.reason: not in the live demo: it needs Mechvane's own handling on the server (install Mechvane to use it)

library.export.label: Export Design Library
library.export.help: path: .json; id? (default user.local), name?, provenance?, overwrite? false, format? solidcraft-library/2 (default) | solidcraft-library/1 (refuses PBR/cards). Copies assigned looks and design-local physical definitions; never changes the design
library.export.description:
Write the looks assigned in this design and its own physical materials to a library file.
The design is never changed.

fields.name: format
fields.description:
The file format. `solidcraft-library/1` refuses a design whose looks or materials have
PBR or physical cards, before writing anything.

fields.name: id
fields.description:
The library's id, which qualifies each entry's id: lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_`
and `-`, starting with a letter, at most 64.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The library's name: 1 to 128 bytes, without surrounding spaces or control characters.

fields.name: overwrite
fields.description: Replace the file if it exists. Without it, an existing file is refused and left as it is.

fields.name: path
fields.description: Where to write it: a `.json` file.

fields.name: provenance
fields.description: Where the entries come from, saved with each entry.

library.export.reason: not in the live demo: it needs Mechvane's own handling on the server (install Mechvane to use it)

library.inspect.label: Inspect Local Library
library.inspect.help: path: v1/v2 library JSON; returns validated catalog and exact entry revisions, without changing the design
library.inspect.description: Read a local library file and check it, without changing the design.

fields.name: path
fields.description: The library file (`solidcraft-library/1` or `/2` JSON, at most 4 MiB).

library.inspect.reason: not in the live demo: it needs Mechvane's own handling on the server (install Mechvane to use it)

material.assign.label: Physical Material
material.assign.help: bodies: [names]; material: name (Steel, Aluminum, ABS Plastic, …, or one made with material.create; `material.list`)
material.assign.description:
Give bodies a physical material (a built-in one, or one made with `material.create`), which
their mass and density come from. One undo step.

fields.name: bodies
fields.description: The bodies, by name: one or a list, at least one, each an existing body.

fields.name: material
fields.description:
The material's name (Steel, Aluminum, ABS Plastic, …, or one made with `material.create`;
`material.list` lists them). Letter case and spaces at either end don't matter.

material.create.label: New Physical Material
material.create.help: name (not a built-in material's); density_g_cm3: (0, 1000]; appearance?: library name (appearance.library) | color?: "#rrggbb" or [r, g, b] (0–255), opacity? (0–1), pbr?: {metallic:0..1, roughness:0.045..1, dielectric_ior:1..3} (opaque only, needs color/appearance): the default look. A named appearance keeps its preset response when pbr is omitted; pbr: null selects scalar shading. Optical edits do not change density. physical_card?: validated SI candidate record (null/omitted means unknown); card density never changes assigned density. Assign it with material.assign
material.create.description:
Define a physical material in this design: a name, a density and an optional default look
and physical card. Assign it with `material.assign`. One undo step.

fields.name: appearance
fields.description: The look, a library appearance by name (see `appearance.library`). Not with `color`.

fields.name: color
fields.description: The look's colour, `"#rrggbb"` or [r, g, b] (0–255), not with `appearance`. `null` clears the material's look, so its bodies show the default.

fields.name: density_g_cm3
fields.description: The density in g/cm³: above 0 and at most 1000.

fields.name: name
fields.description:
The new material's name: 1 to 128 characters, not a built-in material's or another of the
design's (letter case doesn't matter). Spaces at either end are dropped.

fields.name: opacity
fields.description: 0 (clear) to 1 (opaque).

fields.name: pbr
fields.description: The look's opaque PBR response; it needs `appearance` or `color`, and an opaque look. `null` selects scalar shading. Left out, a library appearance keeps its own response.

fields.name: physical_card
fields.description: A validated physical material card in SI units (see docs/physical-material-cards.md). The card's density never changes the assigned density. `null`: no card (an edit clears it). Left out: none for a new material; an edit keeps the current one.

material.delete.label: Delete Physical Material
material.delete.help: material: a material defined in this design; replace?: material for the bodies and configuration cells that use it (without it, a material in use is refused)
material.delete.description: Delete a physical material this design defines. One undo step.

fields.name: material
fields.description: A material, by name (letter case doesn't matter).

fields.name: replace
fields.description:
Another material, built-in or this design's, for the bodies and configuration cells that
use the deleted one. Without it, a material in use is refused.

material.edit.label: Edit Physical Material
material.edit.help: material: a material defined in this design; name? (bodies and configuration cells follow); density_g_cm3?; appearance? | color?, opacity?, pbr? (as material.create; color: null clears the look). physical_card?: validated SI candidate record (omitted retains, null clears). Omitted appearance/color retains the entire current look
material.edit.description:
Change a physical material this design defines: its name (its bodies and configuration cells
follow), its density, its look or its card. A key left out keeps what the material has; with
no look key at all, the whole look is kept. One undo step.

fields.name: appearance
fields.description: The new look, a library appearance by name. Not with `color`.

fields.name: color
fields.description: The look's colour, `"#rrggbb"` or [r, g, b] (0–255), not with `appearance`. `null` clears the material's look, so its bodies show the default.

fields.name: density_g_cm3
fields.description: The density in g/cm³: above 0 and at most 1000.

fields.name: material
fields.description: A material, by name (letter case doesn't matter).

fields.name: name
fields.description: Its new name, as for `material.create`.

fields.name: opacity
fields.description: 0 (clear) to 1 (opaque).

fields.name: pbr
fields.description: The look's opaque PBR response; it needs `appearance` or `color`, and an opaque look. `null` selects scalar shading. Left out, a library appearance keeps its own response.

fields.name: physical_card
fields.description: A validated physical material card in SI units (see docs/physical-material-cards.md). The card's density never changes the assigned density. `null`: no card (an edit clears it). Left out: none for a new material; an edit keeps the current one.

material.inspect.label: Inspect Physical Material
material.inspect.help: material: built-in or design-owned name. Returns assigned density, default appearance, optional physical_card, validation and density comparison. Read-only; missing engineering data remains unknown and card density does not change mass
material.inspect.description:
Read a material, built-in or this design's: its density, default look and physical card,
with the card's check and how its density compares. The design doesn't change.

fields.name: material
fields.description: A material, by name (letter case doesn't matter).

material.list.label: List Materials
material.list.help: → built-in and design-owned materials (user: true, look, optional physical_card/physical_validation/density_comparison). Read-only; candidate engineering records do not certify sources or supply a solver

material.properties.directional.label: Directional Elastic Modulus
material.properties.directional.help: card: schema_version 1 engineering material card; direction: three finite nonzero-vector components in the card's material-local axes. Returns normalized direction, Young modulus in Pa and source/condition review. Read-only constitutive query; no structural solver, persistence or body-axis assignment. See docs/physical-material-cards.md
material.properties.directional.description:
The Young modulus of an engineering material card in one direction, in the card's own
material axes. Read-only: no load case or structural solver.

fields.name: card
fields.description: A schema_version 1 engineering material card in SI units (see docs/physical-material-cards.md).

fields.name: direction
fields.description: A direction in the card's material axes: three numbers, not all zero.

material.properties.validate.label: Validate Physical Material Data
material.properties.validate.help: card: schema_version 1 engineering material card in SI units. Returns numerical consistency, derived isotropic moduli, missing conditions and sources needing review. Read-only; does not assign/save properties or provide an analysis solver. See docs/physical-material-cards.md
material.properties.validate.description:
Check an engineering material card: its numbers' consistency, the isotropic moduli they
imply, and the conditions and sources still to review. Read-only: nothing is assigned or
saved, and there is no analysis solver.

fields.name: card
fields.description: A schema_version 1 engineering material card in SI units (see docs/physical-material-cards.md).

mesh.convert.label: Convert Mesh
mesh.convert.help: body?: mesh body name (default: the selected mesh body); tolerance?: length expression (default 0.05 mm): rebuild a closed mesh as an editable solid — a constant-section part as planar and cylindrical faces, any other closed mesh as the faceted solid its triangles describe — with a parametric timeline feature in the mesh body's owning component (the active component must be that component or an ancestor; otherwise activate the named component first); the active component is unchanged; name?
mesh.convert.description:
Rebuild a closed mesh body as an editable solid, with a parametric feature in the timeline.
The solid keeps the mesh body's name and colour.

Whether the body exists and is a mesh, and whether the active component may edit it, stay the
handler's to check. The kernel checks the tolerance's range when the feature evaluates, so an
expression is taken here whatever its value.

fields.name: body
fields.description:
The mesh body, by name. Default: the one selected body. A blank name also means the
selected body, as the handler reads it.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, which every feature records; each an existing body or `*`. A
conversion changes only `body`, whatever this lists.

fields.name: tolerance
fields.description:
How far the rebuilt faces may stray from the mesh's triangles: a run of facets within it of
an arc becomes a cylinder. From 0.000001 mm to 1 mm. Default: 0.05 mm.

model.body_features.label: List Body Features
model.body_features.help: body?: name (a placed copy's name means the body it shows; default every body) → bodies: [{body, features: [{id, name}]}], in timeline order the feature that created each body, every later one that changed it, and those of bodies consumed into it. Read-only
model.body_features.description: List the timeline features that built each body (#11945).

fields.name: body
fields.description: One body, by name (a placed copy's name means the body it shows); every body when left out.

model.edges.label: List Edges
model.edges.description: List a body's edges or faces, with what picks each one.

fields.name: body
fields.description: The body, by name.

model.faces.label: List Faces
model.faces.help: body: name → per face: index, name (what face.delete, sheet.convert `face`, solid.shell … take in place of a point), exact, area, centroid (not always on the face), plane_normal, point (a point on the face that picks it), cylinder? ({origin, axis, radius} of a cylindrical face), sheet_face? (a folded sheet's face: `sheet:<body>:<panel>:<side>`, panel base or a flange's tag F<feature>.<k>, side top | bottom | rim.<edge> | bend.inner | bend.outer; taken wherever a face name is, and it holds while sizes change and flanges come and go)
model.faces.description: List a body's edges or faces, with what picks each one.

fields.name: body
fields.description: The body, by name.

model.mesh.label: Read Body Mesh
model.mesh.help: body, tolerance?: finite positive chord tolerance in mm (default 0.05); evaluated component-local mesh, at most 8192 vertices and 16384 triangles; no files or model changes
model.mesh.description: Read a body's evaluated triangle mesh in its owning component's coordinates (millimetres).

fields.name: tolerance
fields.description: Chord tolerance in mm. Default: 0.05; must be finite and positive.

motion.delete.label: Delete Motion Study
motion.delete.description: Delete a motion study. One undo step.

fields.name: study
fields.description: The motion study, by id (a number) or name. A number is looked up as an id first, text as a name first.

motion.export.label: Export Motion Study
motion.export.help: study; samples? (default steps + 1); path? (.json or .csv) → occurrence positions per step (the design is not changed)
motion.export.description:
Export the occurrences' positions at evenly spaced steps of a motion study, as the reply or
written to a file. It plays the study on a copy: the design is not changed.

fields.name: path
fields.description:
A file to write the samples to: CSV when it ends in `.csv` (one row per occurrence per
sample), JSON otherwise. The reply then gives the path and the number of samples. Blank
text is read as no path. Default: the reply carries the samples.

fields.name: samples
fields.description: How many samples, evenly spaced from the first step to the last: 2 to 10 000 (a fraction is cut to a whole number). Default: one per step, at most 10 000.

fields.name: study
fields.description: The motion study, by id (a number) or name. A number is looked up as an id first, text as a name first.

motion.export.reason: not in the live demo: it needs Mechvane's own handling on the server (install Mechvane to use it)

motion.export_animation.label: Export Motion Animation
motion.export_animation.help: study: id|name, or joint: id|name with from and to (degrees for angles, mm for distances, or expressions) and index?, or view: id|name (an exploded view, coming apart from the assembled placement) with back? (default false; true: back together too, exploded at the middle frame of an odd count); path: a .gif file, or a folder for PNG frames (frame-0001.png, frame-0002.png, …); samples? (frames, 2…1000; default the study's steps + 1, 100 for a joint, 41 for a view or 81 with back); width?, height? (16…4096 pixels, default 800 × 500); camera?: {target, yaw, pitch, roll?, distance, fov?, up?} (ui.camera's reply; fields left out keep the default view: view.apply's camera, or the home view framing the model, for a view both assembled and exploded); fps? (1…50, default 20); grid?, axes? (default true: the ground grid and the origin's axes) - draws the study as it plays, the joint as it is driven or the view as it explodes, with the headless renderer → path, format, frames, width, height, fps (GIF), bytes, renderer, stopped_at, stopped_by_loop, stopped_by_contact (the design is not changed, nor its placements)
motion.export_animation.description: Draw a motion as an animation, frame by frame with the headless renderer: a motion study played (`study`), one joint driven from `from` to `to` (`joint`), or an exploded view coming apart (`view`, and back together with `back`). Written as an animated GIF, or as a folder of PNG frames. The design is not changed, nor its placements.

fields.name: axes
fields.description: Draw the origin's axes. Default: true.

fields.name: back
fields.description: With `view`: true comes back together too, exploded at the middle frame of an odd count. Default: false.

fields.name: camera
fields.description: The camera the frames are drawn from: fields of ui.camera's reply. Fields left out keep the default view: view.apply's camera, or the home view framing the model (for an exploded view, both assembled and exploded). Angles in radians.

fields.name: fps
fields.description: A GIF's frames per second, 1…50. A GIF counts in hundredths of a second, so the reply's `fps` is the rate it plays at. Default: 20.

fields.name: from
fields.description: With `joint`: the value the motion starts at, a number (degrees for an angle, mm for a distance, between -1e9 and 1e9) or an expression such as "width / 2" or "30 deg". Not read without a joint.

fields.name: grid
fields.description: Draw the ground grid. Default: true.

fields.name: height
fields.description: The frames' height in pixels, 16…4096 (rounded). Default: 500.

fields.name: index
fields.description: With `joint`: which of its values to drive, below its value count. Default: 0. Not read without a joint.

fields.name: joint
fields.description: A joint, by id (a number) or name, driven from `from` to `to`; a rigid joint doesn't move. Instead of `view` or `study`.

fields.name: path
fields.description: A .gif file, or a folder for the PNG frames (frame-0001.png, frame-0002.png, …), made where missing; frames of an earlier export there are removed first. Not one .png file. At most 4096 bytes (the schema counts characters), with no control characters.

fields.name: samples
fields.description: How many frames, 2…1000, with at most 2^26 pixels in all for a GIF and 2^30 for PNG frames, so fewer for big frames (4 at 4096 × 4096 for a GIF). Default: the study's steps + 1, 100 for a joint, 41 for an exploded view (81 with `back`).

fields.name: study
fields.description: A motion study, by id (a number) or name, played from start to end. A number is looked up as an id first, text as a name first. Instead of `view` or `joint`.

fields.name: to
fields.description: With `joint`: the value the motion ends at, a number (degrees for an angle, mm for a distance, between -1e9 and 1e9) or an expression such as "width / 2" or "30 deg". Not read without a joint.

fields.name: view
fields.description: An exploded view, by id (a number) or name: the parts coming apart from where they are assembled. Instead of `study` or `joint`.

fields.name: width
fields.description: The frames' width in pixels, 16…4096 (rounded). Default: 800.

motion.export_animation.reason: not in the live demo: it needs Mechvane's own handling on the server (install Mechvane to use it)

motion.interference.label: Motion Interference
motion.interference.help: study: id|name; occurrences?: [ids or names] (two or more, checked against each other; default every occurrence), with against?: [ids or names] (then each of `occurrences` is checked only against these, such as an arm against the parts it must miss), or contact_sets?: true (the pairs of the design's contact sets); exclude_pairs?: [[a, b]] (occurrences by id or name: pairs of bodies under a and b are not checked); samples? (2…1000, default the study's steps + 1); budget_s?: seconds (above 0, at most 86400; default a fixed work budget): the time the check may take instead, looked at between samples, for a mechanism such as a gear train that needs longer → collisions: [{a, b, first_step, last_step, steps: [[from, to]…] (the step ranges where they overlap), volume_mm3 (the most volume they share at a sample, worked out exactly from the bodies), deepest_step (the first sample sharing that volume), not_measured (null, or why the volume was not worked out at every sample they overlap, such as a budget it ran past: then volume_mm3 and deepest_step are null, never an estimate), depth_mm (how far into each other at most: an estimate from points of the bodies' contact meshes, not exact)}], clear (every sample checked and none collide; never while truncated), pairs (checked), samples (taken), truncated (the work budget, or budget_s, ran out; checked_to: the last step checked), budget_s (when given), stopped_at, stopped_by_loop. The study plays as motion.play plays it but contact sets do not stop it, on a copy (the design is not changed). Parts are tested at the samples only: one that passes wholly through another between two samples is missed
motion.interference.description:
Play a motion study on a copy of the design and find the pairs of parts that pass into each
other along it, with the steps where they overlap. Contact sets don't stop it. Parts are
tested at the samples only: one that passes wholly through another between two samples is
missed. The design is not changed.

fields.name: against
fields.description:
The parts that must be missed: each of `occurrences` is checked only against these.
Default (or `null`): none.

fields.name: budget_s
fields.description:
The seconds the check may take (above 0, at most 86400), looked at between samples, for
a mechanism that needs longer than the fixed work budget. Default (or `null`): that
budget.

fields.name: contact_sets
fields.description: Check the pairs of the design's contact sets instead (not with `occurrences`).

fields.name: exclude_pairs
fields.description:
Pairs left out, such as a pin in its hole: `[a, b]`, each an occurrence's id or name; a
pair of bodies is left out when one is under `a` and the other under `b`. Default: none.

fields.name: occurrences
fields.description: Occurrences, each by id (a number) or name; not the root.

fields.name: samples
fields.description: How many samples, from 2 to 1000 (rounded). Default: the study's steps + 1.

fields.name: study
fields.description: The motion study, by id (a number) or name. A number is looked up as an id first, text as a name first.

motion.list.label: List Motion Studies
motion.list.description:
List the design's motion studies, each with its keys in the units `motion.study` takes, and its
associative traces. Nothing is changed.

motion.play.label: Play Motion Study
motion.play.help: study: id|name; step (0…steps) — sets the joints to the study's values there (contact sets stop them); quiet?: bool (positions of only the occurrences that moved) → values: [{joint, values: [{name, value, unit}]}], positions, moved: whether any occurrence moved, unmoved: [{joint, name, reason}] (keyed joints that can move nothing, such as a chain joined to nothing grounded)
motion.play.description:
Play a motion study: set its joints to the study's values at one step (contact sets stop them
where parts would pass through each other), and report where the parts went. One undo step.

fields.name: quiet
fields.description: True: `positions` lists only the occurrences that moved. Default: false, every occurrence.

fields.name: step
fields.description: The step to play to: 0 to the study's `steps` (a number outside is taken to the nearer end; a fraction falls between two steps).

fields.name: study
fields.description: The motion study, by id (a number) or name. A number is looked up as an id first, text as a name first.

motion.plot.label: Plot Motion Study
motion.plot.help: study: id|name; joints?: [id|name] (default: every joint that moves); occurrence? and point? (a point of a part to follow, as motion.trace takes them); samples? (3…1000, default the study's steps + 1); duration?: seconds the whole study takes, 0.001 or more (velocities and accelerations then per second, else per step) → step: [the study step of each sample], time?: [s], joints: [{joint, name, index, dof, unit, value, velocity, acceleration, velocity_unit, acceleration_unit}] (degrees for angles, mm for distances; angles unwrapped), point?: {occurrence, position: [[x,y,z]…], velocity, acceleration (vectors), speed, acceleration_norm, unit, velocity_unit, acceleration_unit}, samples (taken), stopped_at, stopped_by_loop, stopped_by_contact. The study plays as motion.play plays it, each sample driven from the one before, on a copy (the design is not changed); velocities and accelerations are finite differences between samples (central, one-sided at the ends)
motion.plot.description:
Play a motion study on a copy of the design and plot each joint value, with its velocity
and acceleration (finite differences between samples), and optionally the path of a point of
a part. The study plays as `motion.play` plays it, contact sets included. The design is not
changed.

fields.name: duration
fields.description:
The seconds the whole study takes, 0.001 or more: velocities and accelerations are then
per second, and the reply has `time`. Default (or `null`): per step.

fields.name: joints
fields.description:
The joints to plot, each by id or name: every value of each. Default (or `null`): every
joint that isn't suppressed.

fields.name: occurrence
fields.description:
The part whose point to follow: an occurrence by id or name, or a path of occurrence ids.
Given with `point`.

fields.name: point
fields.description:
The point to follow, [x, y, z] in world mm where the part is now. Given with
`occurrence`.

fields.name: samples
fields.description: How many samples, from 3 to 1000 (rounded). Default: the study's steps + 1.

fields.name: study
fields.description: The motion study, by id (a number) or name. A number is looked up as an id first, text as a name first.

motion.study.label: Motion Study
motion.study.help: name?; study? (edit an existing one); steps? (timeline length, default 100); keys: [{joint, index?, points: [[step, value], …]}] (values: degrees for angles, mm for distances, or expressions)
motion.study.description:
Make a motion study, which drives joints along a timeline of steps: each key gives one value of
one joint at some steps, linear in between and held before the first and after the last. With
`study`, change that study instead. One undo step.

fields.name: keys
fields.description: The study's keys, replacing any it has (at most 1000). Each drives one value of one joint: `joint` by id or name, `index` the value (0 for a revolute's angle; default 0), and `points` as [step, value] pairs (1 to 10 000), a value being degrees for an angle and mm for a distance, or an expression.

fields.name: name
fields.description:
The study's name; blank text keeps it. Default for a new one: "Motion Study" and the first
number no study's name has.

fields.name: steps
fields.description: How many steps the timeline has: 1 to 100 000 (a fraction rounds). Default for a new one: 100.

fields.name: study
fields.description: A study to change, by id (a number) or name; left out, a new one is made.

motion.trace.label: Motion Trace
motion.trace.help: occurrence: id|name, or an occurrence path [ids] (an instance inside sub-assemblies); point: [x,y,z] world point on it, where it is placed now; study: id|name, or joint: id|name with from and to (degrees for angles, mm for distances, or expressions) and index? (which value, default 0); samples? (2…500, default the study's steps + 1, or 100) - the point's path as the study plays or the joint is driven, closed loops following → points: [[x,y,z]…] world positions, samples (taken), stopped_at (the sample where the motion stopped short; the trace ends there), stopped_by_loop, stopped_by_contact (the design is not changed)
motion.trace.description:
Trace a point on a part as a motion study plays or a joint is driven, on a copy: the design is
not changed.

fields.name: from
fields.description: A number (degrees for an angle, mm for a distance; below 1e9 in size), or an expression (text) over the design's parameters, such as "width / 2" or "30 deg".

fields.name: index
fields.description:
With `joint`: which of its values is driven (0 for a revolute's angle), below the joint's
value count. Default: 0.

fields.name: joint
fields.description: A joint's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: occurrence
fields.description: The part the point is on: an occurrence's id (a number) or name (0 or "root": the root), at its first placement, or an occurrence path of ids (one instance inside sub-assemblies, at most 64).

fields.name: point
fields.description: The traced point, in world coordinates (mm) where the parts are placed now: [x, y, z] or {x, y, z}, smaller than 1e7 mm from the origin.

fields.name: samples
fields.description: How many points the motion is sampled at: 2 to 500 (a fraction rounds). Default: the study's steps + 1, or 100 for a joint.

fields.name: study
fields.description: The motion study, by id (a number) or name. A number is looked up as an id first, text as a name first.

fields.name: to
fields.description: A number (degrees for an angle, mm for a distance; below 1e9 in size), or an expression (text) over the design's parameters, such as "width / 2" or "30 deg".

motion.trace.edit.label: Edit Motion Trace
motion.trace.edit.help: sketch: id|name; joint? with from and to, or study?; index?; samples? (2…500); auto_update?: false to detach. Edits a saved associative trace's driving conditions in one undo step
motion.trace.edit.description:
Change a kept associative trace's motion or sample count, or detach it, in one undo step.
`study` or `joint` replaces the motion; `from`, `to` and `index` alone change a joint motion's.

fields.name: auto_update
fields.description: False: the trace stops following, and its spline stays a fixed curve. Default: true.

fields.name: from
fields.description: A number (degrees for an angle, mm for a distance; below 1e9 in size), or an expression (text) over the design's parameters, such as "width / 2" or "30 deg".

fields.name: index
fields.description:
With `joint`: which of its values is driven (0 for a revolute's angle), below the joint's
value count. Default: 0.

fields.name: joint
fields.description: A joint's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: samples
fields.description: How many points the motion is sampled at: 2 to 500 (a fraction rounds). Default: the study's steps + 1, or 100 for a joint.

fields.name: sketch
fields.description: The sketch Keep Motion Trace made, by id (a number) or name, which must still have its associative trace.

fields.name: study
fields.description: The motion study, by id (a number) or name. A number is looked up as an id first, text as a name first.

fields.name: to
fields.description: A number (degrees for an angle, mm for a distance; below 1e9 in size), or an expression (text) over the design's parameters, such as "width / 2" or "30 deg".

motion.trace.keep.label: Keep Motion Trace
motion.trace.keep.help: occurrence: id|name, or an occurrence path [ids] (an instance inside sub-assemblies); point: [x,y,z] world point on it, where it is placed now; study: id|name, or joint: id|name with from and to (degrees for angles, mm for distances, or expressions) and index? (which value, default 0); samples? (2…500, default the study's steps + 1, or 100) - the point's path as the study plays or the joint is driven, closed loops following; name? (default Motion TraceN); auto_update?: bool (default true); point_ref?: joint origin snap - keeps the trace as a root 3D sketch spline. Associative curves follow mechanism and driving-input edits; false keeps a fixed curve. point_ref retains a geometry snap; otherwise point is retained in component coordinates → sketch, name, curves, points
motion.trace.keep.description: Keep a trace as a spline in a new 3D sketch of the root component. One undo step.

fields.name: auto_update
fields.description:
True: the spline follows later edits of the mechanism and of the motion. False: a fixed
curve. Default: true.

fields.name: from
fields.description: A number (degrees for an angle, mm for a distance; below 1e9 in size), or an expression (text) over the design's parameters, such as "width / 2" or "30 deg".

fields.name: index
fields.description:
With `joint`: which of its values is driven (0 for a revolute's angle), below the joint's
value count. Default: 0.

fields.name: joint
fields.description: A joint's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: name
fields.description:
The new sketch's name; blank text is read as no name. Default: "Motion Trace" and the
first number no feature's name has.

fields.name: occurrence
fields.description: The part the point is on: an occurrence's id (a number) or name (0 or "root": the root), at its first placement, or an occurrence path of ids (one instance inside sub-assemblies, at most 64).

fields.name: point
fields.description: The traced point, in world coordinates (mm) where the parts are placed now: [x, y, z] or {x, y, z}, smaller than 1e7 mm from the origin.

fields.name: point_ref
fields.description:
With `auto_update`: the traced point as a joint origin snap on the traced occurrence, kept
in place of `point` (it must resolve to `point`). Default: `point` in the occurrence's
coordinates.

fields.name: samples
fields.description: How many points the motion is sampled at: 2 to 500 (a fraction rounds). Default: the study's steps + 1, or 100 for a joint.

fields.name: study
fields.description: The motion study, by id (a number) or name. A number is looked up as an id first, text as a name first.

fields.name: to
fields.description: A number (degrees for an angle, mm for a distance; below 1e9 in size), or an expression (text) over the design's parameters, such as "width / 2" or "30 deg".

note.add.label: Add Note
note.add.help: anchor?: [x,y,z] (the point in model space, mm; without it, where the selection points, or the origin); text: the note (may span lines); hidden?: bool (saved but not drawn) → note: id
note.add.description: Anchor a new note to a point in model space.

fields.name: anchor
fields.description: A point in mm: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}.

fields.name: hidden
fields.description: Save the note hidden: kept with the design but not drawn.

fields.name: text
fields.description: The note's text (may span lines).

fields.name: note
fields.description: The note's id.

note.list.label: List Notes
note.list.help: → notes: [{id, anchor: [x,y,z], text, hidden}] in creation order

note.update.label: Edit Note
note.update.help: note: id; text?: the new text; anchor?: [x,y,z] (move the anchor); hidden?: bool (show or hide) → note: id
note.update.description: Change a note's text, anchor, or hidden flag.

fields.name: anchor
fields.description: The new anchor point: `[x, y, z]` (mm).

fields.name: hidden
fields.description: Show or hide the note.

fields.name: note
fields.description: The note's id.

fields.name: text
fields.description: The new text (may span lines).

occurrence.align.label: Align Occurrence
occurrence.align.help: occurrence?, occurrences?, path?, paths?: placements to move together; from | from_face | from_plane; to | to_face | to_plane; flip?: bool; capture?: bool (default true); move_grounded?: bool (default false). Moves only the chosen occurrence placements in world coordinates without changing shared component geometry; a placement inside a component placed more than once moves in every placement of it, and the reply's `shared` lists those paths
occurrence.align.description:
Align one or more component occurrence placements in world coordinates without modifying
shared component geometry.

fields.name: capture
fields.description: Capture the aligned position immediately (default: `true`); `false` leaves it pending.

fields.name: flip
fields.description: Flip face/plane normal alignment so normals point the same way instead of meeting opposite.

fields.name: from
fields.description: A world point [x, y, z], "origin", or a snap point {"snap": "vertex"|"edge_mid"|"face_center"|"circle_center", "at": [x, y, z]}.

fields.name: from_face
fields.description: A point in mm: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}.

fields.name: from_plane
fields.description: XY, XZ, YZ, a construction plane name or feature id, or an explicit plane {origin?, normal} / {origin?, x_dir, y_dir}.

fields.name: move_grounded
fields.description: Allow aligning a grounded occurrence while keeping it grounded (default: `false`).

fields.name: occurrence
fields.description: A feature's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: occurrences
fields.description: An occurrence id/name, or 1 to 64 occurrence ids/names.

fields.name: path
fields.description: An exact placement path: 1 to 64 occurrence ids from the root down.

fields.name: paths
fields.description: 1 to 64 exact occurrence placement paths.

fields.name: to
fields.description: A world point [x, y, z], "origin", or a snap point {"snap": "vertex"|"edge_mid"|"face_center"|"circle_center", "at": [x, y, z]}.

fields.name: to_face
fields.description: A point in mm: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}.

fields.name: to_plane
fields.description: XY, XZ, YZ, a construction plane name or feature id, or an explicit plane {origin?, normal} / {origin?, x_dir, y_dir}.

occurrence.copy.label: Paste (Instance)
occurrence.copy.help: component (or occurrence): what to place again; path?: validates selected occurrence; parent?: component (default: the same parent); translate?: [x,y,z]; in_place?: bool (default false: the selected transform within the parent; true: where the selected placement is in the world, translate in world axes; a parent placed more than once is placed by parent_path?, else the active placement, and every instance gets the copy). Copies the selected effective transform, including pending moves
occurrence.copy.description:
Place a component again (Paste as an instance): a new occurrence of the same component, which
shares its contents, at the selected placement's transform (pending moves included) moved by
`translate`. Give the `occurrence` to copy, or the `component`.

fields.name: component
fields.description: A component's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: in_place
fields.description:
`false`: the copy has the selected transform within its parent. `true`: it sits where the
selected placement is in the world, and `translate` is along the world axes. Default:
`false`.

fields.name: occurrence
fields.description: An occurrence's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: parent
fields.description: A component's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: parent_path
fields.description: An exact placement path: up to 64 occurrence ids from the root down; empty for the design itself.

fields.name: path
fields.description: An exact placement path: 1 to 64 occurrence ids from the root down.

fields.name: translate
fields.description: A point in mm: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}.

occurrence.drag.label: Drag Occurrence
occurrence.drag.help: occurrence or path: exact placement; at: [x,y,z] world point on it; point: [x,y,z] where it goes. Moves the placement by point - at (with any chain of joints it is in that is joined to nothing grounded) and captures its position; other pending moves stay pending. Shared definitions move in all placements. Grounded parts and parts joints hold to something fixed are refused (joint.reach moves those)
occurrence.drag.description:
Drag a placement by `point - at`, in world coordinates, and capture its position: the grabbed
point `at` goes to `point`. Any chain of joints it is in that is joined to nothing grounded
moves with it; other pending moves stay pending; shared definitions move in all their
placements. Grounded parts and parts that joints hold to something fixed are refused
(`joint.reach` moves those).

fields.name: at
fields.description: A point in mm: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}.

fields.name: continuous
fields.description:
Reply `continuous`, for a drag that goes on over several calls (the viewport's). It
changes nothing else. Default: `false`.

fields.name: occurrence
fields.description: An occurrence's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: path
fields.description: An exact placement path: 1 to 64 occurrence ids from the root down.

fields.name: point
fields.description: A point in mm: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}.

occurrence.ground.label: Ground
occurrence.ground.description:
Ground a placement, or let it go (a grounded part stays where it is when joints move
things). Without `grounded` it toggles.

fields.name: grounded
fields.description: `true` grounds it, `false` frees it. Default: toggle.

fields.name: occurrence
fields.description: An occurrence's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: path
fields.description: An exact placement path: 1 to 64 occurrence ids from the root down.

occurrence.move.label: Move Occurrence
occurrence.move.help: occurrence; path?: exact placement; space?: local|world (default local); translate?: [x,y,z] (numbers or length expressions: an occurrence moved by expressions that name parameters keeps them and moves with them when the parameters change, along the axes the move was given in; other moves of it stay; a parameter they use can't be deleted, and a renamed one carries into them); axis?: [x,y,z], angle?: radians or "30 deg", origin?: [x,y,z] (numbers or length expressions, kept like translate's: the point the turn is about moves the part by what the turn leaves behind when a parameter in it changes); to?: {position: [x,y,z], axis?: [x,y,z], angle?} or to_matrix?: [12 or 16 numbers] (absolute placement: where it goes in space, not a move; not with translate/axis/angle/origin/matrix); matrix?: [12 or 16 numbers] (instead of translate/axis/angle/origin: a rigid move as a row-major 3x4 rotation-and-translation or 4x4 matrix, flat or as rows, its translation column (entries 4, 8 and 12) numbers or length expressions that are kept and followed like translate's; one that is a rotation only up to rounding is orthonormalised, a scale, shear or mirror is refused); tolerance?: largest accepted |RᵀR − I| (default 1e-9, at most 1e-3); capture?: bool (default true; false keeps it pending until Capture Position); move_grounded?: bool (default false: a grounded occurrence refuses; true moves it and it stays grounded). Nested occurrence definitions remain shared. Replies {occurrence, transform, pending}; when joints hold it to something fixed and put it back, transform is where it is and the reply adds reverted: true and a warning naming the joint
occurrence.move.description:
Move an occurrence: by `translate`, or turned by `angle` about `axis` through `origin`, or by
a rigid `matrix` instead of those. Nested occurrences' definitions stay shared. A grounded
occurrence refuses unless `move_grounded` is true. When joints hold it to something fixed and
put it back, the reply says so (`reverted`).

fields.name: angle
fields.description: An angle in radians (a number) or an angle expression such as "30 deg".

fields.name: axis
fields.description: A point in mm: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}.

fields.name: base_transform
fields.description: A 4x4 matrix as 4 columns of 4 numbers, as a placement's `transform` is given (the translation is the last column): finite, affine (the fourth number of the first three columns is 0, of the last column 1) and invertible.

fields.name: capture
fields.description:
`true` makes the move the occurrence's placement now; `false` keeps it pending until
`component.capture_position`. Default: `true`.

fields.name: matrix
fields.description: A rigid move as a row-major 3x4 (12 numbers) or 4x4 (16 numbers) matrix, flat or as 3 or 4 rows of 4. The translation column (the 4th entry of each of the first three rows) may be a number in mm or a length expression; one that names a parameter is kept, and the occurrence follows the parameter.

fields.name: move_grounded
fields.description: `true` moves a grounded occurrence, which stays grounded. Default: `false`, which refuses.

fields.name: occurrence
fields.description: An occurrence's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: origin
fields.description: A point: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}, each a number in mm or a length expression.

fields.name: path
fields.description: An exact placement path: 1 to 64 occurrence ids from the root down.

fields.name: space
fields.description: Which frame `occurrence.move` reads its move in: `local` or `world`.

fields.name: to
fields.description:
Absolute placement (#12150): where the occurrence goes in `space`, not a move. Not with
`translate`, `axis`, `angle`, `origin`, `matrix`, `to_matrix` or `base_transform`.

fields.name: to_matrix
fields.description: A rigid move as a row-major 3x4 (12 numbers) or 4x4 (16 numbers) matrix, flat or as 3 or 4 rows of 4.

fields.name: tolerance
fields.description:
With `matrix` or `to_matrix`: the largest accepted |RᵀR − I| per entry. Default: 1e-9.
Read only with those.

fields.name: translate
fields.description: A point: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}, each a number in mm or a length expression.

occurrence.properties.label: Occurrence Physical Properties
occurrence.properties.help: occurrence: id or name; path?: [occurrence ids] (required if nested under multiple instances); descendants?: bool (default true); about?: [x, y, z] (mm). Physical properties of this placement in world coordinates, including pending moves; volume, density, mass, center of mass and inertia_g_mm2 only for closed, consistently oriented bodies; total.open_bodies_skipped counts open bodies excluded from volume/mass totals; total inertia as in component.properties
occurrence.properties.description:
Measure an occurrence where its placement puts it, in world coordinates, with what is inside
it unless `descendants` is false: material-aware mass and centre of mass, and volume, density
and inertia for closed, consistently oriented bodies, with totals and principal moments.
Pending moves are included. The design is not changed.

fields.name: about
fields.description: A point in mm, also given the total inertia about it (`total.inertia_about`).

fields.name: descendants
fields.description: Include the placements inside it. Default: `true`.

fields.name: occurrence
fields.description: An occurrence's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: path
fields.description: An exact placement path: 1 to 64 occurrence ids from the root down.

occurrence.reparent.label: Move to Component
occurrence.reparent.help: occurrence; path?: exact placement; parent: component id or name (0 or "root" for the design); parent_path?: the parent's placement to place it by (default: its only one, else the active one; every instance of the parent gets it). The placement keeps its world position; a move that would break a feature is refused

fields.description: occurrence; path?: exact placement; parent: component id or name (0 or "root" for the design); parent_path?: the parent's placement to place it by (default: its only one, else the active one; every instance of the parent gets it). The placement keeps its world position; a move that would break a feature is refused

parameters.add.label: Add User Parameter
parameters.add.help: name, expression, unit?: as parameters.change (text: a text parameter, its expression the text), comment?, favorite?: bool
parameters.add.description:
Add a user parameter: a named number with a unit, or a named text. Features, sketches and
other parameters can use it by name. One undo step.

fields.name: comment
fields.description: A note to show with it.

fields.name: expression
fields.description: The value: a number, or an expression as text (`25 mm`, `W / 2`). For a text parameter, its text; quotes round it are optional.

fields.name: favorite
fields.description: List it with the favourites, first. Default: false.

fields.name: name
fields.description:
The new parameter's name: a letter or `_`, then letters, digits or `_`; not a unit's,
function's or constant's name, nor another parameter's.

fields.name: unit
fields.description:
The unit: `mm`, `cm`, `m`, `in`, `ft`, `deg`, `rad`, `""` (no unit) or `text` (a text
parameter, whose expression is its text). Default: the expression's own unit, a length
in the design's units.

fields.name: value
fields.description: Another name for `expression`, read when `expression` isn't a number or text.

parameters.change.label: Change Parameters
parameters.change.help: name, expression (number or text), unit?: mm|cm|m|in|ft|deg|rad|""|text (new parameters default to their value's unit, a length the design's units; a text parameter's expression is its text, quotes round it optional: sketch texts' words are built from it), comment?, favorite?: bool, new_name?: rename (references follow; an expression `new = value` renames to `new` and sets value, or sets `new` when the expression is just `new`); or delete: name; or changes: {name: expression, …} (existing parameters, checked together and rebuilt once, all or nothing) → changed?: {name: value} (with changes), recomputed: features rebuilt, restored: features whose earlier result for the same inputs was reused (e.g. a value set back), switched?: [{feature, name, suppressed}] (the configuration rules that switch a feature's suppression and read a parameter whose value changed run in their order, as on activation; driven parameters and restrictions wait for a configuration edit or activation)
parameters.change.description: What `parameters.change` takes, in the form it's read in: see [`ParamChangeParams`].

fields.name: changes
fields.description:
Several existing parameters at once, `{name: expression}`: they are checked together and
the design is rebuilt once, all or nothing. Renaming isn't done this way. When given,
no other key is read.

fields.name: comment
fields.description: A note to show with the parameter.

fields.name: delete
fields.description:
Delete this user parameter (refused while something uses it). When given as text, no
other key but `changes` is read.

fields.name: expression
fields.description:
The new value: a number, or an expression as text (`25 mm`, `W / 2`). A text
parameter's expression is its text, quotes round it optional. `name = value` renames
the parameter to `name` and sets the value (or sets `name` when the value is just
`name`). Needed unless `new_name`, `favorite` or `comment` is given.

fields.name: favorite
fields.description: List it with the favourites, first, or not.

fields.name: name
fields.description:
The parameter to change, by name: a user parameter, a sketch dimension or a feature's
named input. Spaces at either end are dropped.

fields.name: new_name
fields.description:
Rename the parameter: the expressions, feature inputs and dimensions that use it follow.
With an `expression` the new value is set too.

fields.name: unit
fields.description:
The unit: `mm`, `cm`, `m`, `in`, `ft`, `deg`, `rad`, `""` (no unit) or `text`. Default:
the parameter's own, or for a new one its value's unit, a length in the design's units.

fields.name: value
fields.description: Another name for `expression`, read when `expression` isn't a number or text.

parameters.comment.label: Comment Parameter
parameters.comment.description: Set a parameter's comment, a note shown with it. One undo step.

fields.name: comment
fields.description: The comment; empty text clears it.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The parameter, by name.

parameters.complete.label: Complete Expression
parameters.complete.help: prefix?: the text before the cursor → word, suggestions [{text, kind: parameter|function|unit|constant, detail}]
parameters.complete.description:
Suggest completions for the word at the end of some expression text: parameters (by name,
anywhere in it), functions, constants and units. Changes nothing.

fields.name: prefix
fields.description:
The text before the cursor; the word being typed is its trailing letters, digits and
underscores. Default: empty, which lists every parameter, function and constant.

parameters.delete.label: Delete Parameter
parameters.delete.help: name (refused while something uses it; the error lists the users)
parameters.delete.description:
Delete a user parameter. It's refused while an expression, a feature input or a dimension
uses it; the message lists them. One undo step.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The parameter, by name.

parameters.export.label: Export Parameters
parameters.export.help: format?: csv|json (default csv, or from the path), path?: write to a file → text
parameters.export.description:
Export the user parameters as CSV or JSON text, and write it to a file when a path is
given. Changes nothing in the design.

fields.name: format
fields.description: `csv` or `json`, ignoring case. Default: `json` when `path` ends in `.json`, else `csv`.

fields.name: path
fields.description: A file to write the text to. Default: none is written.

parameters.export.reason: not in the live demo: it needs Mechvane's own handling on the server (install Mechvane to use it)

parameters.favorite.label: Favorite Parameter
parameters.favorite.description: Mark a parameter as a favourite, listed first, or unmark it. One undo step.

fields.name: favorite
fields.description: Whether it's a favourite. Default: true.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The parameter, by name.

parameters.graph.label: Parameter Graph
parameters.graph.help: → nodes, edges [user, used] (users include Feature:<name>), cycles, errors

parameters.import.label: Import Parameters
parameters.import.help: text: CSV (header with name, expression, unit?, comment?) or JSON [{name, expression, unit?, comment?}] | path; all or nothing
parameters.import.description: What `parameters.import` takes, as the handler reads it: see [`ParamImportParams`].

fields.name: path
fields.description: A file to read the table from, in the same forms. Read when `text` isn't given.

fields.name: text
fields.description:
The table as text: CSV with a header (`name`, `expression`, and optionally `unit` and
`comment`), or JSON `[{name, expression, unit?, comment?}]`. When given, `path` isn't
read.

parameters.import.reason: not in the live demo: it needs Mechvane's own handling on the server (install Mechvane to use it)

parameters.list.label: List Parameters
parameters.list.help: favorites?: bool (only favourites), filter?: all|user|sketch|feature|favorites → parameters (name, expression, unit, value (mm/deg in every reply), display_value (in its own unit), source, feature/input, comment, favorite, uses, used_by, error) and cycles
parameters.list.description:
List the parameters: the user's, the sketch dimensions' and the feature inputs', favourites
first, with each one's expression, value, uses and users, and any cycles. Changes nothing.

fields.name: favorites
fields.description: Only the favourites. When true, `filter` isn't read. Default: false.

fields.name: filter
fields.description:
Which parameters, ignoring case: `all`, `user`, `sketch` (dimensions), `feature` (inputs),
`model` (every one but the user's) or `favorites`. Anything else lists all. Default: all.

parameters.move.label: Move Parameter
parameters.move.help: name, before | after: another user parameter; the user parameter is listed just before or after it
parameters.move.description:
Move a user parameter just before or after another, in the order the user parameters are
listed. Give exactly one of `before` and `after`. One undo step.

fields.name: after
fields.description: Another user parameter, by name: the parameter is listed just after it.

fields.name: before
fields.description: Another user parameter, by name: the parameter is listed just before it.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The user parameter, by name.

parameters.rename.label: Rename Parameter
parameters.rename.help: name, new_name (expressions, feature inputs and dimensions that use it follow)
parameters.rename.description:
Rename a parameter, a user parameter or a feature's named input. The expressions, feature
inputs and dimensions that use it follow. One undo step.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The parameter, by name.

fields.name: new_name
fields.description: Its new name, as for a new parameter. Spaces at either end are dropped.

parameters.users.label: Parameter Users
parameters.users.help: name → users (parameters, feature inputs, dimensions) and the features it drives
parameters.users.description:
List what uses a parameter: other parameters, feature inputs, sketch dimensions,
configurations, joints, rules and canvases, and the features it drives. Changes nothing.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The parameter, by name: a user parameter, a dimension or a feature's named input.

parts.fastener.label: Insert Fastener
parts.fastener.help: the Insert Part dialog's command (same as parts.insert): family, size, length?, at?|point?+direction? (from the shank's tip toward the head), flip?, name?
parts.fastener.description:
Insert a standard part as a new component: seated in holes with a rigid joint each (`at`),
placed at a point (`point`), or at the origin. One undo step.

fields.name: direction
fields.description: With `point`: the direction the part's +Z turns to (default +Z), a non-zero `[x, y, z]`.

fields.name: family
fields.description:
The family, as `parts.library` lists it: socket_head_cap_screw, button_head_cap_screw,
countersunk_socket_screw, hex_bolt, hex_nut, washer, set_screw, dowel_pin, bearing, hex_bolt_gost,
socket_head_cap_screw_gost, set_screw_gost, hex_nut_gost, hex_nut_thin_gost, washer_gost,
washer_large_gost, dowel_pin_gost, hex_cap_screw_inch, hex_nut_inch, washer_sae or washer_uss.

fields.name: flip
fields.description:
Turn the part over from the way it is placed: with `at`, head into the material and shank
out of the face; with `point`, its +Z against `direction` (default false).

fields.name: length
fields.description: For screws, bolts, set screws and pins: the length in mm, inch parts too (default: a standard length near 2.5 diameters).

fields.name: name
fields.description: The component's name (default: the part's, such as `Socket Head Cap Screw M6x20`).

fields.name: point
fields.description: Without `at`: where the part's origin goes, with no joint.

fields.name: size
fields.description:
The size, as `parts.library` lists it: `M6`, `608` for a bearing, `1/2-13 UNC` for an
inch screw or nut, `1/2` for an inch washer.

parts.insert.label: Insert Part
parts.insert.help: family (socket_head_cap_screw | button_head_cap_screw | countersunk_socket_screw | hex_bolt | hex_nut | washer | set_screw | dowel_pin | bearing | hex_bolt_gost | socket_head_cap_screw_gost | set_screw_gost | hex_nut_gost | hex_nut_thin_gost | washer_gost | washer_large_gost | dowel_pin_gost | hex_cap_screw_inch | hex_nut_inch | washer_sae | washer_uss); size ("M6", "608" for bearings, "1/2-13 UNC" for inch screws and nuts, "1/2" for inch washers); length? (mm, inch parts too; screws, bolts, set screws, pins; default a standard length near 2.5 d); at?: [x,y,z] on a hole's rim or wall (the part seats on the hole's face with a rigid joint, head on the picked face and shank into the hole, whichever way the face points) or on a flat face (seated at that point, head out of the face), or a list of them (one component, placed and seated once per pick) | point?: [x,y,z] with direction?: [x,y,z] (no joint: the part's seating plane, under a head or the bottom of a nut, washer or bearing, the top of a set screw, pin or countersunk head, goes to point, and direction is its +z, from the shank's tip toward the head; default [0,0,1], head up, shank down -z); flip?: bool (default false: turned over, head into the material with at, +z against direction with point); name? → component, occurrence, joint?, directions (each placement's head direction in the world, the one chosen), and with at: occurrences, joints (one per pick, in pick order)
parts.insert.description:
Insert a standard part as a new component: seated in holes with a rigid joint each (`at`),
placed at a point (`point`), or at the origin. One undo step.

fields.name: direction
fields.description: With `point`: the direction the part's +Z turns to (default +Z), a non-zero `[x, y, z]`.

fields.name: family
fields.description:
The family, as `parts.library` lists it: socket_head_cap_screw, button_head_cap_screw,
countersunk_socket_screw, hex_bolt, hex_nut, washer, set_screw, dowel_pin, bearing, hex_bolt_gost,
socket_head_cap_screw_gost, set_screw_gost, hex_nut_gost, hex_nut_thin_gost, washer_gost,
washer_large_gost, dowel_pin_gost, hex_cap_screw_inch, hex_nut_inch, washer_sae or washer_uss.

fields.name: flip
fields.description:
Turn the part over from the way it is placed: with `at`, head into the material and shank
out of the face; with `point`, its +Z against `direction` (default false).

fields.name: length
fields.description: For screws, bolts, set screws and pins: the length in mm, inch parts too (default: a standard length near 2.5 diameters).

fields.name: name
fields.description: The component's name (default: the part's, such as `Socket Head Cap Screw M6x20`).

fields.name: point
fields.description: Without `at`: where the part's origin goes, with no joint.

fields.name: size
fields.description:
The size, as `parts.library` lists it: `M6`, `608` for a bearing, `1/2-13 UNC` for an
inch screw or nut, `1/2` for an inch washer.

parts.library.label: Standard Parts
parts.library.help: family? → families (name, standard, system: metric|inch, sizes, lengths) and, with family, each size's dimensions (mm)
parts.library.description: List the standard part families, or one family's sizes with their dimensions (mm).

fields.name: family
fields.description: One family, as the list names it (default: every family).

parts.resize.label: Change Part Size
parts.resize.help: component: id|name of an inserted part; size?; length? — rebuilds it (joints keep it seated)
parts.resize.description:
Change an inserted standard part's size or length, rebuilding it in place; its joints keep it
seated. One undo step.

fields.name: component
fields.description: The part's component, by id or name.

fields.name: length
fields.description: For screws, bolts, set screws and pins: the length in mm, inch parts too (default: a standard length near 2.5 diameters).

fields.name: size
fields.description: The new size (default: the part's).

plastic.assign_rule.label: Assign Plastic Rule
plastic.assign_rule.help: bodies: [names]; rule: name (empty: no rule) — plastic features on these bodies take its draft and clearance as defaults
plastic.assign_rule.description:
Assign a plastic rule to bodies, or take theirs away. Plastic features on those bodies take
the rule's draft and clearance as defaults.

fields.name: bodies
fields.description: The bodies, by name: 1 to 10 000.

fields.name: rule
fields.description:
The rule, by name, as `plastic.rules` lists it. Empty or left out: the bodies have no
rule of their own, so the active rule applies.

plastic.boss.label: Boss
plastic.boss.help: position: [x,y,z] on a face; direction? (default: out of the face); diameter, height; hole_diameter?, hole_depth? (default: to the face); draft? (angle), fillet? (root radius); ribs? (count), rib_thickness?, rib_length? (out from the wall), rib_offset? (below the top); body?
plastic.boss.description:
Add a boss: a round post standing on a face, for a screw, with an optional hole, draft, root
fillet and ribs. It joins the body it stands on. One undo step.

fields.name: body
fields.description: The body the boss joins, by name. Default: the body at `position`.

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: diameter
fields.description: A length: a number in the design's length unit, or an expression such as "w / 2" or "30 mm".

fields.name: direction
fields.description: A point in mm: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}.

fields.name: draft
fields.description:
The post's draft: it narrows towards its top by this angle. Default: the body's plastic
rule's draft, or none.

fields.name: fillet
fields.description: The radius of the round where the post meets the face. Default: none.

fields.name: height
fields.description: A length: a number in the design's length unit, or an expression such as "w / 2" or "30 mm".

fields.name: hole_depth
fields.description: How deep the hole goes from the post's top. Default: down to the face (the post's height).

fields.name: hole_diameter
fields.description: The screw hole's diameter, down from the post's top. Default: no hole.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

fields.name: position
fields.description: A point in mm: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}.

fields.name: rib_length
fields.description: How far each rib reaches out from the post's wall. Default: the post's radius.

fields.name: rib_offset
fields.description: How far below the post's top the ribs stop. Default: 0, the ribs reach the top.

fields.name: rib_thickness
fields.description: Each rib's thickness. Default: 0.3 times the post's radius.

fields.name: ribs
fields.description: How many ribs brace the post, evenly round it: 0 to 64. Default: none.

fields.name: touching
fields.description: What a join makes of pieces that share no face. Default: separate.

plastic.lip.label: Lip
plastic.lip.help: face: [x,y,z] on the rim face of a shelled body; width, height; type?: lip|groove; gap? (groove clearance); side?: inside|outside (which rim edge); body?
plastic.lip.description:
Add a lip or a groove: a band along one edge of a shelled body's rim face, raised for a lip
and cut for a groove, so two halves of a case fit together. A lip joins the body and a groove
cuts it. One undo step.

fields.name: body
fields.description: The shelled body, by name. Default: the body at `face`.

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: face
fields.description: A point in mm: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}.

fields.name: gap
fields.description:
A groove's clearance: it is this much wider than `width`, at least 0. Default: the body's
plastic rule's clearance, or none. A lip doesn't use it.

fields.name: height
fields.description: A length: a number in the design's length unit, or an expression such as "w / 2" or "30 mm".

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: outside
fields.description: True: the band runs along the outside edge, as `side: outside` does. Default: false.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

fields.name: touching
fields.description: What a lip's join makes of pieces that share no face. Default: separate.

fields.name: width
fields.description: A length: a number in the design's length unit, or an expression such as "w / 2" or "30 mm".

plastic.manage_rules.label: Manage Plastic Rules
plastic.manage_rules.help: name (library or new rule; a new one starts from `from`, default ABS (1.5mm)); from?; material?; thickness?, nominal_radius?, clearance?, knife_edge?, reveal_height?, thickness_variation?, draft?, max_thickness?, min_thickness?, min_draft? (expressions; `Thickness` is the rule's); active?: bool (rule for bodies without one); delete?: bool (a design rule; a library rule goes back to the library values)
plastic.manage_rules.description:
Make or edit a plastic rule, make it the active rule (the one for bodies without a rule of
their own), or delete it. A new rule starts from `from`; an existing one keeps the values not
given. Each value is a number or an expression, and may use the design's parameters; in a
rule's other values, `Thickness` is that rule's thickness.

fields.name: active
fields.description: True makes this the active rule; false stops it being the active rule.

fields.name: clearance
fields.description: The clearance between mating parts: a groove's gap when it gives none.

fields.name: delete
fields.description:
True deletes the rule from the design (a library rule goes back to the library's
values). Default: false.

fields.name: draft
fields.description: The draft of plastic features when they give none.

fields.name: from
fields.description: For a new rule: the rule it starts from. Default: "ABS (1.5mm)".

fields.name: material
fields.description: The material the rule is for, as a note (at most 128 characters are kept).

fields.name: max_thickness
fields.description: The thickest wall allowed.

fields.name: min_draft
fields.description: The least draft allowed.

fields.name: min_thickness
fields.description: The thinnest wall allowed.

fields.name: name
fields.description:
The rule, by name: a library rule (to edit it in this design) or a new one. Trimmed,
1 to 128 bytes.

fields.name: nominal_radius
fields.description: The nominal radius of rounds.

fields.name: thickness
fields.description: The nominal wall thickness.

fields.name: thickness_variation
fields.description: How much a wall's thickness may vary.

plastic.rest.label: Rest
plastic.rest.help: position: [x,y,z] on a face (the rest's centre); direction? (default: out of the face); width (round: the diameter); length? (a rectangle, along `along`); along?: [x,y,z]; height; draft? (angle; default: the body's plastic rule); thickness? (wall of a hollow rest); body?
plastic.rest.description:
Add a rest: a pad standing on a face for another part to rest on, round or rectangular, solid
or hollow. It joins the body it stands on. One undo step.

fields.name: along
fields.description: A point in mm: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}.

fields.name: body
fields.description: The body it stands on, by name. Default: the body at `position`.

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: direction
fields.description: A point in mm: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}.

fields.name: draft
fields.description:
The pad's draft, under 57°: it narrows towards its top by this angle. Default: the body's
plastic rule's draft, or none.

fields.name: height
fields.description: A length: a number in the design's length unit, or an expression such as "w / 2" or "30 mm".

fields.name: length
fields.description: A rectangular rest's length, along `along`. Default: a round rest.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

fields.name: position
fields.description: A point in mm: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}.

fields.name: thickness
fields.description: A hollow rest's wall thickness. Default: a solid rest.

fields.name: touching
fields.description: What a join makes of pieces that share no face. Default: separate.

fields.name: width
fields.description: A length: a number in the design's length unit, or an expression such as "w / 2" or "30 mm".

plastic.rules.label: List Plastic Rules
plastic.rules.help: → rules with their expressions and values, the active rule and the rules assigned to bodies
plastic.rules.description:
List the plastic rules (the library's and the design's), the active rule and the rules
assigned to bodies. No parameters.

plastic.snap_fit.label: Snap Fit
plastic.snap_fit.help: position: [x,y,z] on a face; direction? (default: out of the face); hook: [x,y,z] (the catch's direction); length, thickness, width, catch_depth, catch_length; base_height? (extends the base below the face); new_body?: bool (make a separate body instead of joining); body?
plastic.snap_fit.description:
Add a snap fit: a cantilever arm standing on a face with a catch at its tip, which clips into
another part. It joins the body it stands on, or makes a body of its own. One undo step.

fields.name: base_height
fields.description:
How far the arm's base reaches below the face, into the wall, at least 0.01 mm. Default:
none, the arm starts at the face.

fields.name: body
fields.description: The body it stands on, by name. Default: the body at `position`.

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: catch_depth
fields.description: A length: a number in the design's length unit, or an expression such as "w / 2" or "30 mm".

fields.name: catch_length
fields.description: A length: a number in the design's length unit, or an expression such as "w / 2" or "30 mm".

fields.name: direction
fields.description: A point in mm: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}.

fields.name: hook
fields.description: A point in mm: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}.

fields.name: length
fields.description: A length: a number in the design's length unit, or an expression such as "w / 2" or "30 mm".

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: new_body
fields.description: True: the snap fit is a body of its own instead of joining the body. Default: false.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

fields.name: position
fields.description: A point in mm: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}.

fields.name: thickness
fields.description: A length: a number in the design's length unit, or an expression such as "w / 2" or "30 mm".

fields.name: touching
fields.description: What a join makes of pieces that share no face. Default: separate.

fields.name: width
fields.description: A length: a number in the design's length unit, or an expression such as "w / 2" or "30 mm".

plugin.inspect.label: Inspect Plugin
plugin.inspect.help: path: plugin package folder; returns inert manifest and approval hash covering manifest and component; runs no plugin code

fields.name: path
fields.description: Package folder containing plugin.json and its component; subject to the caller's file scope.

plugin.inspect.reason: installs or runs code: needs the user's review of the plugin

plugin.install.label: Install Plugin
plugin.install.help: path: plugin .zip, approval?: exact hash from a reviewed dry run (mismatch refuses installation), archive?: exact .zip hash from that dry run (any changed file refuses installation), replace?: bool (required to replace an installed plugin of the same id), dry_run?: bool, approve?: {command_groups, folders: [{name, path, read, write}], memory_mib?: exactly the manifest's limits.memory_mib, allowed above the user's ceiling for this package}; validates requested approvals and checks the .zip (one plugin, safe paths, size caps, manifest) and unpacks it into the plugins folder; runs no plugin code
plugin.install.description: Install a plugin from a `.zip`: `plugin.json` and its component at the top or in one folder.

fields.name: approval
fields.description: Exact manifest-and-component hash from a reviewed dry run; a mismatch refuses installation.

fields.name: approve
fields.description: Permissions approved by the host user. Omission grants nothing, even on replacement.

fields.name: archive
fields.description: Exact `.zip` hash (`archive`) from a reviewed dry run; any changed file in the archive refuses installation.

fields.name: dry_run
fields.description: Check the `.zip` and describe the plugin; write nothing.

fields.name: path
