render.preflight.label: Check Render Request
render.preflight.help: setup?: saved name OR settings?: full RenderSetup. A typed job selects raster/cpu_raytrace/gpu_path and its numerical options plus embedded HDR before dispatch; only replace and transient studio_weights may accompany it. Without job, the legacy runtime controls below remain available. See docs/render-settings.md. studio_weights?: three finite 0..1 visibility weights for raster or implicit GPU studio sources only; never saved. integrator?: raster (default) or raytrace; progressive?: false (registered GPU path, CPU integrator/LED options are mutually exclusive); texture_filtering?: false (GPU); CPU raytrace.texture_filtering?: false. Explicitly enables ray-footprint mip and bounded anisotropic map filtering on GPU, and bounded anisotropic filtering on CPU. GPU filtering off retains bilinear LOD0; CPU filtering off retains isotropic mip selection, using the coarsest available mip when footprint data is unavailable. samples?: 1..65536; max_depth?: 1..64; seed?: u32 for progressive; raytrace?: bounded runtime progressive/primary_samples/lights/punctual_lights/area_lights/area_samples/seed/exposure_ev/shadows/reflections/anisotropic_faces/emissions/surface_effects/dielectrics/environment options, only with raytrace. CPU raytrace.lens?: {aperture_radius_mm:0..10000000,focus_distance_mm:0.000001..1000000000}; positive aperture requires explicit CPU progressive sampling and a bounded perspective camera; absent/zero keeps the original CPU ray stream. See docs/render-thin-lens.md. CPU raytrace.volume?: one HomogeneousVolume box with world-mm min_mm/max_mm, extinction_per_mm:0..1000, RGB scattering_albedo:0..1 and anisotropy:-0.95..0.95. Positive extinction requires explicit Indirect lighting and cannot combine with Glass/SSS or surface Denoise. Physical eye/pupil prefixes and the orthographic line/box union preserve camera/model framing under existing ray/profile caps. See docs/render-cpu-volume.md. CPU raytrace.sun? uses the shared finite-disk Sun contract; raytrace.sky? uses {gradient,rotation_rad,intensity}. Both require explicit Indirect lighting, and gradient Sky excludes a constant/HDR environment. Their medium NEE uses the HG response/PDF and physical light source; see docs/render-cpu-celestial.md. CPU transparent_background?:false exports straight-alpha primary geometry coverage for fixed/progressive sampling; body/face opacity must remain 1, and active bloom/backdrop/photographic effects require opaque output. CPU raytrace.output?: {tone_map,finishing,backdrop,linear_exr}; shared presentation supports up to 8192 per side and 33554432 output pixels, CPU exposure remains raytrace.exposure_ev; raw FLOAT32 EXR is retained only at final completion. CPU raytrace.budget?: compact (legacy default), studio or workstation; see docs/render-cpu-resource-profiles.md for explicit image/geometry/memory/work limits. CPU raytrace.progressive?: {samples_per_pixel:1..profile limit, seed:u32}; requires primary_samples:1 and selected reflections.samples:1; area/LED sources and certified planar anisotropy/thin-sheet/axis-aligned-box dielectric continuations share the existing bounded transport and compatibility checks. See docs/render-cpu-progressive.md; environment?: {path: scoped HDR, expected_sha256?: inspected digest, rotation_radians: 0, intensity: 1, samples: 16} OR {resource: saved HDR digest, rotation_radians, intensity, samples}; embedded resources cannot combine with path/hash; explicit sRGB/D65 HDR primaries required. Opaque CPU preview with selected mirror/rough-specular reflections and certified planar anisotropy. HDR with rough reflections or anisotropy requires fully metallic selected bodies and all effective faces; unsupported combinations refuse. Optional raytrace.path:{max_depth:1..64} enables CPU diffuse/specular GI with matched rectangle/HDR light and BSDF MIS plus certified closed-mesh Glass. It requires explicit progressive camera sampling, primary_samples:1 and traced shadows; selected reflections and certified anisotropy refuse before HDR IO without changing intent. CPU Path dielectric subsurface?:{scattering_per_mm:0..100,anisotropy:-0.95..0.95} enables homogeneous free-flight/HG walks inside certified closed media; positive rates require denoising off. Contained light connections include scattering survival; closed refractive light connections and combining Glass with external volume remain unsupported. Absent path keeps the old certified thin_sheet/closed_box producer and refuses subsurface intent explicitly. See docs/render-cpu-general-glass.md and render-raytrace-dielectrics.md. CPU emissions are visible radiance and may light neighbors through sampled Path continuation, without mesh-emitter next-event sampling; surface_effects change roughness/shading normals without geometry changes. led_strip?: continuous world-mm LED rectangle recipe; led_samples?: 1/4/16/64 for the whole strip, default16. At most8directional+8punctual+4rectangle/LED sources; shared area N. See docs/render-light-union.md. transparent_background?: false; replace?: false. With progressive:true, raytrace instead accepts GPU dielectrics/clear_coats/textures; environment instead accepts tagged hdr/embedded_hdr/sky with rotation_rad/intensity; file hdr supports expected_sha256, embedded_hdr uses a document resource digest. See docs/render-hdr-resources.md. GPU lens, studio lighting, tone_map, denoise, clamp_indirect?: 0.000001..1000000 (biased; caps each contribution from the first bounce on, keeping its hue; see docs/render-path.md), bounded finishing/backdrop and linear_exr retention are also available. CPU raytrace and GPU top-level controls accept supersampling:1|2 (default 1; doubles internal width and height at 2, averages scene-linear premultiplied samples before tone mapping, exports selected dimensions), denoise_settings:{passes:1..3,strength:0..1,firefly_suppression:bool,optical_filter:bool}, and denoise_diagnostics:false. Optical filtering defaults to true for eligible mirror/glass guides; optical_filter:false restores legacy opaque-only display denoising. Guides and diagnostics retain their independent eligibility policy and conservative highlight protection. CPU raytrace.threads:0..64 selects bounded automatic workers at 0 (default), serial work at 1 or an explicit count from 2 through 64. Resource checks include internal image buffers and worker scratch. See docs/render-quality-controls.md. Both path tracers accept optional metal_energy_compensation: true for rough isotropic metals (inside CPU raytrace or top-level GPU). Both methods accept optional caustics {photons:1..1048576,radius_mm:0.000001..1000000,max_depth:1..64,seed:u32,area_lights?:false,environment?:false,guided_emission?:false,refresh_per_pass?:false} (inside CPU raytrace; top-level GPU). Optical assignments accept optional model {roughness:0..1,dispersion?:{abbe_number:5..200},thin_film?:{ior:1..3,thickness_nm:0..100000}}. CPU advanced models require Path; rough sheets require straight transmitted shadows off. See docs/render-glass-material-models.md. GPU adaptive?: {pilot_samples:16..256,min_samples:16..samples,relative_error:0..1,absolute_error:0.000001..1000000,coverage_error:0.001..0.25} allocates independent production budgets; pilots are discarded, not a certified error guarantee. transmission_samples?:1|2|4 stratifies the first Fresnel branch with extra path cost. volume?:{min_mm:[x,y,z],max_mm:[x,y,z],extinction_per_mm:0..1000,scattering_albedo:[r,g,b],anisotropy:-0.95..0.95} is one finite homogeneous world-mm medium; active media require explicit lighting/environment and refuse glass, denoise and multiple transmission strata. These fields also persist in GPU job.options. See docs/render-materials/TRANSPORT-MASTER-BATCH-2026-10-23.md; see docs/render-transmission.md, render-environment.md, render-runtime-textures.md, render-thin-lens.md, render-studio-lighting.md and render-denoise.md. Optional CPU raytracing requires a raytrace-cpu build and native host, checked before scene capture. Stale geometry is rejected. See docs/render-jobs.md

fields.name: adaptive

fields.name: caustics
fields.description: GPU: photon caustics: `photons`, `radius_mm`, `max_depth`, `seed` and the optional `area_lights`, `environment`, `guided_emission` and `refresh_per_pass`. Default: none.

fields.name: clamp_indirect
fields.description: GPU: cap each contribution from the first bounce on at this value, from 0.000001 to 1000000, keeping its hue. Biased. Without `progressive: true`, only `null`. Default: none.

fields.name: denoise
fields.description: GPU: denoise the image. Without `progressive: true`, only `false`. Default: false.

fields.name: denoise_diagnostics

fields.name: denoise_settings

fields.name: environment
fields.description: Without `progressive`: a CPU HDR environment, with `integrator: raytrace`: `{path, expected_sha256?, rotation_radians?, intensity?, samples?}` for a file or `{resource, rotation_radians?, intensity?, samples?}` for an HDR saved in the design. With `progressive: true`: a GPU environment, by `kind`: `{kind: builtin_hdr, id, rotation_rad?, intensity?}`, `{kind: hdr, path, expected_sha256?, rotation_rad?, intensity?, assume_linear_srgb?}`, `{kind: embedded_hdr, resource, rotation_rad?, intensity?, assume_linear_srgb?}` or `{kind: sky, gradient?, rotation_rad?, intensity?}`. An HDR's `resource` and `expected_sha256` are its SHA-256, 64 lowercase hex digits. Default: none.

fields.name: finishing
fields.description: GPU: creative finishing, as Regrade Linear Master's `presentation` takes it: `looks`, `photographic`, `bloom`, `rgb_gain`, `contrast`, `saturation` and `vignette`. Default: none.

fields.name: integrator
fields.description: `raster` or `raytrace` (CPU ray tracing, in a build with it). With `progressive: true`, only `raster`. Default: raster.

fields.name: led_samples
fields.description: CPU only: the samples for the whole LED strip: 1, 4, 16 or 64. Needs `led_strip`. Default: 16.

fields.name: led_strip
fields.description: CPU only, with `integrator: raytrace`: a continuous LED strip, a rectangle in world mm (`center_mm`, `length_mm`, `width_mm`, `length_axis`, `width_axis`, `color`, `intensity`), lit as area lights.

fields.name: lens
fields.description: GPU: a thin lens, `{aperture_radius_mm, focus_distance_mm}`. Default: none, a pinhole camera.

fields.name: lighting
fields.description: GPU: studio lighting in place of the implicit studio. Default: none.

fields.name: linear_exr
fields.description: GPU: keep the raw linear FLOAT32 master, for `render.export` with `format: exr`. Default: false.

fields.name: max_depth
fields.description: GPU: the most bounces, from 1 to 64. Without `progressive: true`, only `null`.

fields.name: metal_energy_compensation
fields.description: GPU: restore the energy rough isotropic metals lose. Default: false.

fields.name: nested_media
fields.description: GPU: trace strictly nested solids (glass in glass, an air bubble) as nested media. Default: false.

fields.name: progressive
fields.description: `true`: the GPU form, rendered progressively by the GPU path tracer; the keys marked GPU apply. `false` or left out: the runtime form, for the raster executor or, with `integrator: raytrace`, the CPU ray tracer. Default: false.

fields.name: raytrace
fields.description: Without `progressive`: the CPU ray tracer's options (lights, reflections, `path`, `progressive` sampling, `output`, `budget` and others; see docs/render-jobs.md), with `integrator: raytrace`. With `progressive: true`: the GPU's `dielectrics`, `clear_coats` and `textures` overrides, each a list.

fields.name: samples
fields.description: GPU: samples per pixel, from 1 to 65536. Without `progressive: true`, only `null`.

fields.name: seed

sheet.convert.help: body; face: [x,y,z] on its large flat face (a plate of even thickness; recesses in one face up to half the thickness deep, such as an engraved label, become pockets of the sheet), or that face's name from model.faces; rule?; bends?: [[x,y,z] on sharp edges] (a solid or a shelled body: `face` is the fixed face and the flat faces reached from it across these edges become the sheet; a shell keeps its thickness, a solid takes the rule's inward; edges between two of those faces that are no bends are cut open with the rule's gap; a point in the middle of a chamfer between two faces, or on a bend modelled with its radius (a cylinder between two flat faces tangent to it, either skin), makes it one bend of the rule's radius at their virtual sharp; the faces' holes become cut-outs and their engravings, up to half the thickness deep, pockets)

Turn a body into sheet metal. Without `bends`, a plate of even thickness: its large flat face
becomes the sheet, holes become cut-outs and recesses in one face up to half the thickness
deep (an engraved label) become pockets. With `bends`, a solid or shelled body: `face` stays

thickness, a solid takes the rule's inward, and edges between two of those faces that are no
bends are cut open with the rule's gap. `participants` changes nothing.

plate).

Add a sheet metal flange: a base flange from sketch profiles, a contour flange along an open
chain of sketch lines and tangent arcs, or edge flanges on a sheet's edges. Thickness, K-factor, bend radius
and reliefs come from the sheet metal rule (`sheet.manage_rules`), so those keys are refused;
an edge flange may set its own `radius` and corner relief. `participants` changes nothing.

fields.description: Contour: how far the flange runs from the sketch plane, positive.

fields.description: Points in mm on the sheet's top or bottom edges, 1 to 1000: each [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}, or {point: [x, y, z], angle?, height?, segments?} for an edge with its own angle and height (null: the feature's), or split into 1 to 64 segments that tile it.

to the other side of the chain. Edge: the flanges bend the other way. Default: false.

fields.description:
Edge: where the height is measured from: the outer virtual sharp (outer), the inner virtual
sharp (inner), or past 90° the line square to the flange touching the bend's outside

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

fields.description:
Edge: where the bend starts: inside (the outer virtual sharp on the edge), outside or
bend_outside (the bend starting at the edge), middle (half-way), material_outside (the

face; below 90° the bend's end on that face). Default: inside.

fields.name: profiles
fields.description: Which sketch profiles to use: "all" (the default, any case), an index, or a list of indices, of {"point": [x, y]} inside a profile, or of curve selections (a list of curve ids, {"curves": [ids]} or {"loops": [...]}). (default: rule); position?: centerline|start|end|mould (where the line sits in the bend, default centerline); fixed?: [x,y,z] on the side that stays (default: the larger side); flip? (fold the other way); body?
sheet.fold.description:
Fold a sheet along a line on its top or bottom face: a sketch line (followed when the sketch
changes) or two points. The bend zone comes out of the sheet, so the flat pattern keeps its
size. `participants` changes nothing.

fields.description: The bend angle. Default: 90 deg.

fields.name: body
fields.description: The sheet metal body. Default: the sheet with an edge nearest the line's middle.

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: curve
fields.description: The fold line: a line of `sketch`, by id. Required unless `points` is given; ignored then.

fields.name: fixed
fields.description: A point in mm: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}.

fields.name: flip
fields.description: Fold the other way. Default: false.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

fields.name: points
fields.description: The fold line's two ends, in mm.

fields.name: position
fields.description:
Where the line sits in the bend zone: its centre (centerline), its start or end, from the
side that stays, or the mould line (mould: where the outer faces meet). Default:
centerline.

fields.name: radius
fields.description: The inner bend radius. Default: the sheet's rule's.

fields.name: sketch
fields.description: A sketch's feature id (a number) or its name.

sheet.manage_rules.label: Sheet Metal Rules
sheet.manage_rules.help: name (new or existing); thickness?, k_factor?, bend_radius?, relief_width?, relief_depth?, corner_relief?, hem_gap?, gap? (expressions; `Thickness` is the rule's; gap: between flanges that meet at a corner, whose ends are closed toward each other at any angle); corner_relief_shape?: notch|round|rectangular|tear (what is cut where two bends meet at a corner of the base: round and rectangular a relief `corner_relief` across; tear none, each bend's end is cut straight from the corner to its flange's end; default notch); angle_display?: bend|included (how the DXF bend notes read the bend angles: the bend angle, default, or the included angle left between the bend's sides, 180° less it; the bend table gives both, and a flange's `angle` is always the bend angle); active?: bool; delete?: bool
sheet.manage_rules.description:
Create or edit a sheet metal rule, activate it, or delete it. Expressions may use design
parameters; `Thickness` inside a rule's other expressions is that rule's thickness.
The handler evaluates dimensions and ranges against the design after checking the contract.

fields.name: active
fields.description:
Make this the active rule. Default: true if there is no saved active rule, otherwise false.
False leaves the active choice unchanged; ignored when deleting.

fields.name: angle_display
fields.description:
How DXF bend notes show angles: bend or included, ignoring case and surrounding blanks.
Ignored when deleting.

fields.name: bend_radius
fields.description: Inner bend radius, nonnegative. Ignored when deleting.

fields.name: corner_relief
fields.description: Corner relief size across. Ignored when deleting.

fields.name: corner_relief_shape
fields.description: Corner relief shape. Ignored when deleting.

fields.name: delete
fields.description:
Delete the named saved rule instead of editing it. Default: false. Deleting the active
rule clears that choice; listing then uses the first remaining rule, else built-in steel.

fields.name: gap
fields.description: Gap between meeting flanges. Ignored when deleting.

fields.name: hem_gap
fields.description: Inner radius of flat hems. Ignored when deleting.

fields.name: k_factor
fields.description: Neutral-axis fraction, from 0 to 1. Ignored when deleting.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Trimmed, nonempty rule name, at most 128 bytes after trimming.

fields.name: relief_depth
fields.description: Bend relief depth. Ignored when deleting.

fields.name: relief_width
fields.description: Bend relief width. Ignored when deleting.

fields.name: thickness
fields.description: Thickness, more than 0 and less than 10000 mm. Ignored when deleting.

feature, one body. `participants` changes nothing.

sketch.chamfer.distance_angle.label: Distance and Angle Chamfer
sketch.chamfer.distance_angle.help: point | points: [corners] (every corner cut alike; a corner is a point reference or {a, b}, and a point's `a` is the first of its two lines in curve order) | a, b: a corner of two lines (two that share no end are first brought to where they meet, as in sketch.fillet); distance: along a, angle: deg from a. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)
sketch.chamfer.distance_angle.description:
Cut one or several corners of two lines with a straight line that is `distance` back along
`a` and meets `b` at `angle` from `a`. A point's `a` is the first of its two lines in curve
order. Two lines that share no end are first brought to where they meet, as in
`sketch.fillet`. Every corner is cut alike, in one undo step, and a corner that cannot be
cut refuses them all.

fields.name: a
fields.description:
One of the two curves that meet at the corner (used when `point` is not text). Two lines
that share no end are first brought to where they meet.

fields.name: angle
fields.description:

(`line`), or about a point (`point`): each pair then joined by a construction line that the
point is the middle of.

sketch.construction.label: Normal/Construction
sketch.construction.help: curves: [ids], value?: bool (default: construction unless all of them already are)
sketch.construction.description:
Switch curves between normal and construction. The selection switches together (a slot or
polygon as a whole): to construction unless all of it already is. Projected curves may
switch too. A centerline that becomes construction stops being a centerline, and a normal
line is a finite one. One undo step.

fields.name: curves
fields.description: Ids, as a list of text (at least one, at most 10000) or a single id.

fields.name: sketch
fields.description: The sketch. Default: the one being edited.

fields.name: value
fields.description:
True makes them construction, false makes them normal. Default: construction unless all of
them already are.

sketch.construction.reason: runs in the sketch environment: open a sketch first (Create 2D Sketch, or double-click a sketch)

sketch.construction_line.label: Construction Line
sketch.construction_line.help: Construction line, free. at: point; through?: second point; curve?, curve2?: sketch references; angle?: degrees from sketch X; offset?: positive length (parallel: distance from the reference line; horizontal: distance from sketch X; vertical: distance from sketch Y; the side follows at) and a driving dimension at that value; near?: solution selector, and the side a line with a length runs towards; solution?: zero-based solution index; length?: a segment of this length from `at`, held by a length dimension, instead of an infinite line (horizontal, vertical, angle, parallel, perpendicular); construction?: false makes that segment a normal line. Tangents take circles/arcs, or an open spline/conic endpoint for tangent_at.. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)
sketch.construction_line.description: Create a reference line in the active sketch: infinite, or a segment of a given length.

sketch.dimension.label: Sketch Dimension
sketch.dimension.help: entities: [refs] (a line midpoint is "mid:line_id"; a model edge or vertex, {edge: [x,y,z], body?} or {vertex: [x,y,z], body?}, is projected into the sketch first and measured there: a point against the projected edge measures the distance to it), type?: auto|distance|horizontal|distance_x|vertical|distance_y|length|radius|diameter|major|minor|angle, value?: number or expression (default: current; a bare number is in the design's units, e.g. 2 means 2 in in an inch design; give a unit such as "50 mm" to override), or `name = expression` (e.g. "width = 40"; also `#name = expression`), which adds the user parameter `name` with that expression and dimensions with `name` (refused when the name is taken or reserved; the reply's `defined` names it); text_at?: [x, y]. Two points or a line off the axes: with auto, text_at across from them (between the perpendiculars through them, or a tenth of their distance past) is the distance between them; pulled further past an end, up or down from it horizontal, sideways vertical. Two midpoints: placing text above or below their bounding box measures horizontally, beside it vertically, anywhere else (inside it or past its corners) the distance between them. Two lines: the angle between them (acute, or 180° − it when the value is nearer that) unless text_at picks a sector. A line and a circle or arc: the distance from the line to its edge (the gap, or how far the edge reaches past a line that cuts it; 0 is tangent); dimension the centre point for the distance to the centre. A point and a circle or arc: the distance from the point to its edge (or how far within it a point inside lies). Two circles or arcs: the gap between their edges (or how far they overlap when they cross, or the narrowest gap between them when one lies inside the other), or the centre-to-centre distance when they are the two caps of a slot. An ellipse: a half-axis, the distance from the centre to an axis end (major or minor; with auto, text_at pulled across the major axis gives the major half-axis, pulled out past an end of it the minor one, the minor without text_at; previous_axis?: major|minor, the half-axis an earlier placement chose, kept while text_at is near the boundary between them; the reply's axis names the one chosen; with auto, when a driving dimension already holds one half-axis (or its whole axis), the other one, wherever text_at is; without its major axis line the major half-axis goes to the ellipse's own major end, without its minor axis line the minor half-axis is the minor radius); any other type, radius among them, the minor radius; an ellipse's axis line with auto: its length, the whole axis, wherever text_at is; half_axes?: bool (default true; false: with auto, the minor radius wherever text_at is, as before half-axes, which the Dimension tool sends with Draw ellipses with their axes off). An arc and one of its end points: the arc's length (type arc_length does it from the arc alone). A dimension the sketch already determines is refused (naming what determines it); if_redundant?: "driven" places it as a driven (reference) dimension instead. scale_sketch?: bool (the dimension tool sends the Sketch preference, on by default): when this is the sketch's first length dimension and nothing in the sketch fixes a size (no other driving length dimension, nothing fixed or projected), the whole sketch scales to the value instead of distorting: about the origin when the drawing is tied to it (joined to the origin, or constrained to a sketch axis), otherwise about the middle of the drawing, so it stays where it was drawn (#11043); scale_about_origin?: bool (default false; the dimension tool sends the Sketch preference) scales about the origin always, as before #11043. Returns measured in unit (mm or deg), and scaled: the factor when the sketch was scaled
sketch.dimension.description:
Dimension one or two sketch entities: a length, distance, radius, diameter, angle or ellipse
half-axis, driving the sketch (it adds a parameter) or only measuring (`driven: true`). The
kind follows from the entities, `type` and where `text_at` is. One undo step.

fields.name: driven
fields.description:
True to place a driven (reference) dimension: it measures, has no parameter and does not
constrain. Default: false.

fields.name: entities
fields.description: One or two entities: a curve or point id (`l1`, `p3`, `l1.start`, `c1.center`), `x` or `y` (a sketch axis), `mid:<line id>` (a line's midpoint), or a model edge `{edge: [x, y, z], body?}` or vertex `{vertex: [x, y, z], body?}`, projected into the sketch first and measured there. One id may be given as text instead of a list.

fields.name: half_axes
fields.description:
For an ellipse with type auto: true gives the half-axis `text_at` picks, false the minor
radius wherever `text_at` is. Default: true.

fields.name: if_redundant
fields.description:
`driven` (any case): when the sketch already determines the dimension, place it as a
driven (reference) dimension instead of refusing it; the reply then has `redundant` and
`determined_by`. Any other text refuses it. Read only when the dimension turns out to be
determined, and not for a driven dimension.

fields.name: orientation
fields.description:
With type auto or distance: `horizontal` or `vertical` measures along that axis, as
type does. Any other text is ignored.

fields.name: previous_axis
fields.description:
For an ellipse with type auto: `major` or `minor`, the half-axis an earlier placement
chose, kept while `text_at` is near the boundary between them (any case; other text is
ignored).

fields.name: scale_about_origin
fields.description:
Scale about the sketch origin even when the drawing is free. Default: false. Not read
for a driven dimension.

fields.name: scale_sketch
fields.description:
When this is the sketch's first length dimension and nothing in the sketch fixes a size
(no other driving length dimension, nothing fixed or projected), scale the whole sketch
to the value instead of distorting it (the reply's `scaled` is the factor). A free
drawing uses its own centre. A drawing tied to the origin scales about the origin.
Default: false. Not read for a driven dimension.

fields.name: sketch
fields.description: The sketch: its feature id or its name (default: the one being edited).

fields.name: text_at
fields.description: A sketch point in mm: [x, y] or {"x", "y"}.

fields.name: type
fields.description:
What to measure, in any case: auto (the default: from the entities and where `text_at`
is), distance, horizontal (or distance_x), vertical (or distance_y), length, radius,
diameter, major or minor (an ellipse's half-axis), angle, sweep (an arc's angle),
arc_length (arclength), overall_length (a slot's overall length), offset. Other text is no
known type: the entities' default measure (a length or a radius), with no choice by
`text_at`.

fields.name: value
fields.description: A length: a number in the design's length unit, or an expression such as "w / 2" or "30 mm".

sketch.drag.label: Drag Sketch Geometry
sketch.drag.help: entity: point or curve, from: [x,y] where it was grabbed, to: [x,y], live?: bool: points and the material point grabbed on a line move toward `to` within the design constraints. When exact placement is impossible, bounded feasible steps minimize cursor distance. Splines slide by to - from; a circle or arc grabbed on its edge takes the radius to `to`. `with?`: [point or curve ids] moves the rest of a selection with the entity as one translation (circles keep their radii). Long moves retain the solution branch; arcs cannot sweep through their starts. Returns `reached`: progress projected onto the requested move (0..1), `at`: the grabbed position for the next frame, and `retry`: budget-limited progress can continue in another frame. `live: true` shares a work budget across held-solve decomposition and cursor correction; ordinary recovery and the final model evaluation retain their existing limits, not a wall-clock deadline. Later features stay stale until `sketch.drag_end`; `dof` stays from before the drag

Drag a sketch point or curve from where it was grabbed to a position: points and the
material point grabbed on a line move toward it within the design constraints, and when exact
placement is impossible, bounded feasible steps minimize the cursor distance. Splines slide
by `to` minus `from`; a circle or arc grabbed on its edge takes the radius to `to`. Long
moves keep the solution branch, and arcs cannot sweep through their starts. With
`live: true` (one frame of a drag; such calls are not checked against this schema yet), later
features stay stale until `sketch.drag_end`, and `dof` stays from before the drag.

sketch.draw.dimensioned.label: Draw Dimensioned Sketch Geometry
sketch.draw.dimensioned.help: command: sketch creation command, params: object, dimensions: object of role to numeric or expression value, or `name = expression` (also `#name = expression`), which defines the user parameter `name` as sketch.dimension does (the reply's `defined` lists the names) (optional with as_drawn or locate), as_drawn?: bool (also dimension every other role of the shape at its size as drawn; a radius or diameter given takes the place of the other, as an edge polygon's side length does its radius, a circle otherwise takes its diameter, and a size the sketch already determines, such as the angle of a line inferred horizontal, is left out), locate?: bool (then place the shape from the sketch origin until nothing of it is left free: horizontal and vertical distances from the origin to its points, centres first, each kept only where it removes freedom, so a shape anchored to the origin or to placed geometry gets none; a point on an axis goes onto that axis instead of a 0 distance; the reply's located lists them); creates geometry and all driving dimensions atomically in one undo step. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)
sketch.draw.dimensioned.description:
Draw a shape and dimension it in one undo step. `command` names the sketch creator and
`params` its parameters; `dimensions` gives the sizes to place, by role, as driving
dimensions. With `as_drawn` every other size of the shape is placed at its size as drawn
(a size the sketch already determines is left out); with `locate` the shape is then placed
from the sketch origin with horizontal and vertical distances, only where each takes freedom
away. Either one makes `dimensions` optional. A size the sketch already has is placed as a
driven (reference) dimension rather than refused.

fields.name: as_drawn
fields.description:
Also dimension every other size of the shape at its size as drawn. A radius or diameter
given takes the place of the other (as an edge polygon's side length does its radius); a
circle otherwise takes its diameter. Default: false.

fields.name: command
fields.description: A sketch creation command whose shape can be dimensioned.

fields.name: dimensions
fields.description: The sizes to place, each by its role: a number (in the design's unit) or an expression, or `name = expression`, which also defines the user parameter `name`. The roles a creator takes are its own: a line or midpoint line takes `length` and `angle`; a rectangle `width` and `height`; a circle `diameter` or `radius` (not both); an arc by centre `radius` and `sweep`; an ellipse `major_radius` and `minor_radius`; a centre-to-centre, overall or centre-point slot `length` and `width`; a centre arc slot `radius`, `sweep` and `width`; a three-point arc slot `width`; an inscribed or circumscribed polygon `radius`; an edge polygon `radius` or `length` (not both). A role the creator does not take is refused.

fields.name: locate
fields.description:
Then place the shape from the sketch origin until nothing of it is left free: horizontal
and vertical distances from the origin to its points, centres first, each kept only where
it removes freedom, so a shape anchored to the origin or to placed geometry gets none. A
point on an axis goes onto that axis instead of getting a distance of 0. Default: false.

fields.name: params
fields.description: The parameters of the creator `command` names, as that command takes them. The creator checks them.

sketch.equation_curve.label: Equation Curve
sketch.equation_curve.help: x: x(t), y: y(t): formulas of t in the design's expression language and parameters ("r * (cos(t) + t * sin(t))"); or explicit: true and y: f(x) alone (no x); start, end: the range of t (or of x): a number or an expression ("2 * pi", "360 deg" is 2·pi, a length is in the design's unit); tolerance?: mm (default 0.01): how far the curve may stray from the formulas (0.0001 to 10); construction?: bool; variable_unit?: "number" (default) or "range". The variable is a plain number: sin(t) reads it in radians; a result without a unit is in the design's length unit. With variable_unit "range" it is a length, so a ^ 2 / (4 * t) is a length when a is one: start and end must both be lengths, or one a length and the other a plain number, which is then in the design's unit. Makes a fit point spline through fixed points, as many as the tolerance needs (up to 500), closed smoothly when it ends where it starts; the points are placed again from the formulas whenever the parameters change. Returns curve, points (how many), closed, deviation (mm). Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

sketch.fillet.label: Fillet
sketch.fillet.help: point: corner shared by two curves ("l1.end") | points: [corners] (all rounded alike: one radius, the rest equal; a corner is a point reference or {a, b}, the two curves meeting there) | a, b: two lines or arcs meeting at a corner (two lines that share no end are first brought to where they meet: the nearer end of a line that stops short moves there, and a line that runs past is cut there, losing its shorter piece); radius: expr. A corner that dimensions or constraints measure to stays as a virtual sharp corner on both curves' extensions (`virtual_corners`; the moved ones in `moved_to_virtual_corner`). An ellipse's axis line is never a side of a corner (also for the chamfers). A corner of an offset's lines and arcs first releases that offset (also for the chamfers): its curves keep following their sources at the offset's distance, held by dimensions that keep its parameter (`offset_released`: curve ids). Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)
sketch.fillet.description:
Round one or several corners of a sketch with an arc of one radius, tangent to both curves.
The corner is two lines, or a line and an arc, or two arcs, that meet at a point. Two lines
that share no end are first brought to where they meet (the nearer end of a line that stops
short moves there, and a line that runs past is cut there, losing its shorter piece). With
several corners the first arc carries the radius dimension and the rest are equal to it. A
corner that dimensions or constraints measure to stays as a virtual sharp corner on both
curves' extensions. An ellipse's axis line is never a side of a corner. One undo step.

sketch.text.label: Text
sketch.text.help: text: string (\n breaks lines), or text_expression: the words built from text parameters (parameters.add with unit text), number parameters and quoted texts joined by + ("Label + '-L'", "'W' + Width"; a number parameter shows its value in the design's units, "85 mm", an angle in degrees, "30°"; number(Width) is the number alone and number(Width, 2) has 2 decimals): the text keeps it, its words follow the parameters (a parameter edit or a configuration row relabels it) and `exprs` returns it as `text`; at: baseline start [x,y], height?: capital height mm (default 5), angle?: deg; at's x and y, height and angle each take a number or an expression over the design's parameters as a string ("plate_width / 2", "label_size"): the text keeps the expression, follows the parameters, and returns it in `exprs`; an expression naming no parameter is the number it comes to, a bare number in one is in the design's units, font?: an installed font's family or full name, or a .ttf/.otf file path (~ and %VAR% expand; default: the built-in Liberation Sans), bold?, italic?: bool (an installed family's bold or italic face; italic without one is slanted), align?: left|center|right (the lines against `at`, or along the path), vertical_align?: baseline|top|middle|bottom (the block of lines against `at` or the path: the first line's baseline (default), its capitals' tops, halfway between those and the last line's baseline, or the bottom of the last line's descenders), letter_spacing?: extra mm between letters, line_spacing?: times the font's line distance (default 1), path?: a curve id of the sketch the baseline follows ("": none; `at` and `angle` then do not place the text; the curve becomes construction, a guide the letters stand on), reverse?: bool (the other way along the path). Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)
sketch.text.description: Make text in the sketch being edited: outlines that stay linked to their words and style, so a later sketch.edit_text can change them. Give `text` or `text_expression`, and `at`.

fields.name: align
fields.description:
The lines against `at`, or along the path: left, center (or centre) or right, either case.
Default: left. When editing, kept when left out.

fields.name: angle
fields.description:
The direction of the baseline, counter-clockwise from sketch X: a number of degrees or an
expression. Default: 0. When editing, kept when left out. Does not turn a text on a `path`.

fields.name: at
fields.description:
The baseline start, [x, y] in mm, or {x, y}; in `[x, y]` each is a number or an expression
over the design's parameters as a string (`"plate_width / 2"`), which the text keeps and
follows. Needed to make a text; when editing, kept when left out (and moving a text
replaces its expressions with numbers). Does not place a text on a `path`.

fields.name: bold
fields.description: An installed family's bold face. Default: false. When editing, kept when left out.

fields.name: font
fields.description:
An installed font's family or full name, or a .ttf or .otf file path (`~` and `%VAR%`
expand); empty: the built-in Liberation Sans. Default: the built-in font. When editing,
kept when left out.

fields.name: height
fields.description:
The capital height in mm (above 0, below 100 000), a number or an expression over the
design's parameters. Default: 5. When editing, kept when left out.

fields.name: italic
fields.description:
An installed family's italic face (without one, the text is slanted). Default: false. When
editing, kept when left out.

fields.name: letter_spacing
fields.description: Extra space between letters, in mm. Default: 0. When editing, kept when left out.

fields.name: line_spacing
fields.description:
The line distance as a multiple of the font's (above 0). Default: 1. When editing, kept
when left out.

fields.name: path
fields.description:
A curve id of the sketch the baseline follows; empty: none. `at` and `angle` then do not
place the text, and the curve becomes construction, a guide the letters stand on. When
editing, kept when left out.

fields.name: reverse
fields.description:
Run the text the other way along its `path`. Default: false. When editing, kept when left
out.

fields.name: sketch
fields.description: Only for the reply's `created`, which compares this sketch (default: the one being edited); the text always goes into the sketch being edited.

fields.name: text
fields.description:
The words, at most 4096 characters, `\n` breaking lines; not blank. Not with
`text_expression`. When editing, kept when left out.

fields.name: text_expression
fields.description:
The words built from text parameters (`parameters.add` with unit text), number parameters
and quoted texts joined by `+` (`"Label + '-L'"`, `"'W' + Width"`; `number(Width, 2)` is
a number with 2 decimals). The text keeps it and follows the parameters; the reply's
`exprs` returns it as `text`. Not with `text`. When editing, typed words replace it.

sketch.trim.path.help: points: [[x,y]…] (2…2000 positions: a path drawn across the sketch). Every piece the path crosses is removed as `sketch.trim` removes the piece at that crossing, in the order the path crosses them; a piece crossed again after it is gone is not trimmed twice; eligible single-line offset outputs are trimmed while preserving their distance; projected geometry, infinite lines, other offset outputs and pieces trim refuses are passed over (why in `skipped`). dry_run?: bool (report without changing the design). One undo step → trimmed: [each trim's result], removed: [[[x,y]…]] (each removed piece as a polyline). sketch.trim.path.description:
Trim every piece a path drawn across the sketch crosses, as `sketch.trim` removes the piece
at each crossing, in the order the path crosses them. A piece crossed again after it is gone
is not trimmed twice. Projected geometry, infinite lines, offset outputs other than a single
line's, and pieces `sketch.trim` refuses are passed over (the reply's `skipped` says why).

solid.align.label: Align
solid.align.help: bodies: [names]; from: [x,y,z] | "origin" | {snap: vertex|edge_mid|face_center|circle_center, at: [x,y,z]} | from_face: [x,y,z] | from_plane: XY|XZ|YZ|construction or offset plane name or id|{origin, normal}; to: (the same) | to_face: [x,y,z] | to_plane: (a plane as from_plane; the point or face goes onto it along its normal, and the plane may move later: the bodies follow); from_frame / to_frame: a frame found again whenever the design changes, so the bodies follow it, in place of that side's point, face or plane: a joint origin as joint.create takes one ({face|circle|edge|point: [x,y,z]}, a face's name, a named joint origin) or {sketch, point|curve} (a sketch point, or a circle's, arc's or ellipse's centre, z along the sketch's normal), on the bodies' own component; faces, planes and frames also turn to meet; flip?: bool; axes?: [x, y, z] (point-to-point only: which world axes the offset moves along; default all three, at least one true); angle?: expr (a turn about the target's direction after the move)
solid.align.description:
Move bodies so that a point, face, plane or frame on them meets another one, as a feature in
the timeline (one undo step). Each side is one of: a point (`from`, `to`), a planar face
picked by a point on it (`from_face`, `to_face`), a plane (`from_plane`, `to_plane`) or a frame
(`from_frame`, `to_frame`); give one key for each side. A plane or a frame is worked out again
whenever the design changes, so the bodies follow it. Faces, planes and frames also turn the
bodies so that they meet (the first side's face against the second's, or with `flip` side by
side); a point onto a plane moves along the plane's normal. `axes` keeps the move to some
world axes and only goes with two points. Align makes no body, so `body_name` and `body_names`
do nothing here (as for Remove), and `participants` changes nothing in the result.

fields.name: angle
fields.description:
A turn about the target's direction (a face's normal, a plane's normal or a frame's z)
after the move, in degrees or an expression. Needs a face, a plane or a frame as the
target. Default: none.

fields.name: axes
fields.description: Which world axes the move follows: [x, y, z] booleans, at least one true.

fields.name: bodies
fields.description: The bodies to move, by name: one, or a list of 1 to 10 000.

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: flip
fields.description:
With faces, planes or frames: true turns the bodies so that the two normals point the same
way, instead of facing each other. Default: false.

fields.name: from
fields.description: A point: [x, y, z] in mm, the text "origin" (any case), or {"snap"?, "at"}: the nearest vertex, edge midpoint, planar face centre or circular edge centre of the model to the point `at`. {"x", "y", "z"} is not a point here.

fields.name: from_face
fields.description: A point in mm: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}.

fields.name: from_frame
fields.description: A frame that is found again whenever the design changes, so the bodies follow it: a sketch point, or the centre of a sketch circle, arc or ellipse, as {"sketch", "point" | "curve"} (z along the sketch's normal); or a joint origin as joint.create takes one: {face | circle | edge | point: [x, y, z]}, a face's name, or the name of a joint origin. On the bodies' own component, which must hold all of them and be placed once.

fields.name: from_plane
fields.description: A plane: XY, XZ or YZ (or Top, Front or Right; any case), a construction plane's name or feature id, or an explicit plane {"origin"?, "x_dir", "y_dir"} or {"origin"?, "normal"}: directions [x, y, z] (two that aren't parallel, or a normal that isn't zero; the two directions win over normal when both are points) and an origin in mm, each coordinate a number or a length expression (default: the origin).

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

fields.name: to
fields.description: A point: [x, y, z] in mm, the text "origin" (any case), or {"snap"?, "at"}: the nearest vertex, edge midpoint, planar face centre or circular edge centre of the model to the point `at`. {"x", "y", "z"} is not a point here.

fields.name: to_face
fields.description: A point in mm: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}.

fields.name: to_frame
fields.description: A frame that is found again whenever the design changes, so the bodies follow it: a sketch point, or the centre of a sketch circle, arc or ellipse, as {"sketch", "point" | "curve"} (z along the sketch's normal); or a joint origin as joint.create takes one: {face | circle | edge | point: [x, y, z]}, a face's name, or the name of a joint origin. On the bodies' own component, which must hold all of them and be placed once.

fields.name: to_plane
fields.description: A plane: XY, XZ or YZ (or Top, Front or Right; any case), a construction plane's name or feature id, or an explicit plane {"origin"?, "x_dir", "y_dir"} or {"origin"?, "normal"}: directions [x, y, z] (two that aren't parallel, or a normal that isn't zero; the two directions win over normal when both are points) and an origin in mm, each coordinate a number or a length expression (default: the origin).

solid.boundary_fill.label: Boundary Fill
solid.boundary_fill.help: tools: [bodies]; cells: [[x,y,z] a point inside each cell to fill (a cell: inside some tools, outside the rest)]; operation?: new|join|cut|intersect; remove_tools?: bool
solid.boundary_fill.description:
Add a solid made of the cells that tool bodies enclose, each picked by a point inside it, and
combine it with the design's bodies. One undo step.

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: cells
fields.description: A point inside each cell to fill, 1 to 1000. A cell is a region inside some of the tools and outside the rest.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: operation
fields.description: How the filled solid combines with the design's bodies. Default: new.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

fields.name: remove_tools
fields.description: True: the tool bodies are removed once the cells are filled. Default: false.

fields.name: tools
fields.description: The tool bodies whose surfaces bound the cells, by name: 1 to 64.

fields.name: touching
fields.description: What a join makes of pieces that share no face. Default: separate.

solid.bounding_solid.help: bodies?: [names] (default: all); margin?: expr; name?, body_name?
solid.bounding_solid.description: Add a box around bodies, larger by a margin on every side.

fields.name: bodies

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: margin
fields.description: How much larger than the bodies on every side. Default: 0.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

solid.box.label: Box
solid.box.help: length, width, height: expr; corner?: [x,y,z] | center?: [x,y,z] (numbers in mm or length expressions; default: the origin; a box placed by its center stays centred there when its size changes); operation?, touching?, targets?: [body], name?, body_name?

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: center

fields.name: corner
fields.description: A point: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}, each a number in mm or a length expression.

fields.name: height

fields.name: length
fields.description: A length: a number in the design's length unit, or an expression such as "w / 2" or "30 mm".

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: operation
fields.description: How the box combines with existing bodies. Default: new.

fields.name: participants
fields.description: The bodies a join, cut or intersect works on, in place of `targets`.

The bodies a join, cut or intersect works on. Default: every body in the active

solid.cell_grid.label: Cell Grid
solid.cell_grid.help: size: expr (a cell's inscribed diameter); web: expr (the wall between cells); depth: expr (or through_all: true); shape?: hexagon|square|triangle|circle|polygon (default hexagon); sides?: expr (polygon cells, 3 to 64; default 8); dot_grid?: hexagonal|square (where circle and polygon cells sit; default hexagonal); angle?: expr (the grid's rotation about the anchor; angle 45 deg with square cells gives a diamond layout); anchor?: [x,y,z] (a cell's centre, projected onto the sketch plane; default the sketch origin: grids with the same anchor, angle, size and web line up); clip?: whole|snap|free (cells the field's edge crosses: only whole cells; cells cut along the grid's own lines; cells trimmed to the edge as drawn; default snap); keepout_clip?: whole|snap|free (the same for the edges of loops inside the field, the keep-outs; default: the value of clip, so one mode serves every loop; a cell that meets both kinds is dropped if either is whole, else trimmed if either is free); snap_inset?: expr (with clip snap, a whole number of lattice lines each straight field edge moves in after it snaps, so the edge cells are whole and the rim thicker by whole grid rows; default 0; keep-outs are not moved); margin?: expr (with clip whole, the least clearance from a cell to every edge of the field and its keep-outs, measured exactly; default 0, a cell may touch an edge); direction?: positive|negative|symmetric (default positive); sketch?: id|name (default: active or last sketch; its closed profiles hold the field: a loop inside another is a keep-out); profiles?: as solid.extrude; targets?: [body]; mode?: cut (the only mode so far); name?. Cuts at most 250 cells in one operation; not for sheet metal (use sheet.perforate). The faces cut have no stable names yet
solid.cell_grid.description:
Fill the closed profiles of a sketch with cells of one shape and cut them out of the bodies:
vents, speaker grilles, weight-saving pockets. A profile's outer loop is the field to fill;
a loop inside it is a keep-out that no cell crosses. The cells are cut in one operation, a few
hundred at most (the command help names the limit); a sheet metal body is refused (use
`sheet.perforate`). The faces cut have no stable names yet.

fields.name: anchor
fields.description: A point: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}, each a number in mm or a length expression.

fields.name: angle
fields.description: The grid's rotation about the anchor. Default: 0.

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: clip
fields.description: What happens to cells the field's edge crosses. Default: snap.

fields.name: depth
fields.description: How deep the cells are cut along the sketch normal. Required unless `through_all`.

fields.name: direction
fields.description: Which way to cut. Default: positive (along the sketch normal).

fields.name: dot_grid
fields.description: How the centres of `circle` and `polygon` cells are laid out. Default: hexagonal.

fields.name: keepout_clip
fields.description:
What happens to cells a keep-out's edge crosses (a loop inside the field). Default: the
same as `clip`, so one mode serves every loop.

fields.name: margin
fields.description:
The least clearance from a cell to every edge of the field and its keep-outs, with
`clip: whole`. Default 0: a cell may touch an edge.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: What to do with the cells. Default: cut.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

fields.name: profiles
fields.description: Which sketch profiles to use: "all" (the default, any case), an index, or a list of indices, of {"point": [x, y]} inside a profile, or of curve selections (a list of curve ids, {"curves": [ids]} or {"loops": [...]}). Picks by index or point are stored by the curves around the profile.

fields.name: shape
fields.description: The cells' shape. Default: hexagon.

fields.name: sides
fields.description: Sides of a `polygon` cell: a whole number from 3 to 64. Default: 8.

fields.name: size
fields.description: A length: a number in the design's length unit, or an expression such as "w / 2" or "30 mm".

fields.name: sketch
fields.description: A feature's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: snap_inset
fields.description:
With `clip: snap`, how many lattice lines further in each straight field edge moves after
it snaps: a whole number, default 0. The edge cells become whole cells and the rim a
whole number of grid rows thicker. Keep-outs are not moved.

fields.name: targets
fields.description: The bodies to cut. Default: the bodies of the active component (or `participants`).

fields.name: through_all
fields.description: Cut through every body in the way, instead of `depth`.

fields.name: web
fields.description: A length: a number in the design's length unit, or an expression such as "w / 2" or "30 mm".

solid.chamfer.label: Chamfer
solid.chamfer.help: edges: [[x,y,z] | {body, index}] ; distance: expr; tangent_chain?: bool (default true: each picked edge's tangent chain is cut with it; false: exactly the picked edges); distance2?: expr (along the second face) | angle?: expr (from the first face); flip?: bool (which face is first: by default the one facing up most); body?: the body the edges are on (without it, each point is looked up on every placed body, shown or hidden, and a point on edges of 2 bodies is refused, naming them)
solid.chamfer.description:
Bevel edges of a body with a flat face: `distance` back from each edge along both faces, or
along the first face with `distance2` along the second, or with the bevel at `angle` from the
first. Giving both `distance2` and `angle` is the handler's to refuse.

fields.name: angle
fields.description: The bevel's angle from the first face. Not with `distance2`.

fields.name: body
fields.description: The body whose edges the points pick. Default: whichever body has an edge there.

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: distance
fields.description: A length: a number in the design's length unit, or an expression such as "w / 2" or "30 mm".

fields.name: distance2
fields.description: How far the bevel cuts back along the second face. Not with `angle`.

fields.name: edges
fields.description: The edges, 1 to 1000.

fields.name: flip
fields.description:
Which face is first: by default the one facing up most; true takes the other. Default:
false.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

fields.name: tangent_chain
fields.description:
Cut each picked edge's tangent chain with it. Default: true; false cuts exactly the picked
edges.

solid.coil.label: Coil
solid.coil.help: diameter; two of revolutions (or turns), height, pitch; section_size; section?: circular|square; section_position?: inside|center|outside; base?: [x,y,z] (numbers in mm or length expressions; default: the origin); axis?: X|Y|Z|[x,y,z] (default Z); start_angle?; clockwise?: bool; sketch? (a sketch; its plane is the section plane, so its placement sets the radius and start phase), profiles? (default: all; one closed profile without holes); operation?, targets?, name?, body_name?
solid.coil.description:
Add a coil: a section swept along a helix. Give two of `revolutions` (or `turns`), `height` and
`pitch`. The section is either made from `diameter` and `section_size`, or taken from `sketch`.
One undo step.

fields.name: axis
fields.description: An axis: X, Y or Z (any case), or a direction [x, y, z] that isn't zero.

fields.name: base
fields.description: A point: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}, each a number in mm or a length expression.

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: clockwise
fields.description: A left-handed coil, turning the other way while still climbing along `axis`. Default: false.

fields.name: diameter
fields.description: The helix's diameter, greater than zero. Required without `sketch`; refused with it.

fields.name: height
fields.description:
The height of the helix along `axis`. Not used when `revolutions` (or `turns`) and `pitch`
are both given.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: operation
fields.description: How the coil combines with existing bodies. Default: new.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

fields.name: pitch
fields.description: The distance along `axis` between one turn and the next.

fields.name: profiles
fields.description: Which sketch profiles to use: "all" (the default, any case), an index, or a list of indices, of {"point": [x, y]} inside a profile, or of curve selections (a list of curve ids, {"curves": [ids]} or {"loops": [...]}). Picks by index or point are stored by the curves around the profile.

fields.name: revolutions
fields.description: The number of turns, greater than zero; it may be fractional.

fields.name: section
fields.description: Refused with `sketch`.

fields.name: section_position
fields.description: Refused with `sketch`.

fields.name: section_size
fields.description:
The section's diameter when circular, or its side when square, greater than zero. The
section must stay clear of the coil's axis. Required without `sketch`; refused with it.

fields.name: sketch
fields.description:
A sketch whose profile is the section. Its plane is the section plane, so its placement
sets the radius and the start phase.

fields.name: start_angle
fields.description: Where around the axis the section starts. Default: 0. Refused with `sketch`.

fields.name: targets
fields.description:
The bodies a join, cut or intersect works on. Default: every body in the active component.
Ignored when `participants` lists bodies.

fields.name: turns
fields.description: The number of turns, when `revolutions` is not given.

solid.combine.label: Combine
solid.combine.help: target: body; tools: [body]; operation?: join|cut|intersect; touching?: separate|one_body (what a join makes of pieces that share no face: separate, the default, makes each piece that touches another only along an edge or at a point a body of its own and keeps pieces that touch nothing in one body; one_body keeps every piece in one body); keep_tools?: bool; new_component?: bool (the result goes into a new component; component_name?)
solid.combine.description:
Combine bodies: join the tool bodies to the target, cut them from it, or keep only the space
the target shares with them. Whether each body exists stays the handler's to check.

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: component_name
fields.description:
With `new_component`: the new component's name. Default: the target's name and
" Combined".

fields.name: keep_tools
fields.description: Keep the tool bodies as they are. Default: false (the combine uses them up).

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: new_component
fields.description: Move the result into a new component, made for it. Default: false.

fields.name: operation
fields.description: What the tools do to the target. Default: join.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

fields.name: target
fields.description: The body the tools combine with, by name.

fields.name: tools
fields.description: The bodies combined with the target, by name: a name, or a list of one or more names (at most 10000).

fields.name: touching
fields.description: What a join makes of pieces that share no face. Default: separate.

solid.cone.label: Cone
solid.cone.help: radius | diameter, height: expr (the base circle, and the top's distance along the axis; a negative height goes the other way); top_radius? | top_diameter?: expr (the top circle; default 0: a full cone ending in an apex); base?: [x,y,z] (centre of the base circle: numbers in mm or length expressions; default: the origin); axis?: X|Y|Z|[x,y,z] (default Z); operation?, touching?, targets?: [body], name?, body_name?
solid.cone.description:
Add a cone or truncated cone: the base circle and, `height` along `axis`, the top circle (a
point when its radius is 1e-6 mm or less). Its radii, height and base are within 1e7 mm.

fields.name: axis
fields.description: An axis: X, Y or Z (any case), or a direction [x, y, z] that isn't zero.

fields.name: base
fields.description: A point: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}, each a number in mm or a length expression.

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: diameter
fields.description: The base circle's diameter, instead of `radius`.

fields.name: height
fields.description: A length: a number in the design's length unit, or an expression such as "w / 2" or "30 mm".

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: operation
fields.description: How the cone combines with existing bodies. Default: new.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

fields.name: radius
fields.description:
The base circle's radius, above 1e-6 mm. Give it or `diameter`; when both are given,
`radius` is used.

fields.name: targets
fields.description:
The bodies a join, cut or intersect works on. Default: every body in the active
component (an intersect removes those the cone doesn't meet).
Ignored when `participants` lists bodies.

fields.name: top_diameter
fields.description: The top circle's diameter, instead of `top_radius`.

fields.name: top_radius
fields.description:
The top circle's radius, 0 or more; up to 1e-6 mm makes a full cone ending in a point.
When both are given, `top_radius` is used. Default: 0.

solid.cylinder.label: Cylinder
solid.cylinder.help: radius | diameter, height: expr; base?: [x,y,z] (centre of the bottom: numbers in mm or length expressions; default: the origin); axis?: X|Y|Z|[x,y,z] (default Z); references?: [{edge: [x,y,z] on a straight edge of the face it stands on, distance: expr}] (at most two, as solid.hole's: the base centre goes that far from each edge's line, in the face's plane, and follows the edges; with a numeric base only); operation?, touching?, targets?: [body], name?, body_name?

fields.name: axis

fields.name: base

fields.name: diameter
