solid.extrude.label: Extrude
solid.extrude.help: distance: expr (or through_all: true); taper?: angle expr (positive: outward, so the far end is larger along the extrusion direction; negative: inward, so the far end is smaller); corner?: preserve_curvature|tangent|round (how a taper closes a sharp corner its offset opens: each wall continues as itself, a line's plane or an arc's cone, until it meets its neighbour; each continues straight along its end tangent; or an arc about the corner. Without it, each profile preserves curvature where every curve is a line or an arc and takes tangent where another curve has a corner, and the feature's warning says so; a corner rule given is kept, and refused where the kernel cannot build it); sketch?: id|name (default: active or last sketch); profiles?: all | [index] | [{curves: [ids]}] (the profile whose outer loop is made of exactly these curves, or pieces of them; found again on every recompute, so it follows parameter changes; islands inside are its holes; an error when no profile or several match) | [{point:[x,y]}] (index and point picks are stored by their curves when that finds the same profile; a pick on a drawn profile that reference geometry, such as the projected outline of the face the sketch is on, cuts into regions takes the whole drawn profile); exact_regions?: bool (each index or point pick is exactly the region it names, as the dialogs send); default: every drawn profile, except that a loop inside another is its hole and a loop inside that hole is material again; face?: [x,y,z] (extrude a planar body face instead of a sketch profile); faces?: [[x,y,z],…] (coplanar faces of one body); face_body?: name (whose face, where faces of several bodies meet at the point); fixed?: true (with face or faces: start on the face's plane as a fixed plane, which won't follow later changes to the face; for a face whose history can't keep an attachment, such as a converted mesh's); direction?: positive|negative|symmetric (distance is total thickness, split evenly around the start plane); convention?: total_distance|legacy_per_side (how a symmetric distance is read; default total_distance, split evenly around the start plane; legacy_per_side: the distance on each side, as older symmetric extrudes keep); distance2?: expr (Two Sides: a second distance on the side direction leaves free, the first side may be through_all or to; with direction: negative the first side goes against the normal and distance2 along it; a negative distance only turns its own side over); start_offset?: expr (along the sketch normal, also with direction: negative); to?: [x,y,z] (To Object: a face, vertex or point; to_offset?: expr past it); from?: [x,y,z] (From Object: start at that face or point); operation?: new|join|cut|intersect|auto (cut into a body, otherwise join existing solids; new in an empty component); touching?: separate|one_body (what a join makes of pieces that share no face: separate, the default, makes each piece that touches another only along an edge or at a point a body of its own and keeps pieces that touch nothing in one body; one_body keeps every piece in one body); targets?: [body] (Join from a face, or from a sketch on a body's face, defaults to that face's body; explicit targets or participants override); name?; body_name?; thin?: true (Thin: a wall along sketch curves instead of the profiles) with curves?: [curve ids] (open chains and closed loops, joined where they meet end to end; default: every drawn curve of the sketch), thickness: expr, side?: center|inside|outside|two_sides (a closed loop's inside is the area it encloses, an open chain's the side it bends toward, a straight line's the left of its first curve as drawn; default center), thickness2?: expr (two_sides: the thickness outside); corners are mitred, crossing walls are one
solid.extrude.description: Extrude sketch profiles (or a planar body face) into a solid.

fields.name: body
fields.description:
With `face`, among placed instances: the body whose placement `face` is read in (read by
the engine's frame mapping, before the command runs). Default: `face_body`, else the
body nearest the point.

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: convention
fields.description: total_distance (the default): a symmetric distance is the total thickness. legacy_per_side keeps older designs' per-side meaning.

fields.name: curves
fields.description: With `thin`: the curves the wall follows. Default: every drawn curve of the sketch.

fields.name: direction
fields.description: Which way to extrude. Default: positive.

fields.name: distance
fields.description:
How far: the length one way; with `direction: symmetric`, the total thickness (per side
with `convention: legacy_per_side`); with `distance2`, the first side's length. Required
unless `through_all` or `to` is given.

fields.name: distance2
fields.description:
Two Sides: a second distance on the side `direction` leaves free; the first side may be
`through_all` or `to`. With `direction: negative` the first side goes against the normal
and `distance2` along it. A negative distance only turns its own side over.

fields.name: exact_regions
fields.description:
Each index or point pick is exactly the region it names. Without it, a pick on a drawn
profile that reference geometry (a face's projected outline) cuts into regions takes the
whole drawn profile. The dialogs send `true`: they highlight the regions they pick.

fields.name: extent
fields.description: `"through_all"`, the same as `through_all: true`.

fields.name: face
fields.description: A point on a planar body face to extrude instead of a sketch profile.

fields.name: face_body
fields.description: The body whose face to use, where faces of several bodies meet at `face` (or `faces`).

fields.name: faces
fields.description: Points in mm, one on each of the coplanar faces of one body to extrude together.

fields.name: fixed
fields.description:
With `face` or `faces`: start on the face's plane as a fixed plane, which won't follow later
changes to the face (for a face whose history can't keep an attachment, such as a converted
mesh's).

fields.name: from
fields.description: A point in mm: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: operation
fields.description: How the extrusion combines with existing bodies. Default: new.

fields.name: participants
fields.description: The bodies taking part; overrides the default scope.

fields.name: profiles
fields.description: Which sketch profiles to use: "all" (the default, any case), an index, or a list of indices, of {"point": [x, y]} inside a profile, or of curve selections (a list of curve ids, {"curves": [ids]} or {"loops": [...]}). Picks by index or point are stored by the curves around the profile.

fields.name: side
fields.description: With `thin`: which side of the curves the wall lies on. Default: center.

fields.name: sketch
fields.description: A feature's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: start_offset
fields.description: Start this far from the sketch plane, along its normal.

fields.name: taper
fields.description:
Draft angle of the side walls (positive: outward, so the far end is larger along the
extrusion direction; negative: inward, so the far end is smaller).

fields.name: targets
fields.description:
The bodies a join, cut or intersect works on. Default for a join from a body's face:
that body.

fields.name: thickness
fields.description: With `thin`: the wall's thickness.

fields.name: thickness2
fields.description: With `thin` and `side: two_sides`: the thickness outside.

fields.name: thin
fields.description: A thin wall along sketch curves instead of solid profiles.

fields.name: through_all
fields.description: Extrude through everything in the way.

fields.name: to
fields.description: A point in mm: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}.

fields.name: to_offset
fields.description: How far past `to` to go.

fields.name: touching
fields.description: What a join makes of pieces that share no face. Default: separate.

solid.fillet.label: Fillet
solid.fillet.help: edges: [[x,y,z] point on edge | {body, index}] ; radius: expr; tangent_chain?: bool (default true: each picked edge's tangent chain is rounded with it; false: exactly the picked edges); body?: the body the edges are on (without it, each point is looked up on every placed body, shown or hidden, and a point on edges of 2 bodies is refused, naming them); type?: constant|curvature (alias g2: curvature-continuous quintic between planar faces along straight edges, one planar end face at each end (including sloped ends); radius sets the equivalent circular setback, not constant curvature; exact fit only)|chord (radius is the width across)|variable (radius at the end nearest start, radius2 at the other; one end may be 0, where the round closes to the corner)|spline (the radius along the edge is a clamped B-spline from the end nearest start: radius is its first control radius, radii the rest, knots its knot vector from 0 to 1; one end may be 0); radius2?; start?: [x,y,z]; radii?: [expr, …]; knots?: [number, …]; mid?: [[position 0…1 from start, radius expr], …] (variable radii between the ends); smooth?: bool (smooth instead of straight between the radii); corner?: rolling|g2 (rolling, the default: the corners where three blended edges meet are pieces of the rolling ball's sphere, tangent to each blend; a curvature round's corners are always g2 patches, between its own sections; g2: each corner where three or more rounded edges meet, and every edge there is rounded, is set back (1.5 × the radius along each edge unless `setbacks` names it) and filled with a patch meeting the rounds and the faces round it to the second order (curvature-continuous seams, clear of the points where a round's section ends on a face), constant-radius exact fillets only, refused where it cannot be built); setbacks?: [{vertex: [x,y,z], distance: expr}, …] (corner setbacks: the corner at the vertex nearest `vertex`, where every edge meeting it is rounded, starts its patch `distance` along each of those edges from the vertex, past where the rounds would meet (past the radius at a square corner), so the rounds blend through a larger patch; one distance for all of a corner's edges; constant-radius exact fillets only; with `corner: g2`, the G2 patch's corners); turn?: mitre|swept (where two rounds turn round a sharp, straight, convex side edge square to both on a plane, such as the rounds along a boss's base at its upright edges: mitre, the default, runs them on to meet in a mitre; swept ends them at the side edge and fills the corner with their section revolved about it, a torus; swept takes type: constant, corner: rolling, no setbacks and fit: exact or reduce, and is refused with the reason where the rounds are unequal or the side edge is concave, curved or tangent); fit?: exact|reduce|taper (exact, the default: a radius too large for the geometry around the edges is refused, naming the largest that fits; reduce: where it doesn't fit it is reduced to the largest that does, one radius for edges sharing a face; the smallest used is returned as `radius_applied`, each edge's as `radii_applied: [{edge: [x,y,z], radius}]`, and noted in the feature's warning; taper: along each straight edge between planar faces where it doesn't fit, the radius follows the room there as a smooth spline, down to 0 where a face closes to a point, noted in the feature's warning)
solid.fillet.description:
Round edges of a body: a constant radius by default, or a chord, a curvature-continuous
section or a radius varying along each edge (`type`).

fields.name: body
fields.description:
The body whose edges the points pick. Default: each point is looked up on every placed
body, shown or hidden, and a point on edges of 2 bodies is refused, naming them.

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: edges
fields.description: The edges, 1 to 1000.

fields.name: knots
fields.description:
`type: spline`: the knot vector from 0 to 1, as many knots as all control radii, the
degree (1 to 3) and one more.

fields.name: mid
fields.description:
`type: variable`: radii between the ends, each `[position, radius]`, the position between 0
and 1 from the start end. At most 100 are read.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

fields.name: radii
fields.description: `type: spline`: the control radii after `radius`. At most 100 are read.

fields.name: radius
fields.description: A length: a number in the design's length unit, or an expression such as "w / 2" or "30 mm".

fields.name: radius2
fields.description:
`type: variable`: the radius at the end away from `start`; it or `radius` may be 0, where
the round closes to the corner.

fields.name: setbacks
fields.description:
Corner setbacks: the corner at the vertex nearest each `vertex`, where every edge meeting it
is rounded, starts its patch `distance` along each of those edges from the vertex, past
where the rounds would meet. Constant-radius exact fillets only.

fields.name: smooth
fields.description: `type: variable`: smooth instead of straight between the radii. Default: false.

fields.name: start
fields.description: `type: variable` or `spline`: a point near the end the radius starts from.

fields.name: tangent_chain
fields.description:
Round each picked edge's tangent chain with it. Default: true; false rounds exactly the
picked edges.

those the pipe doesn't meet), or for a cut or intersect where it has none, every body.

fields.name: wall
fields.description:
The wall thickness, for a hollow tube: above 0 and less than half `diameter`. Default:
solid.

solid.press_pull.label: Press Pull
solid.press_pull.help: face: [x,y,z] and distance: expr (positive adds material, negative cuts), or edges: [[x,y,z]…] and distance (a fillet); body?: the body the face or edges are on (for edges, as for solid.fillet)
solid.press_pull.description:
Press Pull a face or round edges. A flat face moves along its normal: a positive distance joins
material outward, a negative one cuts inward. A curved face offsets. A fillet's or chamfer's
face changes that feature's size by the distance. Edges are rounded with the distance as the
radius. `edges` is read before `face`. One undo step.

fields.name: body
fields.description: The body the face or edges are on. Default: found from the points.

fields.name: distance
fields.description: How far the face moves, positive outward; the radius for `edges`.

fields.name: edges
fields.description: The edges to round: a point on each, or `{body, index}`.

fields.name: face
fields.description: A point on the face to move.

solid.remove.label: Remove
solid.remove.help: bodies: [names] (removed from here on in the timeline)
solid.remove.description: Remove bodies from the design, from this point in the timeline on. One undo step.

fields.name: bodies
fields.description: The bodies, by name: one, or a list of 1 to 10 000.

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

solid.replace_face.label: Replace Face
solid.replace_face.help: faces: [[x,y,z] points on planar faces, or face names from model.faces]; target: plane (XY|XZ|YZ|construction plane|{origin, normal}) | target_face: [x,y,z] on a parallel planar face; body?
solid.replace_face.description:
Move planar faces onto a plane, or onto the plane of a parallel planar face. `target_face` is
read before `target`. One undo step.

fields.name: body
fields.description: The body the faces are on. Default: found from the faces.

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

fields.name: target
fields.description: The plane to move the faces onto.

fields.name: target_face
fields.description: A point on a planar face, whose plane the faces move onto.

solid.revolve.label: Revolve
solid.revolve.help: axis: sketch line id | x | y (sketch axes) | X|Y|Z (world) | {type: world, axis: X|Y|Z} (as returned by timeline.inspect) | {sketch, curve} (a line of another sketch, followed in that sketch) | construction axis name (followed when edited) | {origin, dir} (origin: numbers or length expressions, followed when parameters change) | {edge|face: [x,y,z]} (a straight or circular edge, or a cylinder, cone or torus face: about its axis, followed as the model changes); angle?: expr (default 360 deg); angle2?: expr (Two Sides: the other side's angle); direction?: symmetric (angle split either side, independent of axis direction); convention?: sketch_normal|legacy_axis_start (default sketch_normal; legacy retains older angular starts); to?: [x,y,z] (To Object: turn until that face, vertex or point); sketch?, profiles? | face: [x,y,z] (a planar body face as the profile) and face_body?: name (whose face, where faces of several bodies meet) and fixed?: true (the face's plane as a fixed plane, as solid.extrude's), operation?, touching?, targets?, name?, body_name?
solid.revolve.description: Revolve sketch profiles (or a planar body face) about an axis into a solid.

fields.name: angle
fields.description:
How far to turn: more than 0 and at most 360 degrees. With `angle2`, the angle on the
first side, the two adding up to the turn; with `direction: symmetric`, the whole turn,
split either side. Default: 360 deg. Not used when `to` is given, though it must still
evaluate.

fields.name: angle2
fields.description:
Two Sides: the angle on the other side, turned back from the profile. Not used when `to`
is given; used instead of `direction: symmetric` when both are given.

fields.name: axis
fields.description: The axis to turn about: a sketch line's id or name (a line of the profile's sketch wins over a construction axis of the same name); {"sketch"?: an id or name, "curve": an id} — a line of that sketch, which the revolve follows when that sketch is edited; x or y, the sketch's own axes; X, Y or Z, the world axes (any other case is a name); a construction axis's name, which the revolve follows when it is edited; {"type": "world", "axis": X, Y or Z}, as timeline.inspect gives one back; {"origin"?: [x, y, z] (numbers or length expressions; default: the world origin), "dir": [x, y, z]}, which the revolve follows when parameters change; or an edge or face of a body ({"edge": [x, y, z]} or {"face": [x, y, z]}, a point on a straight or circular edge, or on a cylinder, cone or torus face, or as saved: {"type": "edge" or "face", "at", "name"?}), about whose axis it turns, followed as the model changes.

fields.name: body
fields.description:
With `face`, among placed instances: the body whose placement `face` is read in (read by
the engine's frame mapping, before the command runs). Default: `face_body`, else the
body nearest the point.

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: convention
fields.description: sketch_normal (the default): the angle is measured from the sketch plane, turning about the axis as the sketch's normal sweeps. legacy_axis_start keeps the angular start older designs had.

fields.name: direction
fields.description:
`symmetric` splits the angle evenly either side of the profile, whichever way the axis
points. The handler ignores every other value.

fields.name: exact_regions
fields.description:
Each index or point pick is exactly the region it names. Without it, a pick on a drawn
profile that reference geometry (a face's projected outline) cuts into regions takes the
whole drawn profile. The dialogs send `true`: they highlight the regions they pick.

fields.name: face
fields.description: A point on a planar body face to revolve instead of a sketch profile.

fields.name: face_body
fields.description: The body whose face to use, where faces of several bodies meet at `face`.

fields.name: fixed
fields.description: With `face`: the face's plane as a fixed plane, as `solid.extrude`'s.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: operation
fields.description: How the revolve combines with existing bodies. Default: new.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

fields.name: profiles
fields.description: Which sketch profiles to use: "all" (the default, any case), an index, or a list of indices, of {"point": [x, y]} inside a profile, or of curve selections (a list of curve ids, {"curves": [ids]} or {"loops": [...]}). Picks by index or point are stored by the curves around the profile.

fields.name: sketch
fields.description: A feature's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: symmetric
fields.description: When true, the same as `direction: symmetric`.

fields.name: targets
fields.description:
The bodies a join, cut or intersect works on. Default for a join from a body's face, or
from a sketch on one: that body. Explicit `targets` or `participants` replace it.

fields.name: to
fields.description: A point in mm: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}.

fields.name: touching
fields.description: What a join makes of pieces that share no face. Default: separate.

solid.rib.label: Rib
solid.rib.help: sketch, curves: [open curve ids, in order]; thickness (across the sketch plane, or across the curves when normal); depth? (default: to the next face); flip?: bool (fill to the other side); direction?: in_plane|normal (grow across the sketch plane, the default, or along its normal)
solid.rib.description:
Add a rib or a web, thin walls from open sketch curves grown until they meet the part. A rib
(`solid.rib`) is one wall along a chain of curves, in order; a web (`solid.web`) is one wall
along each curve. It joins the part. One undo step.

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: curves
fields.description: The sketch's open curves, by id: 1 to 1000.

fields.name: depth
fields.description: How far the wall grows. Default: until it meets the part.

fields.name: flip
fields.description: True: the wall grows to the other side of the curves. Default: false.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

fields.name: sketch
fields.description: A feature's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: thickness
fields.description: A length: a number in the design's length unit, or an expression such as "w / 2" or "30 mm".

fields.name: touching
fields.description: What the join makes of pieces that share no face. Default: separate.

solid.scale.label: Scale
solid.scale.help: bodies: [names]; factor: expr | factors: [x, y, z] exprs; origin?: [x,y,z]

fields.name: bodies
fields.description: A name, or a list of names.

fields.name: factor
fields.description: The same factor in every direction, above 1e-9 and below 1e6. Give it or `factors`.

fields.name: factors
fields.description:
Different factors along X, Y and Z, each above 1e-9 and below 1e6. When given, these set
the scale; a `factor` given too has no effect but must still evaluate.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: origin
fields.description: The point that stays where it is, in mm. Default: the origin.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, which every feature records; each an existing body or `*`. A
scale changes only `bodies`, whatever this lists.

solid.shell.label: Shell
solid.shell.help: faces: [[x,y,z] points on the faces to remove, or face names from model.faces; none: a closed hollow body]; thickness: expr; direction?: inside|outside|both; tangent_chain?: bool (also open faces joined smoothly to the picked ones); body? (needed with no faces when there are several bodies)

fields.description: faces: [[x,y,z] points on the faces to remove, or face names from model.faces; none: a closed hollow body]; thickness: expr; direction?: inside|outside|both; tangent_chain?: bool (also open faces joined smoothly to the picked ones); body? (needed with no faces when there are several bodies)

solid.sphere.label: Sphere
solid.sphere.help: radius | diameter: expr; center?: [x,y,z] (numbers in mm or length expressions; default: the origin); operation?, touching?, targets?: [body], name?, body_name?

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: center
fields.description: A point: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}, each a number in mm or a length expression.

fields.name: diameter
fields.description: The diameter, instead of `radius`.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: operation
fields.description: How the sphere combines with existing bodies. Default: new.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

fields.name: radius
fields.description: The radius. Give it or `diameter`; when both are given, `radius` is used.

fields.name: targets
fields.description:
The bodies a join, cut or intersect works on. Default: every body in the active
component (an intersect removes those the sphere doesn't meet).
Ignored when `participants` lists bodies.

solid.split_body.label: Split Body
solid.split_body.help: body: name; plane: XY|XZ|YZ|plane name|{origin, normal} — or tool: {body, point} (a face of a body, its surface extended) — or sketch: id, line: curve id (a straight sketch line, along the sketch's normal)
solid.split_body.description:
Cut a body into pieces along a plane, a face of another body (its surface extended), or a
straight sketch line (along the sketch's normal). Each piece becomes a body.

fields.name: body
fields.description: The body to split, by name.

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: line
fields.description:
With `sketch`: a straight line's id; the body is split by the plane through it along the
sketch's normal, which follows the line when the sketch changes.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

fields.name: plane
fields.description:
The plane to split across. Read when none of `tool`, `sketch` and `line` is given; then it
is required.

fields.name: sketch
fields.description: With `line`: the sketch, by feature id (not its name), whose line splits the body.

fields.name: tool
fields.description:
A face of a body to split along, its surface extended. Read when neither `sketch` nor
`line` is given.

solid.split_face.label: Split Face
solid.split_face.help: faces: [[x,y,z] points on the faces to split, or face names from model.faces]; body?; and the splitting tool: plane: XY|XZ|YZ|plane name|{origin, normal} — or tool: {body, point} (a face of a body, its surface extended) — or sketch: id or name (its curves, along the sketch's normal; each curve on its own, an open one extended past its ends) and loops?: bool (default false: true joins the curves end to end first, so a closed loop cuts along itself only)
solid.split_face.description:
Divide faces of a body along a plane, a face of another body (its surface extended), or a
sketch's curves (along the sketch's normal), without cutting the body: each face becomes
several, and the body keeps its shape.

fields.name: body
fields.description:
The body the faces are on, by name: where faces of several bodies meet at a point, whose
face it is. Default: the body each point or name finds.

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: faces
fields.description: The faces, 1 to 1000.

fields.name: loops
fields.description:
With `sketch`: true joins its curves end to end first, so a closed loop of lines and arcs
splits the faces along the loop only. Default: false, each curve on its own, an open one
extended past its ends.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

fields.name: plane
fields.description:
The plane to split along. Read when neither `tool` nor `sketch` is given; then it is
required.

fields.name: sketch
fields.description:
A sketch, by id or name, whose curves split the faces along its normal. Read when no
`tool` is given.

fields.name: tool
fields.description: A face of a body to split along, its surface extended.

solid.sweep.label: Sweep
solid.sweep.help: sketch: profile sketch; profiles?; path_sketch: sketch; path: [curve ids in order]; path_body?: body name; path_edges?: [points on its edges] (the path is a chain of that body's edges, instead of a sketch's curves); orientation?: perpendicular (default: square to the path, turning with it) | parallel (as drawn: the profile moves without turning; the path must keep crossing its plane) | [x,y,z] (square to the path, its turn about the path fixed by this direction); twist?: angle expr (the profile turns this much about the path over its length; within 4 turns); scale?: expr (the profile's scale at the end, linear along the path; 0.01…100); rails?: [{sketch?: sketch (default path_sketch), curves: [curve ids in order]}] (guide rails, one or two, each meeting every plane square to the path once along it, from the end nearest the path's start: one rail turns the profile so its point where the rail starts stays on the rail and scales it with the rail's distance from the path; two rails carry it between them, its points where they start staying on both; rails take the default orientation, no twist and no scale, and a path without sharp corners); rail_fit?: scale (default: the profile grows and shrinks evenly) | stretch (only across to the rail, between the rails); operation?, touching?, targets?, name?, body_name?
solid.sweep.description: Sweep sketch profiles along a path of sketch curves into a solid.

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: exact_regions
fields.description:
Each index or point pick is exactly the region it names. Without it, a pick on a drawn
profile that reference geometry (a face's projected outline) cuts into regions takes the
whole drawn profile. The dialogs send `true`: they highlight the regions they pick.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: operation
fields.description: How the sweep combines with existing bodies. Default: new.

fields.name: orientation
fields.description: How the profile turns as it follows the path. Default: perpendicular.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

fields.name: path
fields.description: A name, or a list of names.

fields.name: path_body
fields.description: The name of the body whose edges are the path, instead of a sketch's curves.

fields.name: path_edges
fields.description: The points on the body's edges that are the path, one on each edge of the chain: 1 to 1000.

fields.name: path_sketch
fields.description: A sketch's feature id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: profiles
fields.description: Which sketch profiles to use: "all" (the default, any case), an index, or a list of indices, of {"point": [x, y]} inside a profile, or of curve selections (a list of curve ids, {"curves": [ids]} or {"loops": [...]}). Picks by index or point are stored by the curves around the profile.

fields.name: rail_fit
fields.description: How the rails reshape the profile. Default: scale. Used only with `rails`.

fields.name: rails
fields.description:
Guide rails, each meeting every plane square to the path once along it, followed from the
end nearest the path's start. One rail turns the profile so that its point where the rail
starts stays on the rail, and scales it with the rail's distance from the path; two rails
carry it between them, its points where they start staying on both. The path must have no
sharp corners.

fields.name: scale
fields.description:
The profile's scale at the end of the path, changing linearly along it from 1 at the
start: 0.01 to 100. Default: 1.

fields.name: sketch
fields.description: A feature's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: targets
fields.description:
The bodies a join, cut or intersect works on; given, they win over `participants`.
Default: `participants`, else for a join from a sketch on a body's face that body, else
every body in the active component (an intersect removes those the sweep doesn't meet),
or for a cut or intersect where it has none, every body.

fields.name: touching
fields.description: What a join makes of pieces that share no face. Default: separate.

fields.name: twist
fields.description:
How far the profile turns about the path over its length, from none at the start: within
four turns (1440 deg) either way. Default: none.

solid.thread.label: Thread
solid.thread.help: face: [x,y,z] on a cylindrical face OR faces: [{body, point:[x,y,z]}, ...] (1 to 1024 selected faces of the same component in one Thread feature; every plural face requires its body identity; exact world body names or unambiguous definition names; do not combine with face); single_face_selection?: bool (default false; true requires exactly one entry in faces and keeps single-face replacement when editing); shared options apply to every face, automatic size fits each independently; cosmetic replies include threads for faces and retain thread as the first; form?: metric|trapezoidal|acme|buttress|buttress_asme|bspp|rp|bspt|npt (default: the one `designation` names, else metric; square is refused: no current standard defines it); designation?: the size, as its standard writes it: metric "M8", "M8x1", "M16xPh3P1.5" (ISO 68-1, ISO 261, ISO 965-1); trapezoidal "Tr20x4", "Tr40x14(P7)" (ISO 2904, ISO 2903); buttress "S20x4", "S40x14(P7)" (DIN 513, 3°/30°); acme "1/2-10 ACME" (ASME B1.5); buttress_asme "2.5-8 BUTT" (ASME B1.9, 7°/45°, basic profile; no size table); bspp "G 1/2" (ISO 228-1, 55° parallel); rp "Rp 1/2" (ISO 7-1's parallel internal thread, 55°, an R screws into it; internal only); bspt "R 1/2" external, "Rc 1/2" internal (ISO 7-1, 55°, taper 1 in 16); npt "1/2-14 NPT" (ASME B1.20.1, 60°, taper 1 in 16) — a taper thread starts at a free end (the pipe end or the hole mouth) with its standard diameter there, and an external one runs its standard length unless `length` or `up_to` says otherwise (default: the standard size that fits the face, a shaft its major diameter, a hole its nominal diameter (a 12 mm hole is M12) or else the size whose tap drill it is); hand?: right|left|both (default right; both: a right- and a left-handed groove crossing); old_auto_size?: bool (an automatic size keeps the rule of designs saved before a hole was sized by its nominal diameter: a 12 mm hole is M14; set on those threads, keeps them as they were when edited); steep_flank?: start|end (buttress only, default end: the steep flank of the screw's teeth faces the thread's end, the way its axis points); starts?: 1..8 (lead = starts x pitch: that many grooves, each a turn's starts-th further round; a designation that gives the lead gives the starts); ease_out?: expr|standard|short (modelled threads: the inner end, away from where the thread starts, fades out over this length (shorter than a turn too), its section moving out of the material as it turns; standard 2.5 P, short 1.25 P per ISO 3508; it lies past the full-form length, up to a shoulder's clearance; at a free end, inside the face; without it the groove stops square there, ending in its own profile; the start never fades: it runs off its free end, plain or chamfered (`tip`)); tip?: none|start|both (modelled external threads: start chamfers the end the thread starts from, which must be free, both each free end the thread reaches, ISO 4753's chamfered end, the last teeth tapering into the cone; chamfer_angle?: angle expr to the axis, default 45 deg; chamfer_depth?: expr, radial from the major diameter, default for a metric thread down to the external minor diameter d3 = d - 1.226869 P (ISO 724), the largest ISO 4753 allows; other forms give it); extent?: full|length|up_to (default: length when `length` is given, up_to when `up_to` is, else full: the whole face); length?: expr (from the end the thread starts at); up_to?: [x,y,z] (a point, such as on a shoulder face: the thread runs to its place along the axis) | plane name or {origin, normal} (to where the plane crosses the axis); from?: [x,y,z] near the end of the face the thread starts at (default: the face's only free end, the one with no material past it; else the end the `face` point lies within a third of the face of; a pick in the middle of a face whose ends are alike is refused); modeled?: bool (default false); continuous_flanks?: bool (default true; false keeps the historical half-turn faces and groove-before-chamfer construction). Cosmetic: the model is unchanged, model.threads lists it. Modeled: cuts the thread profile into the body: past a free end the groove runs out a pitch into the air (or through a chamfer); at a shoulder, a head or a blind hole's bottom it stops with its section clear of it, never cutting into it; a hole as wide as the thread or wider is narrowed to the thread's minor diameter first, and the reply's warning says so, unless its wall is open along the thread (a cross hole, a cut through the side, a slanted end), which is refused with the drill to use; a shaft thicker than the thread is refused with the size to make it, never turned down

from?: [x,y,z] near the end of the face the thread starts at (default: the face's only free end, the one with no material past it; else the end the `face` point lies within a third of the face of; a pick in the middle of a face whose ends are alike is refused); modeled?: bool (default false); continuous_flanks?: bool (default true; false keeps the historical half-turn faces and groove-before-chamfer construction). Cosmetic: the model is unchanged, model.threads lists it. Modeled: cuts the thread profile into the body: past a free end the groove runs out a pitch into the air (or through a chamfer); at a shoulder, a head or a blind hole's bottom it stops with its section clear of it, never cutting into it; a hole as wide as the thread or wider is narrowed to the thread's minor diameter first, and the reply's warning says so, unless its wall is open along the thread (a cross hole, a cut through the side, a slanted end), which is refused with the drill to use; a shaft thicker than the thread is refused with the size to make it, never turned down

surface.stitch.help: bodies: [names] (surfaces sewn into the first; a solid when they close); tolerance?: expr (default: tight)
surface.stitch.description:
Sew surface bodies into the first one along the edges they share; a solid when they close. One
undo step.

fields.name: bodies
fields.description: The surface bodies, by name: one, or a list of 1 to 10 000.

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

fields.name: tolerance
fields.description: How far apart two edges may be and still be sewn together. Default: 0, edges that meet.

surface.sweep.label: Surface Sweep
surface.sweep.help: sketch?: id|name; curves?: [curve ids] and/or profiles? (as surface.extrude); path_sketch: sketch; path: [curve ids in order] (a path with corners, or 3D curves, gives ruled walls mitred at the corners); path_body?: body name; path_edges?: [points on its edges] (the path is a chain of that body's edges, instead of a sketch's curves); orientation?, twist?, scale?, rails?, rail_fit? (as solid.sweep); name?, body_name? (a surface body, no caps)
surface.sweep.description:
Sweep sketch curves or profile boundaries along a path of sketch curves into a surface body:
walls only, no caps. A path with corners, or of 3D curves, gives ruled walls mitred at the
corners. `participants` changes nothing here.

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: curves
fields.description: Curve ids to sweep, at most 1000: open or closed chains of curves meeting end to end.

fields.name: exact_regions
fields.description:
Each index or point pick is exactly the region it names. Without it, a pick on a drawn
profile that reference geometry (a face's projected outline) cuts into regions takes the
whole drawn profile. The dialogs send `true`: they highlight the regions they pick.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: orientation
fields.description: How the profile turns as it follows the path. Default: perpendicular.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

fields.name: path
fields.description: A name, or a list of names.

fields.name: path_body
fields.description: The name of the body whose edges are the path, instead of a sketch's curves.

fields.name: path_edges
fields.description: The points on the body's edges that are the path, one on each edge of the chain: 1 to 1000.

fields.name: path_sketch
fields.description: A sketch's feature id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: profiles
fields.description: Which sketch profiles to use: "all" (the default, any case), an index, or a list of indices, of {"point": [x, y]} inside a profile, or of curve selections (a list of curve ids, {"curves": [ids]} or {"loops": [...]}). Picks by index or point are stored by the curves around the profile.

fields.name: rail_fit
fields.description: How the rails reshape the profile. Default: scale. Used only with `rails`.

fields.name: rails
fields.description:
Guide rails, each meeting every plane square to the path once along it, followed from the
end nearest the path's start. One rail turns the profile so that its point where the rail
starts stays on the rail, and scales it with the rail's distance from the path; two rails
carry it between them, its points where they start staying on both. The path must have no
sharp corners.

fields.name: scale
fields.description:
The profile's scale at the end of the path, changing linearly along it from 1 at the
start: 0.01 to 100. Default: 1.

fields.name: sketch
fields.description: A feature's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: twist
fields.description:
How far the profile turns about the path over its length, from none at the start: within
four turns (1440 deg) either way. Default: none.

surface.thicken.label: Thicken
surface.thicken.help: bodies: [surface names]; thickness: expr (negative: against the normal); symmetric?: bool; operation?: new|join|cut|intersect; targets?
surface.thicken.description:
Give surface bodies a thickness, making solids, and combine them with other bodies. One undo
step.

fields.name: bodies
fields.description: The surface bodies, by name: one, or a list of 1 to 10 000.

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: operation
fields.description: How the thickened bodies combine with existing ones. Default: new.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

fields.name: symmetric
fields.description: True: half the thickness each side of the surface. Default: false.

fields.name: targets
fields.description:
The bodies a join, cut or intersect works on, by name. Default: every body in the active
component.

fields.name: thickness
fields.description: A length: a number in the design's length unit, or an expression such as "w / 2" or "30 mm".

fields.name: touching
fields.description: What a join makes of pieces that share no face. Default: separate.

surface.trim.label: Trim
surface.trim.help: body: surface name; plane: XY|XZ|YZ|plane name|{origin, normal} or tool: {body, point} (a face, its surface extended) or curves: {sketch, curves?: [curve ids] (chains of curves meeting end to end; default every curve), direction?: normal|[x,y,z] (swept onto the surface along the sketch's normal, the default, or this direction)}; keep: [x,y,z] (a point on the side to keep) or [[x,y,z], ...] (points on the regions to keep: the pieces that hang together once cut). Mutual trim: with: another surface (one face each; leave out plane, tool and curves), keep_with: [x,y,z] or [[x,y,z], ...] (what to keep of it); each is cut where the other's surface (extended) meets it; extend?: bool (a surface that stops short of the other is extended to meet it); stitch?: bool (the kept pieces sewn into `body`; `with` is then gone)
surface.trim.description:
Cut a surface body with a plane, a face or sketch curves and keep the side or regions asked
for, or trim two surfaces against each other. One undo step.

fields.name: body
fields.description: The surface body, by name.

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: curves
fields.description: Sketch curves to cut with.

fields.name: extend
fields.description: Mutual trim: a surface that stops short of the other is extended to meet it.

fields.name: keep
fields.description: A point on the side to keep, or points on the regions to keep: the pieces that hang together once cut.

fields.name: keep_with
fields.description: A point on the side to keep, or points on the regions to keep: the pieces that hang together once cut.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

fields.name: plane
fields.description: The plane to cut with.

fields.name: stitch
fields.description: Mutual trim: the kept pieces are sewn into `body`, and `with` is then gone.

fields.name: tool
fields.description: A face to cut with, its surface extended.

fields.name: with
fields.description: Mutual trim: another surface body, one face each; each is cut where the other's surface (extended) meets it. Leave out `plane`, `tool` and `curves`.

surface.unstitch.label: Unstitch
surface.unstitch.help: body; faces?: [[x,y,z]] (points on the faces to take out, each its own surface body; the rest stay together under the body's name; default: every face its own surface body). A solid comes apart into surfaces
surface.unstitch.description:
Take faces out of a body, each a surface body of its own; the rest stay together under the
body's name. A solid comes apart into surfaces. One undo step.

fields.name: body
fields.description: The body, by name.

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: faces
fields.description: Points on the faces to take out. Default: every face, each its own surface body.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

surface.untrim.label: Untrim
surface.untrim.help: face: {body, point}; holes?: all|[[x,y,z]] (points on the inner loops to remove; default: all); outer?: bool (restore the outer boundary to the surface's natural bounds: a free-form surface's own, an analytic surface's span of the face); in_place?: bool (untrim a surface body's face where it is; a solid's face is always copied out). A surface body; the face keeps its name
surface.untrim.description:
Remove a face's holes, or restore its outer boundary, as a surface body; the face keeps its
name. A solid's face is copied out. One undo step.

fields.name: body_name
fields.description: The new body's name.

fields.name: body_names
fields.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

fields.name: face
fields.description: The face to untrim: `body`, by name, and `point`, a point on the face.

fields.name: in_place
fields.description:
True: untrim a surface body's face where it is, not as a copy. A solid's face is always
copied out. Default: false.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

fields.name: outer
fields.description:
True: restore the outer boundary to the surface's natural bounds (a free-form surface's
own, an analytic surface's span of the face). Default: false.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

timeline.add.label: Add Recorded Feature
timeline.add.help: feature: a feature as the design file and timeline.inspect hold it ({type, name?, id?, …}; the name is kept even when another feature has it, the id is kept and refused when another feature has it, so later steps can refer to them); params?: [{name, expression, unit?, comment?}] (the model parameters its sketch dimensions use); the feature goes at the marker → feature, name, error, warning
timeline.add.description:
Append one recorded feature to the timeline, as the design file holds it, so every feature
kind replays exactly: the same ids, names, parameter names and stored edge and face names (the
steps `timeline.export_script` writes). It goes at the timeline marker. One undo step.

fields.name: feature
fields.description: A feature as the design file and timeline.inspect hold it: {type, name?, id?, …}. The name is kept even when another feature has it; the id is kept, and refused when another feature has it. Whether the rest is a feature is the command's to check.

fields.name: params
fields.description: Model parameters the feature's sketch dimensions use.

timeline.compute_all.label: Compute All
timeline.compute_all.description:
`timeline.compute_all` takes no parameters: it throws away every cached result and computes
the whole timeline again.

timeline.copy.label: Copy Features
timeline.copy.help: features: [ids or names] (in timeline order on paste)
timeline.copy.description:
Copy features to the session's clipboard, and a snapshot of them for pasting into another
design. The features stay where they are; the clipboard replaces what was copied before. Not an
undo step.

fields.name: features
fields.description: Features by name or id: one name, or a list of names and ids in any mix.

timeline.delete.label: Delete
timeline.delete.help: feature: id|name | features: [id|name] | groups: [timeline folder ids] (a folder goes with all its features, joints and nested folders; one undo step; a sketch takes its dependent features with it) → deleted: [feature ids]; joints?: [joint ids]; groups?: [folder ids deleted]; failing?: [{feature, error}] (later features that worked and now fail)
timeline.delete.description:
Delete features, and the timeline folders given with their features, joints and nested
folders, as one undo step. A sketch takes the features built on
it with it, and a feature that owns a component takes the component's contents; later
features that fail without a deleted one stay and are named in `failing`. Give at least one of
`feature`, `features` and `groups`.

fields.name: feature
fields.description: A feature by id (a whole number) or by name.

fields.name: features
fields.description: Features, by name or id: one name, or a list. `null` is read as absent.

fields.name: groups
fields.description: Timeline folder ids.

timeline.delete.reason: not in the live demo: it needs Mechvane's own handling on the server (install Mechvane to use it)

timeline.dependents.label: Feature Dependents
timeline.dependents.help: feature: id|name → features deleted with it, and features that would fail without it
timeline.dependents.description:
What would go with a feature if it were deleted, and which later features would fail
without it. Nothing is changed.

fields.name: feature
fields.description: A feature by id (a whole number) or by name.

timeline.edit.label: Edit Feature
timeline.edit.help: feature: id|name, set: {fields to change, merged into the feature's definition as timeline.inspect returns it, e.g. {"extent": {"distance": "30"}} (extrude), {"angle": "90 deg"} (revolve); a dotted key names a nested field ({"plane.distance": "8 mm"} = {"plane": {"distance": "8 mm"}}); expressions are text, or a number in mm or degrees} → recomputed: features rebuilt, restored: features whose earlier result for the same inputs was reused
timeline.edit.description:
Change a feature's fields: `set` is merged into the feature's definition as
`timeline.inspect` returns it, and the design is rebuilt. The feature's type can't change. When the edited feature fails to build, the call returns
that build error.

fields.name: feature
fields.description: A feature by id (a whole number) or by name.

fields.name: set
fields.description: The fields to change, merged into the feature's definition as `timeline.inspect` returns it, e.g. {"extent": {"distance": "30"}} for an extrude or {"angle": "90 deg"} for a revolve. A dotted key names a nested field ({"plane.distance": "8 mm"} is {"plane": {"distance": "8 mm"}}). Expressions are text, or a number in mm or degrees. A field the definition doesn't have is refused.

timeline.edit.reason: not in the live demo: it needs Mechvane's own handling on the server (install Mechvane to use it)

timeline.export_script.label: Export Command Script
timeline.export_script.help: path?: write the script to this file → script: {commands: [...]} that rebuilds the design (solidcraft-cli eval/run), steps, omitted: what the script leaves out (appearances, folders, views, configurations, print-face assignments); components and assemblies are not supported yet
timeline.export_script.description:
Write the design's history as a command script that rebuilds it (`solidcraft-cli eval` and
`run` replay it): one step per setting and feature, and a list of what the script leaves out.
A design with components or joints is refused for now. The design is not changed.

fields.name: path
fields.description: A file to write the script to, as JSON. Default: none, the script is only returned.

timeline.export_script.reason: not in the live demo: it needs Mechvane's own handling on the server (install Mechvane to use it)

timeline.group.label: New Feature Folder
timeline.group.help: name?; features?: [id|name]; joints?: [id|name]; groups?: [folder ids]; parent?: folder id (features and joints leave any other timeline folder)
timeline.group.description:
Make a new timeline folder holding features, joints and other folders, inside another folder
or at the top level. The features and joints leave any other folder they were in. Each folder
must hold one unbroken run of features, so the features given must be next to each other in
the history. One undo step.

fields.name: features
fields.description: Features, each by id or name.

fields.name: groups
fields.description: Timeline folder ids.

fields.name: joints
fields.description: Joints, each by id or name.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The folder's name. Default: `Folder` and the number of folders there will be.

fields.name: parent
fields.description: The folder to put the new one in, by id. Default: the top level. `null` is read as absent.

timeline.inspect.label: Inspect Feature
timeline.inspect.help: group: folder id → group, name, parent, features, joints; or feature: id|name → type, definition (the fields timeline.edit's set changes, with their current values), inputs: [{label, param, expression, unit}] (named inputs parameters.change can also set), error, warning
timeline.inspect.description:
Describe a timeline folder (`group`), or a feature (`feature`): its definition, the fields
`timeline.edit` changes with their values, and its named inputs. Nothing is changed.

fields.name: feature
fields.description: A feature by id (a whole number) or by name.

fields.name: group
fields.description: A timeline folder, by id.

timeline.move_many.label: Move Timeline Items
timeline.move_many.help: features?: [id|name], groups?: [folder ids], group?: folder id, position: insertion slot, active?: bool (true = the moved contents end up before the history marker, false = behind it; other features keep their state); atomically changes folder membership and moves all selected contents as one block
timeline.move_many.description:
Move features and folders (with everything in them) to a place in the timeline and into a
folder, together, as one block and one undo step. The block keeps the order its features had.
Give at least one of `features` and `groups`. Refused when a feature that worked would fail.

fields.name: active
fields.description:
True: the moved features end up before the history marker. False: behind it. Other
features keep their state. Default: the marker stays where it is. `null` is read as
absent.

fields.name: features
fields.description: Features, each by id or name.

fields.name: group
fields.description: The folder to move them into, by id. Default: the top level, also when `null`.

fields.name: groups
fields.description: Timeline folder ids.

fields.name: position
fields.description:
Where the block goes: the insertion slot among the timeline's features, counted before
the block is taken out. A number below 0 is 0, a fraction is cut to a whole number, and a
number past the end is the end.

timeline.move_to_group.label: Move Features to Folder
timeline.move_to_group.help: features?: [id|name], joints?: [id|name], groups?: [ids], group?: id (omit or null to move to the timeline root)
timeline.move_to_group.description:
Move features, joints and folders into a timeline folder, or to the top level. They leave the
folders they were in, and each folder must still hold one unbroken run of features. Give at
least one of `features`, `joints` and `groups`. One undo step.

fields.name: features
fields.description: Features, each by id or name.

fields.name: group
fields.description: The folder to move them into, by id. Default: the top level, also when `null`.

fields.name: groups
fields.description: Timeline folder ids.

fields.name: joints
fields.description: Joints, each by id or name.

timeline.paste.label: Paste Features
timeline.paste.help: translate?: [x,y,z] (moves the copies' geometry); component?: where the copies go (default: the active one), component_path?: its placement (default: the active one, else its only one); the copies go at the marker, each where its original is in the world (copies into their own component keep its coordinates); body transfers are left out; from_design?: true to paste sketch features from the host's cross-design clipboard snapshot
timeline.paste.description:
Paste the copied features as independent copies at the timeline marker: sketches get their own
dimension parameters, features their own names, and references inside the copied set point at
the copies. Body transfers are left out. One undo step. With `from_design`, only sketch
features are pasted, from the snapshot another design's copy left. Every key reads the same
either way.

fields.name: component
fields.description: A component's id (a number) or its name.

fields.name: component_path
fields.description: The occurrence ids from the top of the design down to a placement.

fields.name: from_design
fields.description:
True pastes the sketch features of the clipboard snapshot of another design, with their
parameters. Default: false, the features copied in this design.

fields.name: translate
fields.description: A distance in mm, as [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}.

timeline.play.label: Play History
timeline.play.help: action?: toggle|play|stop (default toggle) → action: validated display request; the connected UI plays from the marker to the end with a half-second pause per rebuilt step. Headless callers only validate the request; no dialog, document edit or animation clock is created

fields.name: action
fields.description: Display-only timeline playback requests. The connected UI owns the animation clock.

timeline.redefine.label: Edit Feature
timeline.redefine.help: feature: id|name, command: the feature's command id, params: its parameters (the feature is rebuilt in place) → feature, recomputed, restored, rolled_back: bool (the feature is after the history marker, so the edit is not built yet; `note` then says so), warning?
timeline.redefine.description:
Rebuild a feature in place from its command and parameters, keeping its place in the
timeline, its name and its folder. The feature's type can't change. Only the commands that
make features are taken. When the edited feature fails to build, the call returns that error
and the design is left as it was.

fields.name: command
fields.description: The id of the command that makes the feature (`solid.extrude`, `solid.fillet`, …). Only the commands that make features are taken.

fields.name: feature
fields.description: A feature by id (a whole number) or by name.

fields.name: params
fields.description: That command's parameters. Default: none.

timeline.rename.label: Rename
timeline.rename.help: feature: id|name, name (references to it follow)
timeline.rename.description:
Rename a feature; references to it (a sketch used by an extrude, a body name in a later
feature) follow. A construction plane's name may not be an origin plane's.

fields.name: feature
fields.description: A feature by id (a whole number) or by name.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Text with something in it besides whitespace, at most 128 bytes long once the whitespace around it is trimmed (the bytes of its UTF-8, so fewer characters when some are not ASCII).

timeline.rename.reason: not in the live demo: it needs Mechvane's own handling on the server (install Mechvane to use it)

timeline.rename_group.label: Rename Feature Folder
timeline.rename_group.help: group: id, name (renames the folder holding features and joints)
timeline.rename_group.description: Rename a timeline folder (the one that holds features and joints).

fields.name: group
fields.description: A timeline folder, by id.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Text with something in it besides whitespace, at most 128 bytes long once the whitespace around it is trimmed (the bytes of its UTF-8, so fewer characters when some are not ASCII).

timeline.reorder.label: Reorder Feature
timeline.reorder.help: feature: id|name, position: its new index, active?: bool (true = it ends up before the history marker, false = behind it; other features keep their state); refused when a feature that worked would fail, unless allow_errors?: bool (default false): then made, and broken: [{feature, error}] lists the features it broke → feature, position: its index now, from: its index before, moved: bool, note?: why nothing moved, or that a position past the end meant the last slot
timeline.reorder.description:
Move one feature to another place in the timeline. Refused when a feature that worked would
fail, unless `allow_errors` is true. A feature in a timeline folder must stay next to the
others of its folder.

fields.name: active
fields.description:
True: the feature ends up before the history marker. False: behind it. Other features keep
their state. Default: the marker stays where it is. `null` is read as absent.

fields.name: allow_errors
fields.description:
True: make the move even when it breaks features that worked; they are listed in `broken`.
Default: false, the move is refused. `null` is read as absent. Anything but true, false
or `null` is refused, except when `allow_errors` is not read: when the feature is already
at `position` (and `active` is not given) nothing is moved, and a move that would break a
timeline folder is refused first.

fields.name: feature
fields.description: A feature by id (a whole number) or by name.

fields.name: position
fields.description:
Its new index in the timeline, from 0. A number below 0 is 0, a fraction is cut to a whole
number, and a number past the end is the last slot (the reply's `note` says so).

timeline.reorder_many.label: Reorder Features
timeline.reorder_many.help: features: [id|name], position: insertion slot in the current history; selected features keep their relative order; active?: bool (as timeline.reorder's); refused when a feature that worked would fail, unless allow_errors?: bool (default false): then made, and broken: [{feature, error}] lists the features it broke
timeline.reorder_many.description:
Move several features together to one place in the timeline, as one block that keeps the
order the features have there. Refused when a feature that worked would fail, unless
`allow_errors` is true.

fields.name: active
fields.description:
True: the moved features end up before the history marker. False: behind it. Other
features keep their state. Default: the marker stays where it is. `null` is read as
absent.

fields.name: allow_errors
fields.description:
True: make the move even when it breaks features that worked; they are listed in `broken`.
Default: false, the move is refused. `null` is read as absent.

fields.name: features
fields.description: Features, each by id or name.

fields.name: position
fields.description:
Where the block goes: the insertion slot among the timeline's features, counted before the
block is taken out. A number below 0 is 0, a fraction is cut to a whole number, and a
number past the end is the end.

timeline.roll_to.label: Roll History Marker
timeline.roll_to.help: position: number of features to keep active, or "end" (omit = end) | feature: id|name (the marker goes right after it)
timeline.roll_to.description: Move the history marker right after a feature, or to a number of features from the start, or to the end: the features after it are not built, and the selection is cleared. `timeline.rollback` does the same.

fields.name: feature
fields.description: A feature by id (a whole number) or by name.

fields.name: position
fields.description:
How many features stay active, or "end". Default: end, also when `null`. Ignored when
`feature` is given.

timeline.roll_to.reason: the workspace shows no rolled-back part yet (Mechvane's part_end rolls it only for the agent)

timeline.rollback.label: Move Timeline Marker
timeline.rollback.help: position: number of features to keep active, or "end" (omit = end)
timeline.rollback.description: Move the history marker: the features after it are not built, as if rolled back, and the selection is cleared. Give `position`, the number of features to keep active (or "end"), or `feature` to put the marker right after one. `timeline.roll_to` does the same.

fields.name: feature
fields.description: A feature by id (a whole number) or by name.

fields.name: position
fields.description:
How many features stay active, or "end". Default: end, also when `null`. Ignored when
`feature` is given.

timeline.rollback.reason: the workspace shows no rolled-back part yet (Mechvane's part_end rolls it only for the agent)

timeline.suppress.label: Suppress Feature
timeline.suppress.help: feature: id|name | features: [id|name] | groups: [timeline folder ids] (every feature and joint in those folders and their nested folders; one undo step), suppressed?: bool (default toggles: features and joints are all suppressed unless all of them already are, then all are unsuppressed) → feature: id (or features: [ids]; groups: [ids] and joints: [ids] when groups are given), suppressed
timeline.suppress.description:
Suppress features (and the joints of the folders given), or bring them back, as one undo
step. A suppressed feature is skipped when the design is built. Give at least one of
`feature`, `features` and `groups`.

fields.name: feature
fields.description: One feature, by id or name. `null` is read as absent.

fields.name: features
fields.description: Features, by id or name: one, or a list. `null` is read as absent.

fields.name: groups
fields.description: Timeline folder ids.

fields.name: suppressed
fields.description:
